title: Reverence begins where measurement fails
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 273
summary: This shabad dismantles the habit of auditing holiness from the outside. The Brahm Giani cannot be priced, fully described, or reduced to a public rank, because a life saturated with God carries a depth only God-consciousness can truly know.
whyItMatters: When the mind turns spiritual life into comparison, suspicion, or status-mapping, this shabad refuses the whole game. It teaches reverence without possession: bow to depth, stop trying to control it, and let humility become the more truthful intelligence.
takeaway: Stop measuring what the Guru teaches you to revere.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੀ ਕੀਮਤਿ ਨਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kee keemat naeh ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being cannot be appraised.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਸਗਲ ਮਨ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai sagal man maeh ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being has all within his mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਕਉਨ ਜਾਨੈ ਭੇਦੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa kaun jaanai bhedh ||
lines.translation: Who can know the mystery of the God-conscious being?

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਉ ਸਦਾ ਅਦੇਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kau sadhaa adhes ||
lines.translation: Forever bow to the God-conscious being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਕਥਿਆ ਨ ਜਾਇ ਅਧਾਖੵਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa kathiaa na jai adhaakhayer ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being cannot be described in words.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸਰਬ ਕਾ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sarab kaa Thaakur ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is the Lord and Master of all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੀ ਮਿਤਿ ਕਉਨੁ ਬਖਾਨੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kee mit kaun bakhaanai ||
lines.translation: Who can describe the limits of the God-conscious being?

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੀ ਗਤਿ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kee gat braham giaanee jaanai ||
lines.translation: Only the God-conscious being can know the state of the God-conscious being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਪਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa a(n)t na paar ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being has no end or limitation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਉ ਸਦਾ ਨਮਸਕਾਰੁ ॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee kau sadhaa namasakaar ||7||
lines.translation: O Nanak, to the God-conscious being, bow forever in reverence. ||7||

structure: The shabad begins by denying the marketplace any power to appraise the God-conscious being.
It deepens the refusal: mystery, description, limit, and rank all fail before a consciousness joined to the Lord.
It leaves the listener not with analysis but with reverent bowing, the only honest posture before such depth.

evidence.coreClaim: The Brahm Giani cannot be priced, described, bounded, or spiritually audited; the shabad turns evaluation into reverence.
evidence.turn: After denying appraisal, the shabad keeps removing every smaller measuring tool until only bowing remains credible.
evidence.practicalImplication: Do not use comparison to manage holiness. Let the presence of real depth make you humbler, less possessive, and more willing to learn.

title: Do not spend a passing life on a dirty tongue
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 154
summary: This shabad speaks to the body as if waking it from a dangerous dream. Comfort, gossip, lust, hoarding, theft, and display all look powerful for a moment, but only truthful deeds and the sweetness of Naam remain when the soul has to leave.
whyItMatters: It is easy to waste a rare day on slander, appetite, and the small intoxication of being right about other people. This shabad brings death close enough to clean the mouth, loosen the fist, and ask what will still matter when the performance collapses.
takeaway: Let mortality make your speech cleaner and your deeds worth carrying.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਚੇਤੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee chetee mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree Chaytee, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਕਾਇਆ ਰਹੈ ਸੁਖਾਲੀ ਬਾਜੀ ਇਹੁ ਸੰਸਾਰੋ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)mirat kaiaa rahai sukhaalee baajee ih sa(n)saaro ||
lines.translation: With your nectar-like body, you live in comfort, but this world is just a passing drama.

lines.gurmukhi: ਲਬੁ ਲੋਭੁ ਮੁਚੁ ਕੂੜੁ ਕਮਾਵਹਿ ਬਹੁਤੁ ਉਠਾਵਹਿ ਭਾਰੋ ॥
lines.transliteration: lab lobh much kooR kamaaveh bahut uThaaveh bhaaro ||
lines.translation: You practice greed, avarice and great falsehood, and you carry such a heavy burden.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਕਾਇਆ ਮੈ ਰੁਲਦੀ ਦੇਖੀ ਜਿਉ ਧਰ ਉਪਰਿ ਛਾਰੋ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) kaiaa mai ruladhee dhekhee jiau dhar upar chhaaro ||1||
lines.translation: O body, I have seen you blowing away like dust on the earth. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਣਿ ਸੁਣਿ ਸਿਖ ਹਮਾਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: sun sun sikh hamaaree ||
lines.translation: Listen - listen to my advice!

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਕ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਕੀਤਾ ਰਹਸੀ ਮੇਰੇ ਜੀਅੜੇ ਬਹੁੜਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਵਾਰੀ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: sukirat keetaa rahasee mere jeeaRe bahuR na aavai vaaree ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Only the good deeds which you have done shall remain with you, O my soul. This opportunity shall not come again! ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉ ਤੁਧੁ ਆਖਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਕਾਇਆ ਤੂੰ ਸੁਣਿ ਸਿਖ ਹਮਾਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: hau tudh aakhaa meree kaiaa too(n) sun sikh hamaaree ||
lines.translation: I say to you, O my body: listen to my advice!

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿੰਦਾ ਚਿੰਦਾ ਕਰਹਿ ਪਰਾਈ ਝੂਠੀ ਲਾਇਤਬਾਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: ni(n)dhaa chi(n)dhaa kareh paraiee jhooThee laitabaaree ||
lines.translation: You slander, and then praise others; you indulge in lies and gossip.

lines.gurmukhi: ਵੇਲਿ ਪਰਾਈ ਜੋਹਹਿ ਜੀਅੜੇ ਕਰਹਿ ਚੋਰੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: vel paraiee joheh jeeaRe kareh choree buriaaree ||
lines.translation: You gaze upon the wives of others, O my soul; you steal and commit evil deeds.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੰਸੁ ਚਲਿਆ ਤੂੰ ਪਿਛੈ ਰਹੀਏਹਿ ਛੁਟੜਿ ਹੋਈਅਹਿ ਨਾਰੀ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: ha(n)s chaliaa too(n) pichhai rahe'eeh chhuTaR hoie'eeh naaree ||2||
lines.translation: But when the swan departs, you shall remain behind, like an abandoned woman. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਕਾਇਆ ਰਹੀਅਹਿ ਸੁਪਨੰਤਰਿ ਤੁਧੁ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) kaiaa rahe'eeh supana(n)tar tudh kiaa karam kamaiaa ||
lines.translation: O body, you are living in a dream! What good deeds have you done?

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਚੋਰੀ ਮੈ ਜਾ ਕਿਛੁ ਲੀਆ ਤਾ ਮਨਿ ਭਲਾ ਭਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar choree mai jaa kichh leeaa taa man bhalaa bhaiaa ||
lines.translation: When I stole something by deception, then my mind was pleased.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਲਤਿ ਨ ਸੋਭਾ ਪਲਤਿ ਨ ਢੋਈ ਅਹਿਲਾ ਜਨਮੁ ਗਵਾਇਆ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: halat na sobhaa palat na ddoiee ahilaa janam gavaiaa ||3||
lines.translation: I have no honor in this world, and I shall find no shelter in the world hereafter. My life has been lost, wasted in vain! ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉ ਖਰੀ ਦੁਹੇਲੀ ਹੋਈ ਬਾਬਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਮੇਰੀ ਬਾਤ ਨ ਪੁਛੈ ਕੋਈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: hau kharee dhuhelee hoiee baabaa naanak meree baat na puchhai koiee ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: I am totally miserable! O Baba Nanak, no one cares for me at all! ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾਜੀ ਤੁਰਕੀ ਸੁਇਨਾ ਰੁਪਾ ਕਪੜ ਕੇਰੇ ਭਾਰਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: taajee turakee suinaa rupaa kapaR kere bhaaraa ||
lines.translation: Turkish horses, gold, silver and loads of gorgeous clothes

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਸ ਹੀ ਨਾਲਿ ਨ ਚਲੇ ਨਾਨਕ ਝੜਿ ਝੜਿ ਪਏ ਗਵਾਰਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: kis hee naal na chale naanak jhaR jhaR pe gavaaraa ||
lines.translation: - none of these shall go with you, O Nanak. They are lost and left behind, you fool!

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੂਜਾ ਮੇਵਾ ਮੈ ਸਭ ਕਿਛੁ ਚਾਖਿਆ ਇਕੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਤੁਮਾਰਾ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: koojaa mevaa mai sabh kichh chaakhiaa ik a(n)mrit naam tumaaraa ||4||
lines.translation: I have tasted all the sugar candy and sweets, but Your Name alone is Ambrosial Nectar. ||4||

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੇ ਦੇ ਨੀਵ ਦਿਵਾਲ ਉਸਾਰੀ ਭਸਮੰਦਰ ਕੀ ਢੇਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhe dhe neev dhivaal usaaree bhasama(n)dhar kee dderee ||
lines.translation: Digging deep foundations, the walls are constructed, but in the end, the buildings return to heaps of dust.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਚੇ ਸੰਚਿ ਨ ਦੇਈ ਕਿਸ ਹੀ ਅੰਧੁ ਜਾਣੈ ਸਭ ਮੇਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)che sa(n)ch na dheiee kis hee a(n)dh jaanai sabh meree ||
lines.translation: People gather and hoard their possessions, and give nothing to anyone else - the poor fools think that everything is theirs.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋਇਨ ਲੰਕਾ ਸੋਇਨ ਮਾੜੀ ਸੰਪੈ ਕਿਸੈ ਨ ਕੇਰੀ ॥੫॥
lines.transliteration: soin la(n)kaa soin maaRee sa(n)pai kisai na keree ||5||
lines.translation: Riches do not remain with anyone - not even the golden palaces of Sri Lanka. ||5||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਣਿ ਮੂਰਖ ਮੰਨ ਅਜਾਣਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: sun moorakh ma(n)n ajaanaa ||
lines.translation: Listen, you foolish and ignorant mind

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੋਗੁ ਤਿਸੈ ਕਾ ਭਾਣਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: hog tisai kaa bhaanaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: - only His Will prevails. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਹੁ ਹਮਾਰਾ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਭਾਰਾ ਹਮ ਤਿਸ ਕੇ ਵਣਜਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: saahu hamaaraa Thaakur bhaaraa ham tis ke vanajaare ||
lines.translation: My Banker is the Great Lord and Master. I am only His petty merchant.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਉ ਪਿੰਡੁ ਸਭ ਰਾਸਿ ਤਿਸੈ ਕੀ ਮਾਰਿ ਆਪੇ ਜੀਵਾਲੇ ॥੬॥੧॥੧੩॥
lines.transliteration: jeeau pi(n)dd sabh raas tisai kee maar aape jeevaale ||6||1||13||
lines.translation: This soul and body all are His. He Himself kills, and brings back to life. ||6||1||13||

structure: The shabad opens by naming worldly comfort as a passing drama, not a secure home.
It exposes the weight of greed, falsehood, slander, lust, deception, and hoarding as burdens the soul cannot proudly carry beyond death.
It ends by placing all ownership under the Lord, where Naam is the only sweetness that does not get left behind.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad warns that gossip, falsehood, hoarding, and sensual display collapse at death, while truthful deeds and Naam remain meaningful.
evidence.turn: The address shifts from bodily comfort to moral inventory — what has the tongue done, what has the hand taken, what can the soul carry?
evidence.practicalImplication: Before speaking or grasping, remember that this chance will not return. Choose deeds and words that can stand when comfort, wealth, and image are gone.

title: Do not murder the soul by wasting a rare life
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: This shabad treats human birth as a rare trust, not a casual backdrop for entertainment. Without Naam, eating, laughing, showing off, and even staying alive become hollow; with the GurMantra planted inside, the heart finally holds what the life was given for.
whyItMatters: The shabad is severe because the opportunity is precious. It cuts through the lie that distraction is harmless and asks whether the day is feeding the soul or quietly helping it disappear.
takeaway: Use the rare human life for Naam before distraction spends it for you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੁਲਭ ਦੇਹ ਪਾਈ ਵਡਭਾਗੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhulabh dheh paiee vaddabhaagee ||
lines.translation: This human body is so difficult to obtain; it is only obtained by great good fortune.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਮੁ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਤੇ ਆਤਮ ਘਾਤੀ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naam na japeh te aatam ghaatee ||1||
lines.translation: Those who do not meditate on the Naam, the Name of the Lord, are murderers of the soul. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਰਿ ਨ ਜਾਹੀ ਜਿਨਾ ਬਿਸਰਤ ਰਾਮ ॥
lines.transliteration: mar na jaahee jinaa bisarat raam ||
lines.translation: Those who forget the Lord might just as well die.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਮ ਬਿਹੂਨ ਜੀਵਨ ਕਉਨ ਕਾਮ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: naam bihoon jeevan kaun kaam ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Without the Naam, of what use are their lives? ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਖਾਤ ਪੀਤ ਖੇਲਤ ਹਸਤ ਬਿਸਥਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: khaat peet khelat hasat bisathaar ||
lines.translation: Eating, drinking, playing, laughing and showing off

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਵਨ ਅਰਥ ਮਿਰਤਕ ਸੀਗਾਰ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: kavan arath mritak seegaar ||2||
lines.translation: - what use are the ostentatious displays of the dead? ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਨ ਸੁਨਹਿ ਜਸੁ ਪਰਮਾਨੰਦਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo na suneh jas paramaana(n)dhaa ||
lines.translation: Those who do not listen to the Praises of the Lord of supreme bliss,

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਸੁ ਪੰਖੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਗਦ ਜੋਨਿ ਤੇ ਮੰਦਾ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: pas pa(n)khee tiragadh jon te ma(n)dhaa ||3||
lines.translation: are worse off than beasts, birds or creeping creatures. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰਿ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੁ ਦ੍ਰਿੜਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak gur ma(n)tr dhiraRaiaa ||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, the GurMantra has been implanted within me;

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੇਵਲ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਿਦ ਮਾਹਿ ਸਮਾਇਆ ॥੪॥੪੨॥੧੧੧॥
lines.transliteration: keval naam ridh maeh samaiaa ||4||42||111||
lines.translation: the Name alone is contained within my heart. ||4||42||111||

structure: The shabad opens by calling the human body difficult to obtain and therefore impossible to treat casually.
It confronts the life without Naam as self-harm, stripping pleasure, display, and noise of their borrowed importance.
It comes to rest with GurMantra implanted within and the Name occupying the heart as the life’s true center.

evidence.coreClaim: A rare human life is spiritually wasted when Naam is absent; the shabad presses the listener toward GurMantra and inward remembrance.
evidence.turn: After naming human birth as rare, the shabad moves from warning to contrast: pleasure and display cannot replace the Name in the heart.
evidence.practicalImplication: Treat the day as entrusted, not disposable. Put remembrance before appetite, performance, and drift have spent the best strength of the life.

title: Belonging is not private property
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: This pauree breaks open the possessive mind. All are Yours, You belong to all, and everyone begs from the same inexhaustible Source. The ego has no independent ground to stand on; even the place from which it asks is given by the One it depends on.
whyItMatters: When belonging becomes a competition, people turn insecure, territorial, and cruel. This shabad restores scale: no one owns the Divine, no one is self-supplied, and the enlightened door is reached through shared dependence rather than private claim.
takeaway: Receive belonging from the One who holds everyone.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਉੜੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: pauRee ||
lines.translation: Pauree:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਤੇਰਾ ਤੂੰ ਸਭਸੁ ਦਾ ਤੂੰ ਸਭਨਾ ਰਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabh ko teraa too(n) sabhas dhaa too(n) sabhanaa raas ||
lines.translation: All are Yours, and You belong to all. You are the wealth of all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭਿ ਤੁਧੈ ਪਾਸਹੁ ਮੰਗਦੇ ਨਿਤ ਕਰਿ ਅਰਦਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabh tudhai paasahu ma(n)gadhe nit kar aradhaas ||
lines.translation: Everyone begs from You, and all offer prayers to You each day.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਤੂੰ ਦੇਹਿ ਤਿਸੁ ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਇਕਨਾ ਦੂਰਿ ਹੈ ਪਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: jis too(n) dheh tis sabh kichh milai ikanaa dhoor hai paas ||
lines.translation: Those, unto whom You give, receive everything. You are far away from some, and You are close to others.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੁਧੁ ਬਾਝਹੁ ਥਾਉ ਕੋ ਨਾਹੀ ਜਿਸੁ ਪਾਸਹੁ ਮੰਗੀਐ ਮਨਿ ਵੇਖਹੁ ਕੋ ਨਿਰਜਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: tudh baajhahu thaau ko naahee jis paasahu ma(n)geeaai man vekhahu ko nirajaas ||
lines.translation: Without You, there is not even a place to stand begging. See this yourself and verify it in your mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭਿ ਤੁਧੈ ਨੋ ਸਾਲਾਹਦੇ ਦਰਿ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਾ ਨੋ ਪਰਗਾਸਿ ॥੯॥
lines.transliteration: sabh tudhai no saalaahadhe dhar gurmukhaa no paragaas ||9||
lines.translation: All praise You, O Lord; at Your Door, the Gurmukhs are enlightened. ||9||

structure: The pauree begins by overturning ownership itself: the Lord belongs to all because all already belong to the Lord.
It gathers every prayer and every need back to the same Source, exposing dependence as universal rather than shameful.
It closes at the Lord’s Door, where the Gurmukh is enlightened by praise instead of defended by possession.

evidence.coreClaim: The pauree teaches universal dependence on the Lord — all belong to the One, all beg from the One, and no ego has ground apart from the One.
evidence.turn: The language moves from belonging to begging to praise, showing that dependence is not humiliation but the truth that opens the Door.
evidence.practicalImplication: Stop making love, status, or spiritual access into private property. Pray from the same ground as everyone else and let praise widen the heart.

title: The highest religion becomes visible in conduct
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 266
summary: This shabad refuses to let religion remain an identity, performance, or ritual résumé. The highest path is Naam joined to clean conduct, the finest ritual is the dirty mind washed in holy company, and the sweetest speech is praise that actually lives on the tongue.
whyItMatters: It confronts the gap between devotional language and daily behavior. If the mouth chants but the conduct stays polluted, the shabad will not flatter us; it sends speech, action, and the heart back to Naam until they become one life.
takeaway: Let Naam clean the conduct, the company, the tongue, and the heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰਬ ਧਰਮ ਮਹਿ ਸ੍ਰੇਸਟ ਧਰਮੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sarab dharam meh sresaT dharam ||
lines.translation: Of all religions, the best religion

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਕਰਮੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: har ko naam jap niramal karam ||
lines.translation: is to chant the Name of the Lord and maintain pure conduct.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਗਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਆ ਮਹਿ ਊਤਮ ਕਿਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: sagal kiraa meh uootam kiriaa ||
lines.translation: Of all religious rituals, the most sublime ritual

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਦੁਰਮਤਿ ਮਲੁ ਹਿਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: saadhasa(n)g dhuramat mal hiriaa ||
lines.translation: is to erase the filth of the dirty mind in the Company of the Holy.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਗਲ ਉਦਮ ਮਹਿ ਉਦਮੁ ਭਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: sagal udham meh udham bhalaa ||
lines.translation: Of all efforts, the best effort

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਹੁ ਜੀਅ ਸਦਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kaa naam japahu jeea sadhaa ||
lines.translation: is to chant the Name of the Lord in the heart, forever.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਗਲ ਬਾਨੀ ਮਹਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਬਾਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: sagal baanee meh a(n)mirat baanee ||
lines.translation: Of all speech, the most ambrosial speech

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਜਸੁ ਸੁਨਿ ਰਸਨ ਬਖਾਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: har ko jas sun rasan bakhaanee ||
lines.translation: is to hear the Lord's Praise and chant it with the tongue.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਗਲ ਥਾਨ ਤੇ ਓਹੁ ਊਤਮ ਥਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sagal thaan te oh uootam thaan ||
lines.translation: Of all places, the most sublime place,

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਿਹ ਘਟਿ ਵਸੈ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੮॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: naanak jeh ghaT vasai har naam ||8||3||
lines.translation: O Nanak, is that heart in which the Name of the Lord abides. ||8||3||

structure: The shabad ranks religion by lived purity: chanting the Name must become clean action.
It names holy company as the place where the dirty mind is washed more deeply than ritual display can reach.
It culminates in the heart where Naam abides, making praise not decoration but the soul’s dwelling place.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad defines the highest religion as Naam embodied through pure conduct, cleansed mind, truthful praise, and a heart where the Name abides.
evidence.turn: The teaching moves from religion to ritual to effort to speech to place, measuring every spiritual category by whether Naam has entered it.
evidence.practicalImplication: Do not let devotion stay verbal. Bring the tongue, habits, company, and private mind under the cleansing authority of Naam.

title: Worldly greatness carries anxiety inside it
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: This shabad punctures the impressive surface of worldly power. The people who look great are still afflicted by anxiety, the landlord still fights over land he must leave, and only loving attachment to the Lord gives greatness that is not already sick with loss.
whyItMatters: Status promises security but often produces a more defended fear. This shabad names that disease without envy or resentment, then offers a better measure: greatness is not what you control, but what frees you from being controlled by Maya.
takeaway: Measure greatness by devotion, not by what anxiety is guarding.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਵਡੇ ਵਡੇ ਜੋ ਦੀਸਹਿ ਲੋਗ ॥
lines.transliteration: vadde vadde jo dheeseh log ||
lines.translation: Those who seem to be great and powerful,

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਨ ਕਉ ਬਿਆਪੈ ਚਿੰਤਾ ਰੋਗ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: tin kau biaapai chi(n)taa rog ||1||
lines.translation: are afflicted by the disease of anxiety. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਉਨ ਵਡਾ ਮਾਇਆ ਵਡਿਆਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: kaun vaddaa maiaa vaddiaaiee ||
lines.translation: Who is great by the greatness of Maya?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਵਡਾ ਜਿਨਿ ਰਾਮ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: so vaddaa jin raam liv laiee ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: They alone are great, who are lovingly attached to the Lord. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੂਮੀਆ ਭੂਮਿ ਊਪਰਿ ਨਿਤ ਲੁਝੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhoomeeaa bhoom uoopar nit lujhai ||
lines.translation: The landlord fights over his land each day.

lines.gurmukhi: ਛੋਡਿ ਚਲੈ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨਾ ਨਹੀ ਬੁਝੈ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: chhodd chalai tirasanaa nahee bujhai ||2||
lines.translation: He shall have to leave it in the end, and yet his desire is still not satisfied. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਇਹੁ ਤਤੁ ਬੀਚਾਰਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak ih tat beechaaraa ||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, this is the essence of Truth:

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਭਜਨ ਨਾਹੀ ਛੁਟਕਾਰਾ ॥੩॥੪੪॥੧੧੩॥
lines.transliteration: bin har bhajan naahee chhuTakaaraa ||3||44||113||
lines.translation: without the Lord's meditation, there is no salvation. ||3||44||113||

structure: The shabad opens by looking straight at the visibly powerful and naming the anxiety hidden inside their stature.
It questions Maya’s definition of greatness, then exposes land and possession as things people fight over but cannot keep.
It ends with the essence: without meditation on the Lord, no amount of worldly weight becomes liberation.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad teaches that worldly greatness is diseased by anxiety and impermanence, while true greatness is loving attachment to the Lord.
evidence.turn: After exposing anxiety in the powerful, the shabad narrows the question to ownership and release: what can greatness mean if it cannot save?
evidence.practicalImplication: Notice what your ambition makes you defend. Let devotion, not possession, decide whether your life is becoming free.

title: Appetite grows into a life unless the Guru interrupts it
subtitle: Raag Maajh · Ang 137
summary: This shabad traces craving from infancy to death with unsentimental precision — milk, family, play, food, sexual desire, wealth, anger, decline, cremation. The pattern is not harmless just because it is familiar; without the Guru, the soul is left asking where to go as the world drowns.
whyItMatters: Craving often feels like personality because it has been rehearsed for so long. This shabad gives appetite a biography, showing how small loves harden into a whole direction unless the Guru teaches the soul another way to live.
takeaway: Name appetite early, before it names the whole life.

lines.transliteration: mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਿਆਰਿ ਲਗਾ ਥਣ ਦੁਧਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: pahilai piaar lagaa than dhudh ||
lines.translation: First, the baby loves mother's milk;

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੂਜੈ ਮਾਇ ਬਾਪ ਕੀ ਸੁਧਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhoojai mai baap kee sudh ||
lines.translation: second, he learns of his mother and father;

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੀਜੈ ਭਯਾ ਭਾਭੀ ਬੇਬ ॥
lines.transliteration: teejai bhayaa bhaabhee beb ||
lines.translation: third, his brothers, sisters-in-law and sisters;

lines.gurmukhi: ਚਉਥੈ ਪਿਆਰਿ ਉਪੰਨੀ ਖੇਡ ॥
lines.transliteration: chauthai piaar upa(n)nee khedd ||
lines.translation: fourth, the love of play awakens.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੰਜਵੈ ਖਾਣ ਪੀਅਣ ਕੀ ਧਾਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: pa(n)javai khaan peean kee dhaat ||
lines.translation: Fifth, he runs after food and drink;

lines.gurmukhi: ਛਿਵੈ ਕਾਮੁ ਨ ਪੁਛੈ ਜਾਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: chhivai kaam na puchhai jaat ||
lines.translation: sixth, in his sexual desire, he does not respect social customs.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਵੈ ਸੰਜਿ ਕੀਆ ਘਰ ਵਾਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: satavai sa(n)j keeaa ghar vaas ||
lines.translation: Seventh, he gathers wealth and dwells in his house;

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਠਵੈ ਕ੍ਰੋਧੁ ਹੋਆ ਤਨ ਨਾਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: aThavai karodh hoaa tan naas ||
lines.translation: eighth, he becomes angry, and his body is consumed.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਵੈ ਧਉਲੇ ਉਭੇ ਸਾਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: naavai dhaule ubhe saeh ||
lines.translation: Ninth, he turns grey, and his breathing becomes labored;

lines.gurmukhi: ਦਸਵੈ ਦਧਾ ਹੋਆ ਸੁਆਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhasavai dhadhaa hoaa suaaeh ||
lines.translation: tenth, he is cremated, and turns to ashes.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਏ ਸਿਗੀਤ ਪੁਕਾਰੀ ਧਾਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: ge sigeet pukaaree dhaeh ||
lines.translation: His companions send him off, crying out and lamenting.

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਡਿਆ ਹੰਸੁ ਦਸਾਏ ਰਾਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: auddiaa ha(n)s dhasaae raeh ||
lines.translation: The swan of the soul takes flight, and asks which way to go.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਇਆ ਗਇਆ ਮੁਇਆ ਨਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: aaiaa giaa muiaa naau ||
lines.translation: He came and he went, and now, even his name has died.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਿਛੈ ਪਤਲਿ ਸਦਿਹੁ ਕਾਵ ॥
lines.transliteration: pichhai patal sadhih kaav ||
lines.translation: After he left, food was offered on leaves, and the birds were called to come and eat.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਮਨਮੁਖਿ ਅੰਧੁ ਪਿਆਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak manmukh a(n)dh piaar ||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the self-willed manmukhs love the darkness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਾਝੁ ਗੁਰੂ ਡੁਬਾ ਸੰਸਾਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: baajh guroo ddubaa sa(n)saar ||2||
lines.translation: Without the Guru, the world is drowning. ||2||

structure: The shabad follows desire through the ordinary stages of life, refusing to romanticize how attachment grows.
It shows appetite maturing into possession, anger, bodily decline, death, and the soul’s disoriented departure.
It closes with the sharp diagnosis: without the Guru, the world’s familiar loves still leave it drowning.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad maps the lifelong growth of appetite and attachment, ending with the soul lost without the Guru.
evidence.turn: The sequence turns ordinary development into moral revelation — what begins as natural appetite can become a drowning life when no Guru interrupts it.
evidence.practicalImplication: Do not excuse a craving because it has a long history. Bring it under the Guru’s teaching while there is still time to redirect the life.

title: Take the scattered question to the Guru
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 34
summary: This shabad begins with honest confusion — whom shall I serve, what shall I chant? The answer is not more spiritual shopping, but accepting the True Guru’s will, uprooting selfishness, guarding the field of the mind, and letting Naam and Shabad make peace real.
whyItMatters: When the mind is anxious, it multiplies options until practice becomes another form of wandering. This shabad gives confusion a disciplined path: ask the Guru, stay awake, protect the crop, and let ego be pulled out by the root.
takeaway: Clarity comes when the restless search submits to the Guru’s Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa teejaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, Third Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਸੁ ਹਉ ਸੇਵੀ ਕਿਆ ਜਪੁ ਕਰੀ ਸਤਗੁਰ ਪੂਛਉ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: kis hau sevee kiaa jap karee satagur poochhau jai ||
lines.translation: Whom shall I serve? What shall I chant? I will go and ask the Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਭਾਣਾ ਮੰਨਿ ਲਈ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਆਪੁ ਗਵਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: satagur kaa bhaanaa ma(n)n liee vichahu aap gavai ||
lines.translation: I will accept the Will of the True Guru, and eradicate selfishness from within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਏਹਾ ਸੇਵਾ ਚਾਕਰੀ ਨਾਮੁ ਵਸੈ ਮਨਿ ਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ehaa sevaa chaakaree naam vasai man aai ||
lines.translation: By this work and service, the Naam shall come to dwell within my mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਮੈ ਹੀ ਤੇ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਈਐ ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਸੁਹਾਇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naamai hee te sukh paieeaai sachai sabadh suhai ||1||
lines.translation: Through the Naam, peace is obtained; I am adorned and embellished by the True Word of the Shabad. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਮੇਰੇ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਜਾਗੁ ਹਰਿ ਚੇਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: man mere anadhin jaag har chet ||
lines.translation: O my mind, remain awake and aware night and day, and think of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਣੀ ਖੇਤੀ ਰਖਿ ਲੈ ਕੂੰਜ ਪੜੈਗੀ ਖੇਤਿ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: aapanee khetee rakh lai koo(n)j paRaigee khet ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Protect your crops, or else the birds shall descend on your farm. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਕੀਆ ਇਛਾ ਪੂਰੀਆ ਸਬਦਿ ਰਹਿਆ ਭਰਪੂਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: man keeaa ichhaa pooreeaa sabadh rahiaa bharapoor ||
lines.translation: The desires of the mind are fulfilled, when one is filled to overflowing with the Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੈ ਭਾਇ ਭਗਤਿ ਕਰਹਿ ਦਿਨੁ ਰਾਤੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਵੇਖੈ ਸਦਾ ਹਦੂਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhai bhai bhagat kareh dhin raatee har jeeau vekhai sadhaa hadhoor ||
lines.translation: One who fears, loves, and is devoted to the Dear Lord day and night, sees Him always close at hand.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਸਦਾ ਮਨੁ ਰਾਤਾ ਭ੍ਰਮੁ ਗਇਆ ਸਰੀਰਹੁ ਦੂਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: sachai sabadh sadhaa man raataa bhram giaa sareerahu dhoor ||
lines.translation: Doubt runs far away from the bodies of those, whose minds remain forever attuned to the True Word of the Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਰਮਲੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਾਚਾ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੀਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: niramal saahib paiaa saachaa gunee gaheer ||2||
lines.translation: The Immaculate Lord and Master is found. He is True; He is the Ocean of Excellence. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਜਾਗੇ ਸੇ ਉਬਰੇ ਸੂਤੇ ਗਏ ਮੁਹਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo jaage se ubare soote ge muhai ||
lines.translation: Those who remain awake and aware are saved, while those who sleep are plundered.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਨ ਪਛਾਣਿਓ ਸੁਪਨਾ ਗਇਆ ਵਿਹਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sachaa sabadh na pachhaanio supanaa giaa vihai ||
lines.translation: They do not recognize the True Word of the Shabad, and like a dream, their lives fade away.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁੰਞੇ ਘਰ ਕਾ ਪਾਹੁਣਾ ਜਿਉ ਆਇਆ ਤਿਉ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: su(n)n(j)e ghar kaa paahunaa jiau aaiaa tiau jai ||
lines.translation: Like guests in a deserted house, they leave just exactly as they have come.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਮੁਖ ਜਨਮੁ ਬਿਰਥਾ ਗਇਆ ਕਿਆ ਮੁਹੁ ਦੇਸੀ ਜਾਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: manmukh janam birathaa giaa kiaa muh dhesee jai ||3||
lines.translation: The life of the self-willed manmukh passes uselessly. What face will he show when he passes beyond? ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਪੇ ਆਪਿ ਹੈ ਹਉਮੈ ਵਿਚਿ ਕਹਨੁ ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabh kichh aape aap hai haumai vich kahan na jai ||
lines.translation: God Himself is everything; those who are in their ego cannot even speak of this.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਪਛਾਣੀਐ ਦੁਖੁ ਹਉਮੈ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਗਵਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai sabadh pachhaaneeaai dhukh haumai vichahu gavai ||
lines.translation: Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, He is realized, and the pain of egotism is eradicated from within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਸੇਵਨਿ ਆਪਣਾ ਹਉ ਤਿਨ ਕੈ ਲਾਗਉ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: satagur sevan aapanaa hau tin kai laagau pai ||
lines.translation: I fall at the feet of those who serve their True Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਰਿ ਸਚੈ ਸਚਿਆਰ ਹਹਿ ਹਉ ਤਿਨ ਬਲਿਹਾਰੈ ਜਾਉ ॥੪॥੨੧॥੫੪॥
lines.transliteration: naanak dhar sachai sachiaar heh hau tin balihaarai jaau ||4||21||54||
lines.translation: O Nanak, I am a sacrifice to those who are found to be true in the True Court. ||4||21||54||

structure: The shabad opens with a clean question rather than pretending the seeker already knows how to serve.
It answers by accepting the Guru’s will, losing selfishness, staying awake, and guarding the field from what would devour it.
It ends with Shabad-realization, ego’s pain removed, and truth proven in service rather than in restless speculation.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad turns spiritual confusion toward the Guru, where hukam, service, Naam, wakefulness, and Shabad replace ego-driven wandering.
evidence.turn: The teaching moves from asking to accepting, then to guarding and serving, showing that clarity is lived through obedience rather than collected as an idea.
evidence.practicalImplication: When the mind scatters, do not keep multiplying paths. Ask the Guru, protect your attention, serve, and let the Shabad do its inward work.

title: Bow until wandering stops asking for the lead
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: This brief shabad begins in full prostration before the All-powerful Lord. It does not stay ceremonial: the bow becomes a direct cry for protection from wandering and for the Lord's own hand.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose devotion has gone formal while the mind still keeps roaming. Stayed with honestly, it turns bowing into dependence instead of performance.
takeaway: Let prayer become a real request for rescue.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਲੋਕੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: salok ||
lines.translation: Shalok:

lines.gurmukhi: ਡੰਡਉਤਿ ਬੰਦਨ ਅਨਿਕ ਬਾਰ ਸਰਬ ਕਲਾ ਸਮਰਥ ॥
lines.transliteration: dda(n)ddaut ba(n)dhan anik baar sarab kalaa samarath ||
lines.translation: I bow down, and fall to the ground in humble adoration, countless times, to the All-powerful Lord, who possesses all powers.

lines.gurmukhi: ਡੋਲਨ ਤੇ ਰਾਖਹੁ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇ ਕਰਿ ਹਥ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: ddolan te raakhahu prabhoo naanak dhe kar hath ||1||
lines.translation: Please protect me, and save me from wandering, God. Reach out and give Nanak Your Hand. ||1||

structure: The shabad opens in repeated prostration before the Lord's power.
From there it turns that posture into a plea for protection from wandering.
The closing movement rests by asking for the Lord's own hand rather than trusting the self.

evidence.coreClaim: This brief shabad begins in full prostration before the All-powerful Lord. It does not stay ceremonial: the bow becomes a direct cry for protection from wandering and for the Lord's own hand.
evidence.turn: From there it turns that posture into a plea for protection from wandering.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whose devotion has gone formal while the mind still keeps roaming. Stayed with honestly, it turns bowing into dependence instead of performance. Let prayer become a real request for rescue.

title: Choose the wealth that endures
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 22
summary: Guru Nanak turns the language of trade toward the soul: not every profit is worth carrying. Praise, truth, and Naam are the wealth that remains when false dealing falls away.
whyItMatters: This shabad challenges the part of us that tries to buy safety through possessions, upgrades, or visible success. It asks the harder question: after the deal is done, has the heart gained truth, or only another weight to carry?
takeaway: Before the next purchase, chase, or status move, ask whether it adds truth to the heart or only weight to the mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਵਣਜੁ ਕਰਹੁ ਵਣਜਾਰਿਹੋ ਵਖਰੁ ਲੇਹੁ ਸਮਾਲਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: vanaj karahu vanajaariho vakhar leh samaal ||
lines.translation: Make your deals, dealers, and take care of your merchandise.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੈਸੀ ਵਸਤੁ ਵਿਸਾਹੀਐ ਜੈਸੀ ਨਿਬਹੈ ਨਾਲਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: taisee vasat visaaheeaai jaisee nibahai naal ||
lines.translation: Buy that object which will go along with you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਗੈ ਸਾਹੁ ਸੁਜਾਣੁ ਹੈ ਲੈਸੀ ਵਸਤੁ ਸਮਾਲਿ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: agai saahu sujaan hai laisee vasat samaal ||1||
lines.translation: In the next world, the All-knowing Merchant will take this object and care for it. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਾਈ ਰੇ ਰਾਮੁ ਕਹਹੁ ਚਿਤੁ ਲਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhaiee re raam kahahu chit lai ||
lines.translation: O Siblings of Destiny, chant the Lord's Name, and focus your consciousness on Him.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਵਖਰੁ ਲੈ ਚਲਹੁ ਸਹੁ ਦੇਖੈ ਪਤੀਆਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: har jas vakhar lai chalahu sahu dhekhai pateeaai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Take the Merchandise of the Lord's Praises with you. Your Husband Lord shall see this and approve. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਾ ਰਾਸਿ ਨ ਸਚੁ ਹੈ ਕਿਉ ਤਿਨਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jinaa raas na sach hai kiau tinaa sukh hoi ||
lines.translation: Those who do not have the Assets of Truth-how can they find peace?

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੋਟੈ ਵਣਜਿ ਵਣੰਜਿਐ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਖੋਟਾ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: khoTai vanaj vana(n)jiaai man tan khoTaa hoi ||
lines.translation: By dealing their deals of falsehood, their minds and bodies become false.

lines.gurmukhi: ਫਾਹੀ ਫਾਥੇ ਮਿਰਗ ਜਿਉ ਦੂਖੁ ਘਣੋ ਨਿਤ ਰੋਇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: faahee faathe mirag jiau dhookh ghano nit roi ||2||
lines.translation: Like the deer caught in the trap, they suffer in terrible agony; they continually cry out in pain. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੋਟੇ ਪੋਤੈ ਨਾ ਪਵਹਿ ਤਿਨ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਦਰਸੁ ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: khoTe potai naa paveh tin har gur dharas na hoi ||
lines.translation: The counterfeit coins are not put into the Treasury; they do not obtain the Blessed Vision of the Lord-Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੋਟੇ ਜਾਤਿ ਨ ਪਤਿ ਹੈ ਖੋਟਿ ਨ ਸੀਝਸਿ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: khoTe jaat na pat hai khoT na seejhas koi ||
lines.translation: The false ones have no social status or honor. No one succeeds through falsehood.

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੋਟੇ ਖੋਟੁ ਕਮਾਵਣਾ ਆਇ ਗਇਆ ਪਤਿ ਖੋਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: khoTe khoT kamaavanaa aai giaa pat khoi ||3||
lines.translation: Practicing falsehood again and again, people come and go in reincarnation, and forfeit their honor. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਮਨੁ ਸਮਝਾਈਐ ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਸਾਲਾਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak man samajhaieeaai gur kai sabadh saalaeh ||
lines.translation: O Nanak, instruct your mind through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, and praise the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮ ਰੰਗਿ ਰਤਿਆ ਭਾਰੁ ਨ ਭਰਮੁ ਤਿਨਾਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: raam naam ra(n)g ratiaa bhaar na bharam tinaeh ||
lines.translation: Those who are imbued with the love of the Name of the Lord are not loaded down by doubt.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਲਾਹਾ ਅਗਲਾ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਹਰਿ ਮਨ ਮਾਹ ॥੪॥੨੩॥
lines.transliteration: har jap laahaa agalaa nirabhau har man maeh ||4||23||
lines.translation: Those who chant the Name of the Lord earn great profits; the Fearless Lord abides within their minds. ||4||23||

structure: Guru Nanak opens with the language of traders and merchandise, asking what kind of wealth can cross the final threshold.
The rahao names that wealth clearly: the Lord's praise, carried with focused consciousness.
The later verses expose false dealing as counterfeit, then return the mind to the Guru's Shabad, Naam, and fearless profit.

evidence.coreClaim: Guru Nanak turns trade language toward the soul: praise, truth, and Naam are the only wealth that can endure beyond false dealing.
evidence.turn: The rahao names the merchandise worth carrying — the Lord's praise held with focused consciousness.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before the next purchase, chase, or status move, ask whether it adds truth to the heart or only weight to the mind.

title: Center hope where the wandering mind cannot rule
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 273
summary: This shabad opens by showing the God-conscious being resting hope in the One alone. It turns the heart toward gathered hope, disciplined mind, and shared remembrance.
whyItMatters: This one speaks to the person whose attachment, distraction, or doubt keeps scattering the heart. It teaches a steadier center than private grasping can provide.
takeaway: Hope steadies when it is centered in the One.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਏਕ ਊਪਰਿ ਆਸ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee ek uoopar aas ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being centers his hopes on the One alone.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਨਹੀ ਬਿਨਾਸ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa nahee binaas ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being shall never perish.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਗਰੀਬੀ ਸਮਾਹਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai gareebee samaahaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is steeped in humility.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਪਰਉਪਕਾਰ ਉਮਾਹਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee paraupakaar umaahaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being delights in doing good to others.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਨਾਹੀ ਧੰਧਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai naahee dha(n)dhaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being has no worldly entanglements.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਲੇ ਧਾਵਤੁ ਬੰਧਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee le dhaavat ba(n)dhaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being holds his wandering mind under control.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਭਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai hoi su bhalaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being acts in the common good.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸੁਫਲ ਫਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sufal falaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being blossoms in fruitfulness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸੰਗਿ ਸਗਲ ਉਧਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sa(n)g sagal udhaar ||
lines.translation: In the Company of the God-conscious being, all are saved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਪੈ ਸਗਲ ਸੰਸਾਰੁ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee japai sagal sa(n)saar ||4||
lines.translation: O Nanak, through the God-conscious being, the whole world meditates on God. ||4||

structure: The shabad begins by gathering hope into a single center.
From there it shows the wandering mind being brought under truthful rule.
The closing movement rests by widening that steadiness into remembrance that benefits more than the self.

evidence.coreClaim: This shabad opens by showing the God-conscious being resting hope in the One alone. It turns the heart toward gathered hope, disciplined mind, and shared remembrance.
evidence.turn: From there it shows the wandering mind being brought under truthful rule.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one speaks to the person whose attachment, distraction, or doubt keeps scattering the heart. It teaches a steadier center than private grasping can provide. Hope steadies when it is centered in the One.

title: Longing is led home in saintly company
subtitle: Raag Maajh
summary: The shabad opens in aching longing for the Beloved and admits it cannot find the way alone. It searches mind and body, turns toward saintly company, and keeps asking to be brought near.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who feels alone, spiritually lost, or emotionally closed in. Taken faithfully, it changes loneliness from sealed isolation into guided longing and gives yearning somewhere truthful to go.
takeaway: Longing ripens when saintly company shows the way.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਾਝ ਮਹਲਾ ੪ ॥
lines.transliteration: maajh mahalaa chauthhaa ||
lines.translation: Maajh, Fourth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਧੁਸੂਦਨ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨ ਤਨ ਪ੍ਰਾਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: madhusoodhan mere man tan praanaa ||
lines.translation: The Lord is my mind, body and breath of life.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉ ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਦੂਜਾ ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਜਾਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: hau har bin dhoojaa avar na jaanaa ||
lines.translation: I do not know any other than the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੋਈ ਸਜਣੁ ਸੰਤੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਵਡਭਾਗੀ ਮੈ ਹਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਿਆਰਾ ਦਸੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: koiee sajan sa(n)t milai vaddabhaagee mai har prabh piaaraa dhasai jeeau ||1||
lines.translation: If only I could have the good fortune to meet some friendly Saint; he might show me the Way to my Beloved Lord God. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਖੋਜੀ ਭਾਲਿ ਭਾਲਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: hau man tan khojee bhaal bhaalaiee ||
lines.translation: I have searched my mind and body, through and through.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਉ ਪਿਆਰਾ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: kiau piaaraa preetam milai meree maiee ||
lines.translation: How can I meet my Darling Beloved, O my mother?

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਲਿ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਖੋਜੁ ਦਸਾਈ ਵਿਚਿ ਸੰਗਤਿ ਹਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਵਸੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: mil satasa(n)gat khoj dhasaiee vich sa(n)gat har prabh vasai jeeau ||2||
lines.translation: Joining the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, I ask about the Path to God. In that Congregation, the Lord God abides. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੇਰਾ ਪਿਆਰਾ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਰਖਵਾਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: meraa piaaraa preetam satigur rakhavaalaa ||
lines.translation: My Darling Beloved True Guru is my Protector.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮ ਬਾਰਿਕ ਦੀਨ ਕਰਹੁ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: ham baarik dheen karahu pratipaalaa ||
lines.translation: I am a helpless child-please cherish me.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੇਰਾ ਮਾਤ ਪਿਤਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਗੁਰ ਜਲ ਮਿਲਿ ਕਮਲੁ ਵਿਗਸੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: meraa maat pitaa gur satigur pooraa gur jal mil kamal vigasai jeeau ||3||
lines.translation: The Guru, the Perfect True Guru, is my Mother and Father. Obtaining the Water of the Guru, the lotus of my heart blossoms forth. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਦੇਖੇ ਨੀਦ ਨ ਆਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: mai bin gur dhekhe needh na aavai ||
lines.translation: Without seeing my Guru, sleep does not come.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨ ਤਨਿ ਵੇਦਨ ਗੁਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਲਗਾਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: mere man tan vedhan gur birahu lagaavai ||
lines.translation: My mind and body are afflicted with the pain of separation from the Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਦਇਆ ਕਰਹੁ ਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਲਹੁ ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰ ਮਿਲਿ ਰਹਸੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੪॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: har har dhiaa karahu gur melahu jan naanak gur mil rahasai jeeau ||4||2||
lines.translation: O Lord, Har, Har, show mercy to me, that I may meet my Guru. Meeting the Guru, servant Nanak blossoms forth. ||4||2||

structure: The shabad starts with longing honest enough to admit it cannot find the Beloved alone.
From there it searches inward and asks how true meeting can happen at all.
The closing movement rests by leaning toward saintly company as the place where yearning is guided home.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens in aching longing for the Beloved and admits it cannot find the way alone. It searches mind and body, turns toward saintly company, and keeps asking to be brought near.
evidence.turn: From there it searches inward and asks how true meeting can happen at all.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person who feels alone, spiritually lost, or emotionally closed in. Taken faithfully, it changes loneliness from sealed isolation into guided longing and gives yearning somewhere truthful to go. Longing ripens when saintly company shows the way.

title: Cling to the One until the mind cools
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: The pauree begins by praising those who release every other hold and cling to the One alone. It sets side by side Maya-drunk unrest with the peace and sweetness that arise in saintly company and Naam.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who is still hungry after chasing ten different supports. Kept near, it teaches that peace comes not from adding more but from holding one thing rightly.
takeaway: Let one true hold replace the many false ones.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਉੜੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: pauRee ||
lines.translation: Pauree:

lines.gurmukhi: ਠਠਾ ਮਨੂਆ ਠਾਹਹਿ ਨਾਹੀ ॥ ਜੋ ਸਗਲ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਏਕਹਿ ਲਪਟਾਹੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: ThaThaa manooaa Thaaheh naahee || jo sagal tiaag ekeh lapaTaahee ||
lines.translation: T'HAT'HA: Those who have abandoned all else, and who cling to the One Lord alone, do not make trouble for anyone's mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਠਹਕਿ ਠਹਕਿ ਮਾਇਆ ਸੰਗਿ ਮੂਏ ॥
lines.transliteration: Thahak Thahak maiaa sa(n)g mooe ||
lines.translation: Those who are totally absorbed and preoccupied with Maya are dead;

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਆ ਕੈ ਕੁਸਲ ਨ ਕਤਹੂ ਹੂਏ ॥
lines.transliteration: auaa kai kusal na katahoo hooe ||
lines.translation: they do not find happiness anywhere.

lines.gurmukhi: ਠਾਂਢਿ ਪਰੀ ਸੰਤਹ ਸੰਗਿ ਬਸਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: Thaa(n)dd paree sa(n)teh sa(n)g basiaa ||
lines.translation: One who dwells in the Society of the Saints finds a great peace;

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਤਹਾ ਜੀਅ ਰਸਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)mirat naam tahaa jeea rasiaa ||
lines.translation: the Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam becomes sweet to his soul.

lines.gurmukhi: ਠਾਕੁਰ ਅਪੁਨੇ ਜੋ ਜਨੁ ਭਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: Thaakur apune jo jan bhaiaa ||
lines.translation: That humble being, who is pleasing to his Lord and Master

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਉਆ ਕਾ ਮਨੁ ਸੀਤਲਾਇਆ ॥੨੮॥
lines.transliteration: naanak uaa kaa man seetalaiaa ||28||
lines.translation: - O Nanak, his mind is cooled and soothed. ||28||

structure: The shabad begins by honoring the one who clings to the Lord instead of multiplying dependencies.
From there it contrasts Maya-soaked unrest with the sweetness found in saintly company.
The closing movement rests with the cooled and soothed mind as the fruit of Naam.

evidence.coreClaim: The pauree begins by praising those who release every other hold and cling to the One alone. It sets side by side Maya-drunk unrest with the peace and sweetness that arise in saintly company and Naam.
evidence.turn: From there it contrasts Maya-soaked unrest with the sweetness found in saintly company.
evidence.practicalImplication: This is for anyone who is still hungry after chasing ten different supports. Kept near, it teaches that peace comes not from adding more but from holding one thing rightly. Let one true hold replace the many false ones.

title: Wear contentment before you speak of conquest
subtitle: Japji Sahib, Pauri 28
summary: The shabad starts by taking visible yogic marks and turning them inward — contentment, humility, meditation, remembrance. It opens into brotherhood and comes to rest where true conquest happens, in the mind rather than the room.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that is tempted by spiritual image, intensity, or performance. Taken seriously, it redirects discipline away from display and into a life that is humbler, steadier, and harder to fake.
takeaway: Conquer the mind before trying to conquer the world.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੁੰਦਾ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ਸਰਮੁ ਪਤੁ ਝੋਲੀ ਧਿਆਨ ਕੀ ਕਰਹਿ ਬਿਭੂਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: mu(n)dhaa sa(n)tokh saram pat jholee dhiaan kee kareh bibhoot ||
lines.translation: Make contentment your ear-rings, humility your begging bowl, and meditation the ashes you apply to your body.

lines.gurmukhi: ਖਿੰਥਾ ਕਾਲੁ ਕੁਆਰੀ ਕਾਇਆ ਜੁਗਤਿ ਡੰਡਾ ਪਰਤੀਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: khi(n)thaa kaal kuaaree kaiaa jugat dda(n)ddaa parateet ||
lines.translation: Let the remembrance of death be the patched coat you wear, let the purity of virginity be your way in the world, and let faith in the Lord be your walking stick.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਈ ਪੰਥੀ ਸਗਲ ਜਮਾਤੀ ਮਨਿ ਜੀਤੈ ਜਗੁ ਜੀਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: aaiee pa(n)thee sagal jamaatee man jeetai jag jeet ||
lines.translation: See the brotherhood of all mankind as the highest order of Yogis; conquer your own mind, and conquer the world.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਦੇਸੁ ਤਿਸੈ ਆਦੇਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: aadhes tisai aadhes ||
lines.translation: I bow to Him, I humbly bow.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਦਿ ਅਨੀਲੁ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਅਨਾਹਤਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਏਕੋ ਵੇਸੁ ॥੨੮॥
lines.transliteration: aadh aneel anaadh anaahat jug jug eko ves ||28||
lines.translation: The Primal One, the Pure Light, without beginning, without end. Throughout all the ages, He is One and the Same. ||28||

structure: The shabad begins by turning external marks of seriousness into inward discipline.
From there it widens the field into brotherhood and a different measure of strength.
The closing movement rests with conquest relocated to the mind and bowed before the Primal One.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by taking visible yogic marks and turning them inward — contentment, humility, meditation, remembrance. It opens into brotherhood and comes to rest where true conquest happens, in the mind rather than the room.
evidence.turn: From there it widens the field into brotherhood and a different measure of strength.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that is tempted by spiritual image, intensity, or performance. Taken seriously, it redirects discipline away from display and into a life that is humbler, steadier, and harder to fake. Conquer the mind before trying to conquer the world.

title: Conquer the self before you fight the world
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: This shabad opens by naming the true battlefield as the soul itself. It directs the heart toward Hukam, inner victory, and the peace that follows self-conquest.
whyItMatters: It matters for anyone living hot, defensive, or split between reaction and discipline. The shabad corrects the urge to master the room before mastering the self.
takeaway: Self-conquest is the way peace enters conduct.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਉੜੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: pauRee ||
lines.translation: Pauree:

lines.gurmukhi: ਣਾਣਾ ਰਣ ਤੇ ਸੀਝੀਐ ਆਤਮ ਜੀਤੈ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanaa ran te seejheeaai aatam jeetai koi ||
lines.translation: NANNA: One who conquers his own soul, wins the battle of life.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਅਨ ਸਿਉ ਲਰਿ ਮਰੈ ਸੋ ਸੋਭਾ ਦੂ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai an siau lar marai so sobhaa dhoo hoi ||
lines.translation: One who dies, while fighting against egotism and alienation, becomes sublime and beautiful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਣੀ ਮਿਟਾਇ ਜੀਵਤ ਮਰੈ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਉਪਦੇਸ ॥
lines.transliteration: manee miTai jeevat marai gur poore upadhes ||
lines.translation: One who eradicates his ego, remains dead while yet alive, through the Teachings of the Perfect Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੂਆ ਜੀਤੈ ਹਰਿ ਮਿਲੈ ਤਿਹ ਸੂਰਤਣ ਵੇਸ ॥
lines.transliteration: manooaa jeetai har milai teh sooratan ves ||
lines.translation: He conquers his mind, and meets the Lord; he is dressed in robes of honor.

lines.gurmukhi: ਣਾ ਕੋ ਜਾਣੈ ਆਪਣੋ ਏਕਹਿ ਟੇਕ ਅਧਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: naa ko jaanai aapano ekeh Tek adhaar ||
lines.translation: He does not claim anything as his own; the One Lord is his Anchor and Support.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰੈਣਿ ਦਿਣਸੁ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਰਹੈ ਸੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: rain dhinas simarat rahai so prabh purakh apaar ||
lines.translation: Night and day, he continually contemplates the Almighty, Infinite Lord God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰੇਣ ਸਗਲ ਇਆ ਮਨੁ ਕਰੈ ਏਊ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ren sagal iaa man karai euoo karam kamai ||
lines.translation: He makes his mind the dust of all; such is the karma of the deeds he does.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੁਕਮੈ ਬੂਝੈ ਸਦਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਪਾਇ ॥੩੧॥
lines.transliteration: hukamai boojhai sadhaa sukh naanak likhiaa pai ||31||
lines.translation: Understanding the Hukam of the Lord's Command, he attains everlasting peace. O Nanak, such is his pre-ordained destiny. ||31||

structure: The shabad begins by naming inner conquest as the real battle of life.
From there it anchors the seeker in the One rather than in private force.
The closing movement rests by tying peace to understanding Hukam instead of egoic victory.

evidence.coreClaim: This shabad opens by naming the true battlefield as the soul itself. It directs the heart toward Hukam, inner victory, and the peace that follows self-conquest.
evidence.turn: From there it anchors the seeker in the One rather than in private force.
evidence.practicalImplication: It matters for anyone living hot, defensive, or split between reaction and discipline. The shabad corrects the urge to master the room before mastering the self. Self-conquest is the way peace enters conduct.

title: Deeper fearlessness comes by tasting Naam
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 154
summary: The shabad begins with the strange claim that speaking the Unspoken becomes nectar. It carries the listener through lesser fears falling away, recognition through the Guru's Shabad, and hearts filled with the Lord's essence.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that is harassed by many small fears. Taken seriously, it replaces scattered fear-management with a deeper orientation to the One that makes the lesser fears lose force.
takeaway: Taste Naam deeply enough that lesser fears stop governing you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਅਕਥੁ ਕਹਾਇਆ ਅਪਿਓ ਪੀਆਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin akath kahaiaa apio peeaaiaa ||
lines.translation: Those who speak the Unspoken, drink in the Nectar.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨ ਭੈ ਵਿਸਰੇ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਇਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: an bhai visare naam samaiaa ||1||
lines.translation: Other fears are forgotten, and they are absorbed into the Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਆ ਡਰੀਐ ਡਰੁ ਡਰਹਿ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: kiaa ddareeaai ddar ddareh samaanaa ||
lines.translation: Why should we fear, when fear is dispelled by the Fear of God?

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਪਛਾਨਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: poore gur kai sabadh pachhaanaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Through the Shabad, the Word of the Perfect Guru, I recognize God. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਨਰ ਰਾਮੁ ਰਿਦੈ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਸਿ ॥ ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਇ ਮਿਲੇ ਸਾਬਾਸਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: jis nar raam ridhai har raas || sahaj subhai mile saabaas ||2||
lines.translation: Those whose hearts are filled with the Lord's essence are blessed and acclaimed, and intuitively absorbed into the Lord. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾਹਿ ਸਵਾਰੈ ਸਾਝ ਬਿਆਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaeh savaarai saajh biaal ||
lines.translation: Those whom the Lord puts to sleep, evening and morning

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਤ ਉਤ ਮਨਮੁਖ ਬਾਧੇ ਕਾਲ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: eit ut manmukh baadhe kaal ||3||
lines.translation: - those self-willed manmukhs are bound and gagged by Death, here and hereafter. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਰਾਮੁ ਰਿਦੈ ਸੇ ਪੂਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ahinis raam ridhai se poore ||
lines.translation: Those whose hearts are filled with the Lord, day and night, are perfect.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਰਾਮ ਮਿਲੇ ਭ੍ਰਮ ਦੂਰੇ ॥੪॥੧੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak raam mile bhram dhoore ||4||11||
lines.translation: O Nanak, they merge into the Lord, and their doubts are cast away. ||4||11||

structure: The shabad begins by turning what cannot be reduced to speech into nectar tasted by the heart.
From there it lets smaller fears fall away as the Guru's Shabad reveals the Lord.
The closing movement rests in hearts filled with divine essence instead of a thousand anxious fragments.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins with the strange claim that speaking the Unspoken becomes nectar. It carries the listener through lesser fears falling away, recognition through the Guru's Shabad, and hearts filled with the Lord's essence.
evidence.turn: From there it lets smaller fears fall away as the Guru's Shabad reveals the Lord.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that is harassed by many small fears. Taken seriously, it replaces scattered fear-management with a deeper orientation to the One that makes the lesser fears lose force. Taste Naam deeply enough that lesser fears stop governing you.

title: Rest where praise and possession lose their force
subtitle: Raag Gauree
summary: The shabad starts by locating rest in the Lord's sanctuary. It then equalizes pleasure and pain, gold and copper, praise and slander, until attachment loses the right to name reality.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whipped around by approval, possession, or comparison. Kept near, it makes detachment feel less like numbness and more like shelter strong enough to keep the heart even.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: steadiness grows where attachment loses its authority.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੯ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa nauvaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Ninth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਧੋ ਰਾਮ ਸਰਨਿ ਬਿਸਰਾਮਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: saadho raam saran bisaraamaa ||
lines.translation: Holy Saadhus: rest and peace are in the Sanctuary of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬੇਦ ਪੁਰਾਨ ਪੜੇ ਕੋ ਇਹ ਗੁਨ ਸਿਮਰੇ ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਨਾਮਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: bedh puraan paRe ko ieh gun simare har ko naamaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: This is the blessing of studying the Vedas and the Puraanas, that you may meditate on the Name of the Lord. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਲੋਭ ਮੋਹ ਮਾਇਆ ਮਮਤਾ ਫੁਨਿ ਅਉ ਬਿਖਿਅਨ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ॥ ਹਰਖ ਸੋਗ ਪਰਸੈ ਜਿਹ ਨਾਹਨਿ ਸੋ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਹੈ ਦੇਵਾ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: lobh moh maiaa mamataa fun aau bikhian kee sevaa || harakh sog parasai jeh naahan so moorat hai dhevaa ||1||
lines.translation: Greed, emotional attachment to Maya, possessiveness, the service of evil, pleasure and pain - those who are not touched by these, are the very embodiment of the Divine Lord. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਰਗ ਨਰਕ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਬਿਖੁ ਏ ਸਭ ਤਿਉ ਕੰਚਨ ਅਰੁ ਪੈਸਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: surag narak a(n)mirat bikh e sabh tiau ka(n)chan ar paisaa ||
lines.translation: Heaven and hell, ambrosial nectar and poison, gold and copper - these are all alike to them.

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਸਤਤਿ ਨਿੰਦਾ ਏ ਸਮ ਜਾ ਕੈ ਲੋਭੁ ਮੋਹੁ ਫੁਨਿ ਤੈਸਾ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: ausatat ni(n)dhaa e sam jaa kai lobh moh fun taisaa ||2||
lines.translation: Praise and slander are all the same to them, as are greed and attachment. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਏ ਬਾਧੇ ਜਿਹ ਨਾਹਨਿ ਤਿਹ ਤੁਮ ਜਾਨਉ ਗਿਆਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhukh sukh e baadhe jeh naahan teh tum jaanau giaanee ||
lines.translation: They are not bound by pleasure and pain - know that they are truly wise.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਤੁਮ ਮਾਨਉ ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਕੋ ਜੋ ਪ੍ਰਾਨੀ ॥੩॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: naanak mukat taeh tum maanau ieh bidh ko jo praanee ||3||7||
lines.translation: O Nanak, recognize those mortal beings as liberated, who live this way of life. ||3||7||

structure: The shabad starts with sanctuary as the true place of rest and peace.
From there it lays opposites side by side until their power to rule the mind starts thinning.
The closing movement rests in a steadiness that no longer depends on possession, praise, or slander.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by locating rest in the Lord's sanctuary. It then equalizes pleasure and pain, gold and copper, praise and slander, until attachment loses the right to name reality.
evidence.turn: From there it lays opposites side by side until their power to rule the mind starts thinning.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whipped around by approval, possession, or comparison. Kept near, it makes detachment feel less like numbness and more like shelter strong enough to keep the heart even. Keep this in front of you: steadiness grows where attachment loses its authority.

title: Do not forget the One who never forgets you
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 289
summary: The shabad begins with a repeated question — why forget the One who sees, gives, sustains, and rescues? It moves from gratitude into recognition, and ends with the humble servant holding remembrance instead of transactional effort.
whyItMatters: This one speaks to the person whose service has become dry, performative, or quietly bargaining. Stayed with, it restores memory of grace and makes devotion less like proving and more like responding.
takeaway: Remember the Giver before you start measuring your effort.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਜਿ ਘਾਲ ਨ ਭਾਨੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau bisarai j ghaal na bhaanai ||
lines.translation: Why forget Him, who does not overlook our efforts?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਜਿ ਕੀਆ ਜਾਨੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau bisarai j keeaa jaanai ||
lines.translation: Why forget Him, who acknowledges what we do?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਜਿਨਿ ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਦੀਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau bisarai jin sabh kichh dheeaa ||
lines.translation: Why forget Him, who has given us everything?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਜਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਜੀਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau bisarai j jeevan jeeaa ||
lines.translation: Why forget Him, who is the Life of the living beings?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਜਿ ਅਗਨਿ ਮਹਿ ਰਾਖੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau bisarai j agan meh raakhai ||
lines.translation: Why forget Him, who preserves us in the fire of the womb?

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਕੋ ਬਿਰਲਾ ਲਾਖੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur prasaadh ko biralaa laakhai ||
lines.translation: By Guru's Grace, rare is the one who realizes this.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਬਿਸਰੈ ਜਿ ਬਿਖੁ ਤੇ ਕਾਢੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau bisarai j bikh te kaaddai ||
lines.translation: Why forget Him, who lifts us up out of corruption?

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨਮ ਜਨਮ ਕਾ ਟੂਟਾ ਗਾਢੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: janam janam kaa TooTaa gaaddai ||
lines.translation: Those separated from Him for countless lifetimes, are re-united with Him once again.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਤਤੁ ਇਹੈ ਬੁਝਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur poorai tat ihai bujhaiaa ||
lines.translation: Through the Perfect Guru, this essential reality is understood.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਨ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: prabh apanaa naanak jan dhiaaiaa ||4||
lines.translation: O Nanak, God's humble servants meditate on Him. ||4||

structure: The shabad repeats the question until forgetfulness starts looking unreasonable.
From there it names the Lord as giver, life-source, protector, and rescuer from corruption.
It finally says the heart understands this through the Guru and answers by meditating on the Lord.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins with a repeated question — why forget the One who sees, gives, sustains, and rescues? It moves from gratitude into recognition, and ends with the humble servant holding remembrance instead of transactional effort.
evidence.turn: From there it names the Lord as giver, life-source, protector, and rescuer from corruption.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one speaks to the person whose service has become dry, performative, or quietly bargaining. Stayed with, it restores memory of grace and makes devotion less like proving and more like responding. Remember the Giver before you start measuring your effort.

title: Do not postpone remembrance
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 35
summary: The shabad starts by exposing the delaying mind that keeps waiting for the right time to remember the Lord. It responds with day-and-night attunement and devotion that does not forget the Beloved even briefly.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who respects practice in principle but keeps scheduling it out of reach. Taken steadily, it breaks procrastination's spell and teaches constancy more than intensity.
takeaway: Remembrance becomes true when it stops waiting for later.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa teejaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, Third Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੇ ਵੇਲਾ ਵਖਤੁ ਵੀਚਾਰੀਐ ਤਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਵੇਲਾ ਭਗਤਿ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: je velaa vakhat veechaareeaai taa kit velaa bhagat hoi ||
lines.translation: If we keep contemplating about the time as to when to remember the Lord, then when will we find the actual time for worship?

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਨਾਮੇ ਰਤਿਆ ਸਚੇ ਸਚੀ ਸੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: anadhin naame ratiaa sache sachee soi ||
lines.translation: Night and day, one who is attuned to the Name of the True Lord is true.

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਕੁ ਤਿਲੁ ਪਿਆਰਾ ਵਿਸਰੈ ਭਗਤਿ ਕਿਨੇਹੀ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: eik til piaaraa visarai bhagat kinehee hoi ||
lines.translation: If someone forgets the Beloved Lord, even for an instant, what sort of devotion is that?

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਸੀਤਲੁ ਸਾਚ ਸਿਉ ਸਾਸੁ ਨ ਬਿਰਥਾ ਕੋਇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: man tan seetal saach siau saas na birathaa koi ||1||
lines.translation: One whose mind and body are cooled and soothed by the True Lord-no breath of his is wasted. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨ ਹਰਿ ਕਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: mere man har kaa naam dhiaai ||
lines.translation: O my mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਚੀ ਭਗਤਿ ਤਾ ਥੀਐ ਜਾ ਹਰਿ ਵਸੈ ਮਨਿ ਆਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: saachee bhagat taa theeaai jaa har vasai man aai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: True devotional worship is performed when the Lord comes to dwell in the mind. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਹਜੇ ਖੇਤੀ ਰਾਹੀਐ ਸਚੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਬੀਜੁ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sahaje khetee raaheeaai sach naam beej pai ||
lines.translation: With intuitive ease, cultivate your farm, and plant the Seed of the True Name.

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੇਤੀ ਜੰਮੀ ਅਗਲੀ ਮਨੂਆ ਰਜਾ ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: khetee ja(n)mee agalee manooaa rajaa sahaj subhai ||
lines.translation: The seedlings have sprouted luxuriantly, and with intuitive ease, the mind is satisfied.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹੈ ਜਿਤੁ ਪੀਤੈ ਤਿਖ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kaa sabadh a(n)mrit hai jit peetai tikh jai ||
lines.translation: The Word of the Guru's Shabad is Ambrosial Nectar; drinking it in, thirst is quenched.

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਹੁ ਮਨੁ ਸਾਚਾ ਸਚਿ ਰਤਾ ਸਚੇ ਰਹਿਆ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: eih man saachaa sach rataa sache rahiaa samai ||2||
lines.translation: This true mind is attuned to Truth, and it remains permeated with the True One. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਖਣੁ ਵੇਖਣੁ ਬੋਲਣਾ ਸਬਦੇ ਰਹਿਆ ਸਮਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: aakhan vekhan bolanaa sabadhe rahiaa samai ||
lines.translation: In speaking, in seeing and in words, remain immersed in the Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਾਣੀ ਵਜੀ ਚਹੁ ਜੁਗੀ ਸਚੋ ਸਚੁ ਸੁਣਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: baanee vajee chahu jugee sacho sach sunai ||
lines.translation: The Word of the Guru's Bani vibrates throughout the four ages. As Truth, it teaches Truth.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਮੇਰਾ ਰਹਿ ਗਇਆ ਸਚੈ ਲਇਆ ਮਿਲਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai meraa reh giaa sachai liaa milai ||
lines.translation: Egotism and possessiveness are eliminated, and the True One absorbs them into Himself.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਨ ਕਉ ਮਹਲੁ ਹਦੂਰਿ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਸਚਿ ਰਹੇ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: tin kau mahal hadhoor hai jo sach rahe liv lai ||3||
lines.translation: Those who remain lovingly absorbed in the True One see the Mansion of His Presence close at hand. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਦਰੀ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਵਿਣੁ ਕਰਮਾ ਪਾਇਆ ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: nadharee naam dhiaaieeaai vin karamaa paiaa na jai ||
lines.translation: By His Grace, we meditate on the Naam, the Name of the Lord. Without His Mercy, it cannot be obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੈ ਭਾਗਿ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਲਹੈ ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਭੇਟੈ ਜਿਸੁ ਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: poorai bhaag satasa(n)gat lahai satagur bheTai jis aai ||
lines.translation: Through perfect good destiny, one finds the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, and one comes to meet the True Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਨਾਮੇ ਰਤਿਆ ਦੁਖੁ ਬਿਖਿਆ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: anadhin naame ratiaa dhukh bikhiaa vichahu jai ||
lines.translation: Night and day, remain attuned to the Naam, and the pain of corruption shall be dispelled from within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਸਬਦਿ ਮਿਲਾਵੜਾ ਨਾਮੇ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੪॥੨੨॥੫੫॥
lines.transliteration: naanak sabadh milaavaRaa naame naam samai ||4||22||55||
lines.translation: O Nanak, merging with the Shabad through the Name, one is immersed in the Name. ||4||22||55||

structure: The shabad begins by mocking the mind's endless search for a more convenient hour.
From there it insists on day-and-night attunement as the real measure of devotion.
The closing movement rests by showing that even brief forgetfulness exposes a heart still learning constancy.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by exposing the delaying mind that keeps waiting for the right time to remember the Lord. It responds with day-and-night attunement and devotion that does not forget the Beloved even briefly.
evidence.turn: From there it insists on day-and-night attunement as the real measure of devotion.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who respects practice in principle but keeps scheduling it out of reach. Taken steadily, it breaks procrastination's spell and teaches constancy more than intensity. Remembrance becomes true when it stops waiting for later.

title: Duality makes decoration hollow
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 18
summary: The shabad starts by calling the life deceived by duality cursed and unstable like a wall of sand. It travels through the uselessness of decoration without the Beloved and ends where beauty becomes real only by being pierced with the Shabad.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person still trying to fix inner separation with outer polish. Stayed with honestly, it exposes display without love and turns the heart back toward the Beloved.
takeaway: Without the Beloved and the Shabad, surface beauty stays false.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਧ੍ਰਿਗੁ ਜੀਵਣੁ ਦੋਹਾਗਣੀ ਮੁਠੀ ਦੂਜੈ ਭਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhirag jeevan dhohaaganee muThee dhoojai bhai ||
lines.translation: The life of the discarded bride is cursed. She is deceived by the love of duality.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਲਰ ਕੇਰੀ ਕੰਧ ਜਿਉ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਕਿਰਿ ਢਹਿ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: kalar keree ka(n)dh jiau ahinis kir ddeh pai ||
lines.translation: Like a wall of sand, day and night, she crumbles, and eventually, she breaks down altogether.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਨੁ ਸਬਦੈ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾ ਥੀਐ ਪਿਰ ਬਿਨੁ ਦੂਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: bin sabadhai sukh naa theeaai pir bin dhookh na jai ||1||
lines.translation: Without the Word of the Shabad, peace does not come. Without her Husband Lord, her suffering does not end. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੁੰਧੇ ਪਿਰ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਆ ਸੀਗਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: mu(n)dhe pir bin kiaa seegaar ||
lines.translation: O soul-bride, without your Husband Lord, what good are your decorations?

lines.gurmukhi: ਦਰਿ ਘਰਿ ਢੋਈ ਨ ਲਹੈ ਦਰਗਹ ਝੂਠੁ ਖੁਆਰੁ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhar ghar ddoiee na lahai dharageh jhooTh khuaar ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: In this world, you shall not find any shelter; in the world hereafter, being false, you shall suffer. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਿ ਸੁਜਾਣੁ ਨ ਭੁਲਈ ਸਚਾ ਵਡ ਕਿਰਸਾਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: aap sujaan na bhuliee sachaa vadd kirasaan ||
lines.translation: The True Lord Himself knows all; He makes no mistakes. He is the Great Farmer of the Universe.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਹਿਲਾ ਧਰਤੀ ਸਾਧਿ ਕੈ ਸਚੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਦੇ ਦਾਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: pahilaa dharatee saadh kai sach naam dhe dhaan ||
lines.translation: First, He prepares the ground, and then He plants the Seed of the True Name.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਉ ਨਿਧਿ ਉਪਜੈ ਨਾਮੁ ਏਕੁ ਕਰਮਿ ਪਵੈ ਨੀਸਾਣੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: nau nidh upajai naam ek karam pavai neesaan ||2||
lines.translation: The nine treasures are produced from Name of the One Lord. By His Grace, we obtain His Banner and Insignia. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕਉ ਜਾਣਿ ਨ ਜਾਣਈ ਕਿਆ ਤਿਸੁ ਚਜੁ ਅਚਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kau jaan na jaaniee kiaa tis chaj achaar ||
lines.translation: Some are very knowledgeable, but if they do not know the Guru, then what is the use of their lives?

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਧੁਲੈ ਨਾਮੁ ਵਿਸਾਰਿਆ ਮਨਮੁਖਿ ਅੰਧ ਗੁਬਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)dhulai naam visaariaa manmukh a(n)dh gubaar ||
lines.translation: The blind have forgotten the Naam, the Name of the Lord. The self-willed manmukhs are in utter darkness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਵਣੁ ਜਾਣੁ ਨ ਚੁਕਈ ਮਰਿ ਜਨਮੈ ਹੋਇ ਖੁਆਰੁ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: aavan jaan na chukiee mar janamai hoi khuaar ||3||
lines.translation: Their comings and goings in reincarnation do not end; through death and rebirth, they are wasting away. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਚੰਦਨੁ ਮੋਲਿ ਅਣਾਇਆ ਕੁੰਗੂ ਮਾਂਗ ਸੰਧੂਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: cha(n)dhan mol anaiaa ku(n)goo maa(n)g sa(n)dhoor ||
lines.translation: The bride may buy sandalwood oil and perfumes, and apply them in great quantities to her hair;

lines.gurmukhi: ਚੋਆ ਚੰਦਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਘਣਾ ਪਾਨਾ ਨਾਲਿ ਕਪੂਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: choaa cha(n)dhan bahu ghanaa paanaa naal kapoor ||
lines.translation: she may sweeten her breath with betel leaf and camphor,

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੇ ਧਨ ਕੰਤਿ ਨ ਭਾਵਈ ਤ ਸਭਿ ਅਡੰਬਰ ਕੂੜੁ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: je dhan ka(n)t na bhaaviee ta sabh adda(n)bar kooR ||4||
lines.translation: but if this bride is not pleasing to her Husband Lord, then all these trappings are false. ||4||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭਿ ਰਸ ਭੋਗਣ ਬਾਦਿ ਹਹਿ ਸਭਿ ਸੀਗਾਰ ਵਿਕਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabh ras bhogan baadh heh sabh seegaar vikaar ||
lines.translation: Her enjoyment of all pleasures is futile, and all her decorations are corrupt.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਬ ਲਗੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਨ ਭੇਦੀਐ ਕਿਉ ਸੋਹੈ ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: jab lag sabadh na bhedheeaai kiau sohai gurdhuaar ||
lines.translation: Until she has been pierced through with the Shabad, how can she look beautiful at Guru's Gate?

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਧੰਨੁ ਸੁਹਾਗਣੀ ਜਿਨ ਸਹ ਨਾਲਿ ਪਿਆਰੁ ॥੫॥੧੩॥
lines.transliteration: naanak dha(n)n suhaaganee jin seh naal piaar ||5||13||
lines.translation: O Nanak, blessed is that fortunate bride, who is in love with her Husband Lord. ||5||13||

structure: The shabad begins by naming duality as a deception that slowly collapses the whole life.
From there it mocks outward decoration and shelter when the heart is still false within.
The closing movement rests by saying real beauty begins only where the Shabad pierces and love for the Beloved is alive.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by calling the life deceived by duality cursed and unstable like a wall of sand. It travels through the uselessness of decoration without the Beloved and ends where beauty becomes real only by being pierced with the Shabad.
evidence.turn: From there it mocks outward decoration and shelter when the heart is still false within.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person still trying to fix inner separation with outer polish. Stayed with honestly, it exposes display without love and turns the heart back toward the Beloved. Without the Beloved and the Shabad, surface beauty stays false.

title: Ego is a chronic illness with a cure inside it
subtitle: Raag Aasaa
summary: Guru Angad does not flatter ego or mystify it. He names it as the pattern behind action and bondage, then says the cure appears through grace and the Guru's Shabad.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who keeps locating every problem outside the self while anger, injury, and self-importance keep returning. Stay close to this shabad after conflict, and it turns self-diagnosis from shame into treatment.
takeaway: Treat ego as illness and keep the Guru's medicine near.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਹਲਾ ੨ ॥
lines.transliteration: mahalaa doojaa ||
lines.translation: Second Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਏਹਾ ਜਾਤਿ ਹੈ ਹਉਮੈ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai ehaa jaat hai haumai karam kamaeh ||
lines.translation: This is the nature of ego, that people perform their actions in ego.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਏਈ ਬੰਧਨਾ ਫਿਰਿ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨੀ ਪਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai eiee ba(n)dhanaa fir fir jonee paeh ||
lines.translation: This is the bondage of ego, that time and time again, they are reborn.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਕਿਥਹੁ ਊਪਜੈ ਕਿਤੁ ਸੰਜਮਿ ਇਹ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai kithahu uoopajai kit sa(n)jam ieh jai ||
lines.translation: Where does ego come from? How can it be removed?

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਏਹੋ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਹੈ ਪਇਐ ਕਿਰਤਿ ਫਿਰਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai eho hukam hai piaai kirat firaeh ||
lines.translation: This ego exists by the Lord's Order; people wander according to their past actions.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਦੀਰਘ ਰੋਗੁ ਹੈ ਦਾਰੂ ਭੀ ਇਸੁ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai dheeragh rog hai dhaaroo bhee is maeh ||
lines.translation: Ego is a chronic disease, but it contains its own cure as well.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰੇ ਜੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਤਾ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਕਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: kirapaa kare je aapanee taa gur kaa sabadh kamaeh ||
