lines.translation: If the Lord grants His Grace, one acts according to the Teachings of the Guru's Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕੁ ਕਹੈ ਸੁਣਹੁ ਜਨਹੁ ਇਤੁ ਸੰਜਮਿ ਦੁਖ ਜਾਹਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak kahai sunahu janahu it sa(n)jam dhukh jaeh ||2||
lines.translation: Nanak says, listen, people: in this way, troubles depart. ||2||

structure: The shabad begins by naming ego as the force behind ordinary action and repeated bondage.
From there it asks the decisive question: where does ego arise, and how does it leave?
The closing movement rests by locating the cure in grace and in living the Guru's Shabad.

evidence.coreClaim: Guru Angad does not flatter ego or mystify it. He names it as the pattern behind action and bondage, then says the cure appears through grace and the Guru's Shabad.
evidence.turn: From there it asks the decisive question: where does ego arise, and how does it leave?
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who keeps locating every problem outside the self while anger, injury, and self-importance keep returning. Stay close to this shabad after conflict, and it turns self-diagnosis from shame into treatment. Treat ego as illness and keep the Guru's medicine near.

title: Everything becomes whole when Naam lives inside
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad begins by calling the path and cleansing bath perfect when the Name is in the heart. It keeps extending that wholeness through peace, contentment, yoga, glory, and the Creator's presence.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that lives with a chronic sense of incompletion and searching for patches everywhere else. Held quietly, it teaches that wholeness grows from sanctuary and Naam, not from frantic improvement.
takeaway: Wholeness begins when the Name is kept in the heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰਾ ਮਾਰਗੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਇਸਨਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: pooraa maarag pooraa isanaan ||
lines.translation: Perfect is the path; perfect is the cleansing bath.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: sabh kichh pooraa hiradhai naam ||1||
lines.translation: Everything is perfect, if the Naam is in the heart. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੀ ਰਹੀ ਜਾ ਪੂਰੈ ਰਾਖੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: pooree rahee jaa poorai raakhee ||
lines.translation: One's honor remains perfect, when the Perfect Lord preserves it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਕੀ ਸਰਣਿ ਜਨ ਤਾਕੀ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: paarabraham kee saran jan taakee ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: His servant takes to the Sanctuary of the Supreme Lord God. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: pooraa sukh pooraa sa(n)tokh ||
lines.translation: Perfect is the peace; perfect is the contentment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰਾ ਤਪੁ ਪੂਰਨ ਰਾਜੁ ਜੋਗੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: pooraa tap pooran raaj jog ||2||
lines.translation: Perfect is the penance; perfect is the Raja Yoga, the Yoga of meditation and success. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੈ ਮਾਰਗਿ ਪਤਿਤ ਪੁਨੀਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kai maarag patit puneet ||
lines.translation: On the Lord's Path, sinners are purified.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੀ ਸੋਭਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਲੋਕੀਕ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: pooree sobhaa pooraa lokeek ||3||
lines.translation: Perfect is their glory; perfect is their humanity. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਣਹਾਰੁ ਸਦ ਵਸੈ ਹਦੂਰਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: karanahaar sadh vasai hadhooraa ||
lines.translation: They dwell forever in the Presence of the Creator Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ ॥੪॥੪੫॥੧੧੪॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak meraa satigur pooraa ||4||45||114||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, my True Guru is Perfect. ||4||45||114||

structure: The shabad begins by placing perfection inside the heart that holds Naam.
From there it shows peace, contentment, honor, and humanity becoming whole under that same keeping.
The closing movement rests with the servant sheltered in the Supreme Lord and the True Guru confessed as complete.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by calling the path and cleansing bath perfect when the Name is in the heart. It keeps extending that wholeness through peace, contentment, yoga, glory, and the Creator's presence.
evidence.turn: From there it shows peace, contentment, honor, and humanity becoming whole under that same keeping.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that lives with a chronic sense of incompletion and searching for patches everywhere else. Held quietly, it teaches that wholeness grows from sanctuary and Naam, not from frantic improvement. Wholeness begins when the Name is kept in the heart.

title: Doubt does not die by wandering
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 22
summary: The shabad begins by saying the fire of doubt is not quenched by roaming. It turns the mind toward the Guru's word, saintly company, and the surrender of selfishness until peace merges like water in water.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who keeps moving, researching, and second-guessing without getting clearer. Taken seriously, it gives doubt a real treatment: the line is kept, ego loosens, and peace becomes more than an idea.
takeaway: Doubt clears when the Guru's word outlasts wandering.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਰਮੇ ਭਾਹਿ ਨ ਵਿਝਵੈ ਜੇ ਭਵੈ ਦਿਸੰਤਰ ਦੇਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bharame bhaeh na vijhavai je bhavai dhisa(n)tar dhes ||
lines.translation: The fire of doubt is not extinguished, even by wandering through foreign lands and countries.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਿ ਮੈਲੁ ਨ ਉਤਰੈ ਧ੍ਰਿਗੁ ਜੀਵਣੁ ਧ੍ਰਿਗੁ ਵੇਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tar mail na utarai dhirag jeevan dhirag ves ||
lines.translation: If inner filth is not removed, one's life is cursed, and one's clothes are cursed.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੋਰੁ ਕਿਤੈ ਭਗਤਿ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਬਿਨੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਉਪਦੇਸ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: hor kitai bhagat na hoviee bin satigur ke upadhes ||1||
lines.translation: There is no other way to perform devotional worship, except through the Teachings of the True Guru. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਰੇ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਅਗਨਿ ਨਿਵਾਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: man re gurmukh agan nivaar ||
lines.translation: O mind, become Gurmukh, and extinguish the fire within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਕਹਿਆ ਮਨਿ ਵਸੈ ਹਉਮੈ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨਾ ਮਾਰਿ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kaa kahiaa man vasai haumai tirasanaa maar ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Let the Words of the Guru abide within your mind; let egotism and desires die. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਮਾਣਕੁ ਨਿਰਮੋਲੁ ਹੈ ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮਿ ਪਤਿ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: man maanak niramol hai raam naam pat pai ||
lines.translation: The jewel of the mind is priceless; through the Name of the Lord, honor is obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਲਿ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਈਐ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਹਰਿ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: mil satasa(n)gat har paieeaai gurmukh har liv lai ||
lines.translation: Join the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, and find the Lord. The Gurmukh embraces love for the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪੁ ਗਇਆ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਮਿਲਿ ਸਲਲੈ ਸਲਲ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: aap giaa sukh paiaa mil salalai salal samai ||2||
lines.translation: Give up your selfishness, and you shall find peace; like water mingling with water, you shall merge in absorption. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਨ ਚੇਤਿਓ ਸੁ ਅਉਗੁਣਿ ਆਵੈ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin har har naam na chetio su aaugun aavai jai ||
lines.translation: Those who have not contemplated the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, are unworthy; they come and go in reincarnation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨ ਭੇਟਿਓ ਸੁ ਭਉਜਲਿ ਪਚੈ ਪਚਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jis satagur purakh na bheTio su bhaujal pachai pachai ||
lines.translation: One who has not met with the True Guru, the Primal Being, is bothered and bewildered in the terrifying world-ocean.

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਹੁ ਮਾਣਕੁ ਜੀਉ ਨਿਰਮੋਲੁ ਹੈ ਇਉ ਕਉਡੀ ਬਦਲੈ ਜਾਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: eih maanak jeeau niramol hai iau kauddee badhalai jai ||3||
lines.translation: This jewel of the soul is priceless, and yet it is being squandered like this, in exchange for a mere shell. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿੰਨਾ ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਰਸਿ ਮਿਲੈ ਸੇ ਪੂਰੇ ਪੁਰਖ ਸੁਜਾਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: ji(n)naa satagur ras milai se poore purakh sujaan ||
lines.translation: Those who joyfully meet with the True Guru are perfectly fulfilled and wise.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਮਿਲਿ ਭਉਜਲੁ ਲੰਘੀਐ ਦਰਗਹ ਪਤਿ ਪਰਵਾਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur mil bhaujal la(n)gheeaai dharageh pat paravaan ||
lines.translation: Meeting with the Guru, they cross over the terrifying world-ocean. In the Court of the Lord, they are honored and approved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇ ਮੁਖ ਉਜਲੇ ਧੁਨਿ ਉਪਜੈ ਸਬਦੁ ਨੀਸਾਣੁ ॥੪॥੨੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak te mukh ujale dhun upajai sabadh neesaan ||4||22||
lines.translation: O Nanak, their faces are radiant; the Music of the Shabad, the Word of God, wells up within them. ||4||22||

structure: The shabad begins by rejecting wandering as a cure for the inner fire.
From there it places the Guru's word inside the mind until ego and desire begin to die.
The closing movement rests in true company, surrendered selfishness, and peace merging without remainder.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by saying the fire of doubt is not quenched by roaming. It turns the mind toward the Guru's word, saintly company, and the surrender of selfishness until peace merges like water in water.
evidence.turn: From there it places the Guru's word inside the mind until ego and desire begin to die.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who keeps moving, researching, and second-guessing without getting clearer. Taken seriously, it gives doubt a real treatment: the line is kept, ego loosens, and peace becomes more than an idea. Doubt clears when the Guru's word outlasts wandering.

title: Fear leaves when schemes do
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 18
summary: The shabad opens with rescue arriving alongside subdued ego. It travels through useless plans being abandoned, fear leaving by meeting the True One, and ends in the genuine merchandise recognized through the Guru.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person trying to survive by cleverness, image-management, or endless contingency planning. Taken seriously, it turns salvation away from schemes and back toward the Guru's truth.
takeaway: Let ego and scheming fall so fear can leave with them.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਲੀ ਸਰੀ ਜਿ ਉਬਰੀ ਹਉਮੈ ਮੁਈ ਘਰਾਹੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhalee saree j ubaree haumai muiee gharaahu ||
lines.translation: It all worked out-I was saved, and the egotism within my heart was subdued.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੂਤ ਲਗੇ ਫਿਰਿ ਚਾਕਰੀ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਵੇਸਾਹੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhoot lage fir chaakaree satigur kaa vesaahu ||
lines.translation: The evil energies have been made to serve me, since I placed my faith in the True Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਲਪ ਤਿਆਗੀ ਬਾਦਿ ਹੈ ਸਚਾ ਵੇਪਰਵਾਹੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: kalap tiaagee baadh hai sachaa veparavaahu ||1||
lines.translation: I have renounced my useless schemes, by the Grace of the True, Carefree Lord. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਰੇ ਸਚੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਭਉ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: man re sach milai bhau jai ||
lines.translation: O mind, meeting with the True One, fear departs.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਕਿਉ ਥੀਐ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਸਬਦਿ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhai bin nirabhau kiau theeaai gurmukh sabadh samai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Without the Fear of God, how can anyone become fearless? Become Gurmukh, and immerse yourself in the Shabad. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੇਤਾ ਆਖਣੁ ਆਖੀਐ ਆਖਣਿ ਤੋਟਿ ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ketaa aakhan aakheeaai aakhan toT na hoi ||
lines.translation: How can we describe Him with words? There is no end to the descriptions of Him.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੰਗਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਕੇਤੜੇ ਦਾਤਾ ਏਕੋ ਸੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ma(n)gan vaale ketaRe dhaataa eko soi ||
lines.translation: There are so many beggars, but He is the only Giver.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸ ਕੇ ਜੀਅ ਪਰਾਣ ਹੈ ਮਨਿ ਵਸਿਐ ਸੁਖੁ ਹੋਇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: jis ke jeea paraan hai man vasiaai sukh hoi ||2||
lines.translation: He is the Giver of the soul, and the praanaa, the breath of life; when He dwells within the mind, there is peace. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਗੁ ਸੁਪਨਾ ਬਾਜੀ ਬਨੀ ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਖੇਲੁ ਖੇਲਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jag supanaa baajee banee khin meh khel khelai ||
lines.translation: The world is a drama, staged in a dream. In a moment, the play is played out.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਜੋਗੀ ਮਿਲਿ ਏਕਸੇ ਵਿਜੋਗੀ ਉਠਿ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)jogee mil ekase vijogee uTh jai ||
lines.translation: Some attain union with the Lord, while others depart in separation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਤਿਸੁ ਭਾਣਾ ਸੋ ਥੀਐ ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਕਰਣਾ ਜਾਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: jo tis bhaanaa so theeaai avar na karanaa jai ||3||
lines.translation: Whatever pleases Him comes to pass; nothing else can be done. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਵਸਤੁ ਵੇਸਾਹੀਐ ਸਚੁ ਵਖਰੁ ਸਚੁ ਰਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh vasat vesaaheeaai sach vakhar sach raas ||
lines.translation: The Gurmukhs purchase the Genuine Article. The True Merchandise is purchased with the True Capital.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨੀ ਸਚੁ ਵਣੰਜਿਆ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਾਬਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: jinee sach vana(n)jiaa gur poore saabaas ||
lines.translation: Those who purchase this True Merchandise through the Perfect Guru are blessed.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਵਸਤੁ ਪਛਾਣਸੀ ਸਚੁ ਸਉਦਾ ਜਿਸੁ ਪਾਸਿ ॥੪॥੧੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak vasat pachhaanasee sach saudhaa jis paas ||4||11||
lines.translation: O Nanak, one who stocks this True Merchandise shall recognize and realize the Genuine Article. ||4||11||

structure: The shabad begins by linking rescue with ego being quieted inside the heart.
From there it drops frantic planning and asks how fearlessness can arise without becoming Gurmukh.
The closing movement rests with true merchandise replacing the false trades of self-protection.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens with rescue arriving alongside subdued ego. It travels through useless plans being abandoned, fear leaving by meeting the True One, and ends in the genuine merchandise recognized through the Guru.
evidence.turn: From there it drops frantic planning and asks how fearlessness can arise without becoming Gurmukh.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person trying to survive by cleverness, image-management, or endless contingency planning. Taken seriously, it turns salvation away from schemes and back toward the Guru's truth. Let ego and scheming fall so fear can leave with them.

title: Forgiveness is the fast that makes one fearless
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 223
summary: The shabad starts by naming forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment as the real fast. It travels through release from disease and death-fear and comes to rest in the Lord already present within and without.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person holding hurt so tightly that it has started feeling like identity. Taken faithfully, it turns forgiveness from sentiment into discipline and lets fear lose some of its hidden power.
takeaway: Remember this: forgiveness, conduct, and contentment free the heart from fear.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਖਿਮਾ ਗਹੀ ਬ੍ਰਤੁ ਸੀਲ ਸੰਤੋਖੰ ॥
lines.transliteration: khimaa gahee brat seel sa(n)tokha(n) ||
lines.translation: To practice forgiveness is the true fast, good conduct and contentment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰੋਗੁ ਨ ਬਿਆਪੈ ਨਾ ਜਮ ਦੋਖੰ ॥
lines.transliteration: rog na biaapai naa jam dhokha(n) ||
lines.translation: Disease does not afflict me, nor does the pain of death.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੁਕਤ ਭਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਰੂਪ ਨ ਰੇਖੰ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: mukat bhe prabh roop na rekha(n) ||1||
lines.translation: I am liberated, and absorbed into God, who has no form or feature. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋਗੀ ਕਉ ਕੈਸਾ ਡਰੁ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jogee kau kaisaa ddar hoi ||
lines.translation: What fear does the Yogi have?

lines.gurmukhi: ਰੂਖਿ ਬਿਰਖਿ ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਸੋਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: rookh birakh gireh baahar soi ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: The Lord is among the trees and the plants, within the household and outside as well. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਰਭਉ ਜੋਗੀ ਨਿਰੰਜਨੁ ਧਿਆਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: nirabhau jogee nira(n)jan dhiaavai ||
lines.translation: The Yogis meditate on the Fearless, Immaculate Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਜਾਗੈ ਸਚਿ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: anadhin jaagai sach liv laavai ||
lines.translation: Night and day, they remain awake and aware, embracing love for the True Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਜੋਗੀ ਮੇਰੈ ਮਨਿ ਭਾਵੈ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: so jogee merai man bhaavai ||2||
lines.translation: Those Yogis are pleasing to my mind. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਾਲੁ ਜਾਲੁ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਅਗਨੀ ਜਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: kaal jaal braham aganee jaare ||
lines.translation: The trap of death is burnt by the Fire of God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਰਾ ਮਰਣ ਗਤੁ ਗਰਬੁ ਨਿਵਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaraa maran gat garab nivaare ||
lines.translation: Old age, death and pride are conquered.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਿ ਤਰੈ ਪਿਤਰੀ ਨਿਸਤਾਰੇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: aap tarai pitaree nisataare ||3||
lines.translation: They swim across, and save their ancestors as well. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਸੇਵੇ ਸੋ ਜੋਗੀ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: satigur seve so jogee hoi ||
lines.translation: Those who serve the True Guru are the Yogis.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੈ ਰਚਿ ਰਹੈ ਸੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhai rach rahai su nirabhau hoi ||
lines.translation: Those who remain immersed in the Fear of God become fearless.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੈਸਾ ਸੇਵੈ ਤੈਸੋ ਹੋਇ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: jaisaa sevai taiso hoi ||4||
lines.translation: They become just like the One they serve. ||4||

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਰ ਨਿਹਕੇਵਲ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਨਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: nar nihakeval nirabhau naau ||
lines.translation: The Name makes a man pure and fearless.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਾਥਹ ਨਾਥ ਕਰੇ ਬਲਿ ਜਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: anaatheh naath kare bal jaau ||
lines.translation: It makes the masterless become the master of all. I am a sacrifice to him.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੁਨਰਪਿ ਜਨਮੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਉ ॥੫॥
lines.transliteration: punarap janam naahee gun gaau ||5||
lines.translation: Such a person is not reincarnated again; he sings the Glories of God. ||5||

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਿ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਏਕੋ ਜਾਣੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tar baahar eko jaanai ||
lines.translation: Inwardly and outwardly, he knows the One Lord;

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦੇ ਆਪੁ ਪਛਾਣੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai sabadhe aap pachhaanai ||
lines.translation: through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, he realizes himself.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਦਰਿ ਨੀਸਾਣੈ ॥੬॥
lines.transliteration: saachai sabadh dhar neesaanai ||6||
lines.translation: He bears the Banner and Insignia of the True Shabad in the Lord's Court. ||6||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਬਦਿ ਮਰੈ ਤਿਸੁ ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਵਾਸਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabadh marai tis nij ghar vaasaa ||
lines.translation: One who dies in the Shabad abides in his own home within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਵੈ ਨ ਜਾਵੈ ਚੂਕੈ ਆਸਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: aavai na jaavai chookai aasaa ||
lines.translation: He does not come or go in reincarnation, and his hopes are subdued.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਕਮਲੁ ਪਰਗਾਸਾ ॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai sabadh kamal paragaasaa ||7||
lines.translation: Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, his heart-lotus blossoms forth. ||7||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਦੀਸੈ ਸੋ ਆਸ ਨਿਰਾਸਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo dheesai so aas niraasaa ||
lines.translation: Whoever is seen, is driven by hope and despair,

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਾਮ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਬਿਖੁ ਭੂਖ ਪਿਆਸਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: kaam karodh bikh bhookh piaasaa ||
lines.translation: by sexual desire, anger, corruption, hunger and thirst.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬਿਰਲੇ ਮਿਲਹਿ ਉਦਾਸਾ ॥੮॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: naanak birale mileh udhaasaa ||8||7||
lines.translation: O Nanak, those detached recluses who meet the Lord are so very rare. ||8||7||

structure: The shabad begins by redefining austerity through forgiveness and character instead of display.
From there it loosens disease, death-fear, and the authority of threat itself.
The closing movement rests in the Lord's nearness within and without, where fear has less room to stand.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by naming forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment as the real fast. It travels through release from disease and death-fear and comes to rest in the Lord already present within and without.
evidence.turn: From there it loosens disease, death-fear, and the authority of threat itself.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person holding hurt so tightly that it has started feeling like identity. Taken faithfully, it turns forgiveness from sentiment into discipline and lets fear lose some of its hidden power. Remember this: forgiveness, conduct, and contentment free the heart from fear.

title: Forgiveness settles into lasting peace
subtitle: Raag Sorath · Ang 628
summary: The shabad begins with the Perfect Guru's completed work — forgiveness given, peace found. It opens wider into peace spreading everywhere and comes to rest in singing the Guru's Bani and meditating on Naam.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who has tasted relief but does not yet know how to live from it. Stayed with, it keeps peace from becoming a passing feeling and turns it into praise, devotion, and a different atmosphere.
takeaway: Remember this: received forgiveness becomes lasting peace when it ripens into Naam.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋਰਠਿ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: soraTh mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Sorat'h, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਪੂਰੀ ਕੀਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur poorai pooree keenee ||
lines.translation: The Perfect Guru has done it perfectly.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਖਸ ਅਪੁਨੀ ਕਰਿ ਦੀਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: bakhas apunee kar dheenee ||
lines.translation: He blessed me with forgiveness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਤ ਅਨੰਦ ਸੁਖ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: nit ana(n)dh sukh paiaa ||
lines.translation: I have found lasting peace and bliss.

lines.gurmukhi: ਥਾਵ ਸਗਲੇ ਸੁਖੀ ਵਸਾਇਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: thaav sagale sukhee vasaiaa ||1||
lines.translation: Everywhere, the people dwell in peace. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਭਗਤਿ ਫਲ ਦਾਤੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kee bhagat fal dhaatee ||
lines.translation: Devotional worship to the Lord is what gives rewards.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਿ ਦੀਨੀ ਵਿਰਲੈ ਕਿਨ ਹੀ ਜਾਤੀ ॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur poorai kirapaa kar dheenee viralai kin hee jaatee || rahaau ||
lines.translation: The Perfect Guru, by His Grace, gave it to me; how rare are those who know this. ||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਗਾਵਹ ਭਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurbaanee gaaveh bhaiee ||
lines.translation: Sing the Word of the Guru's Bani, O Siblings of Destiny.

lines.gurmukhi: ਓਹ ਸਫਲ ਸਦਾ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: oh safal sadhaa sukhadhaiee ||
lines.translation: That is always rewarding and peace-giving.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak naam dhiaaiaa ||
lines.translation: Nanak has meditated on the Naam, the Name of the Lord.

lines.transliteration: poorab likhiaa paiaa ||2||17||81||
lines.translation: He has realized his pre-ordained destiny. ||2||17||81||

structure: The shabad starts with the Guru's forgiveness as a finished gift, not a tentative possibility.
From there it lets that peace widen until it changes the whole atmosphere around the heart.
The closing movement rests by fastening lasting peace to Bani, praise, and meditated Naam.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins with the Perfect Guru's completed work — forgiveness given, peace found. It opens wider into peace spreading everywhere and comes to rest in singing the Guru's Bani and meditating on Naam.
evidence.turn: From there it lets that peace widen until it changes the whole atmosphere around the heart.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who has tasted relief but does not yet know how to live from it. Stayed with, it keeps peace from becoming a passing feeling and turns it into praise, devotion, and a different atmosphere. Remember this: received forgiveness becomes lasting peace when it ripens into Naam.

title: Fresh Naam enters the mind
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 69
summary: The shabad opens by promising freedom from the old cycle through meeting the True Guru. It moves through understanding given by the Shabad and rests in the ever-fresh Naam abiding within the mind.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person worn out by inner repetition and hungry for something truly renewing. Return to this shabad before reaching for novelty, and it will move refreshment from outside stimulation to Naam settling within.
takeaway: Stay still long enough for fresh Naam to settle.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa teejaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, Third Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ ਮਿਲਿਐ ਫੇਰੁ ਨ ਪਵੈ ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: satigur miliaai fer na pavai janam maran dhukh jai ||
lines.translation: Meeting with the True Guru, you shall not have to go through the cycle of reincarnation again; the pains of birth and death will be taken away.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਸਭ ਸੋਝੀ ਹੋਈ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੈ ਰਹੈ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: poorai sabadh sabh sojhee hoiee har naamai rahai samai ||1||
lines.translation: Through the Perfect Word of the Shabad, all understanding is obtained; remain absorbed in the Name of the Lord. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਮੇਰੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਸਿਉ ਚਿਤੁ ਲਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: man mere satigur siau chit lai ||
lines.translation: O my mind, focus your consciousness on the True Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਰਮਲੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਦ ਨਵਤਨੋ ਆਪਿ ਵਸੈ ਮਨਿ ਆਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: niramal naam sadh navatano aap vasai man aai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: The Immaculate Naam itself, ever-fresh, comes to abide within the mind. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖਹੁ ਅਪੁਨੀ ਸਰਣਾਈ ਜਿਉ ਰਾਖਹਿ ਤਿਉ ਰਹਣਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: har jeeau raakhahu apunee saranaiee jiau raakheh tiau rahanaa ||
lines.translation: O Dear Lord, please protect and preserve me in Your Sanctuary. As You keep me, so do I remain.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਜੀਵਤੁ ਮਰੈ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਭਵਜਲੁ ਤਰਣਾ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai sabadh jeevat marai gurmukh bhavajal taranaa ||2||
lines.translation: Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, the Gurmukh remains dead while yet alive, and swims across the terrifying world-ocean. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਵਡੈ ਭਾਗਿ ਨਾਉ ਪਾਈਐ ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਸਬਦਿ ਸੁਹਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: vaddai bhaag naau paieeaai gurmat sabadh suhaiee ||
lines.translation: By great good fortune, the Name is obtained. Following the Guru's Teachings, through the Shabad, you shall be exalted.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪੇ ਮਨਿ ਵਸਿਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਸਹਜੇ ਰਹਿਆ ਸਮਾਈ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: aape man vasiaa prabh karataa sahaje rahiaa samaiee ||3||
lines.translation: God, the Creator Himself, dwells within the mind; remain absorbed in the state of intuitive balance. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਕਨਾ ਮਨਮੁਖਿ ਸਬਦੁ ਨ ਭਾਵੈ ਬੰਧਨਿ ਬੰਧਿ ਭਵਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: eikanaa manmukh sabadh na bhaavai ba(n)dhan ba(n)dh bhavaiaa ||
lines.translation: Some are self-willed manmukhs; they do not love the Word of the Shabad. Bound in chains, they wander lost in reincarnation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਲਖ ਚਉਰਾਸੀਹ ਫਿਰਿ ਫਿਰਿ ਆਵੈ ਬਿਰਥਾ ਜਨਮੁ ਗਵਾਇਆ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: lakh chauraaseeh fir fir aavai birathaa janam gavaiaa ||4||
lines.translation: Through 8.4 million lifetimes, they wander over and over again; they waste away their lives in vain. ||4||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਗਤਾ ਮਨਿ ਆਨੰਦੁ ਹੈ ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਰੰਗਿ ਰਾਤੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhagataa man aana(n)dh hai sachai sabadh ra(n)g raate ||
lines.translation: In the minds of the devotees there is bliss; they are attuned to the Love of the True Word of the Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਵਹਿ ਸਦ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਸਹਜੇ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਤੇ ॥੫॥
lines.transliteration: anadhin gun gaaveh sadh niramal sahaje naam samaate ||5||
lines.translation: Night and day, they constantly sing the Glories of the Immaculate Lord; with intuitive ease, they are absorbed into the Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||5||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਬਾਣੀ ਬੋਲਹਿ ਸਭ ਆਤਮ ਰਾਮੁ ਪਛਾਣੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh a(n)mirat baanee boleh sabh aatam raam pachhaanee ||
lines.translation: The Gurmukhs speak the Ambrosial Bani; they recognize the Lord, the Supreme Soul in all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਏਕੋ ਸੇਵਨਿ ਏਕੁ ਅਰਾਧਹਿ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਅਕਥ ਕਹਾਣੀ ॥੬॥
lines.transliteration: eko sevan ek araadheh gurmukh akath kahaanee ||6||
lines.translation: They serve the One; they worship and adore the One. The Gurmukhs speak the Unspoken Speech. ||6||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਸੇਵੀਐ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਵਸੈ ਮਨਿ ਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sachaa saahib seveeaai gurmukh vasai man aai ||
lines.translation: The Gurmukhs serve their True Lord and Master, who comes to dwell in the mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਦਾ ਰੰਗਿ ਰਾਤੇ ਸਚ ਸਿਉ ਅਪੁਨੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰੇ ਮਿਲਾਇ ॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: sadhaa ra(n)g raate sach siau apunee kirapaa kare milai ||7||
lines.translation: They are forever attuned to the Love of the True One, who bestows His Mercy and unites them with Himself. ||7||

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪੇ ਕਰੇ ਕਰਾਏ ਆਪੇ ਇਕਨਾ ਸੁਤਿਆ ਦੇਇ ਜਗਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: aape kare karaae aape ikanaa sutiaa dhei jagai ||
lines.translation: He Himself does, and He Himself causes others to do; He wakes some from their sleep.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪੇ ਮੇਲਿ ਮਿਲਾਇਦਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਬਦਿ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੮॥੭॥੨੪॥
lines.transliteration: aape mel milaidhaa naanak sabadh samai ||8||7||24||
lines.translation: He Himself unites us in Union; Nanak is absorbed in the Shabad. ||8||7||24||

structure: The shabad starts with the True Guru breaking the old cycle of pain and return.
From there it gives understanding through the Shabad instead of through restless striving.
The closing movement rests with Naam arriving as something ever-fresh inside the mind itself.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens by promising freedom from the old cycle through meeting the True Guru. It moves through understanding given by the Shabad and rests in the ever-fresh Naam abiding within the mind.
evidence.turn: From there it gives understanding through the Shabad instead of through restless striving.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person worn out by inner repetition and hungry for something truly renewing. Return to this shabad before reaching for novelty, and it will move refreshment from outside stimulation to Naam settling within. Stay still long enough for fresh Naam to settle.

title: Fruitful service gives the life a path
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: The shabad opens by calling service to the Lord fruitful and honorable. It travels through meeting the Guru, finding the Lord through the Shabad, and rejecting stubbornness as a path to discovery.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who feels busy but inwardly aimless. Kept close, it reconnects usefulness, guidance, and purpose so the day is no longer just maintenance.
takeaway: Remember this: the path becomes visible when service turns fruitful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਉੜੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: pauRee ||
lines.translation: Pauree:

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸਫਲ ਹੈ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਪਾਵੈ ਥਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kee sevaa safal hai gurmukh paavai thai ||
lines.translation: Service to the Lord is fruitful; through it, the Gurmukh is honored and approved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਹਰਿ ਭਾਵੈ ਤਿਸੁ ਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਸੋ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jis har bhaavai tis gur milai so har naam dhiaai ||
lines.translation: That person, with whom the Lord is pleased, meets with the Guru, and meditates on the Name of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਈਐ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਰਿ ਲਘਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur sabadhee har paieeaai har paar laghai ||
lines.translation: Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, the Lord is found. The Lord carries us across.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਹਠਿ ਕਿਨੈ ਨ ਪਾਇਓ ਪੁਛਹੁ ਵੇਦਾ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: manahaTh kinai na paio puchhahu vedhaa jai ||
lines.translation: Through stubborn-mindedness, none have found Him; go and consult the Vedas on this.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸੋ ਕਰੇ ਜਿਸੁ ਲਏ ਹਰਿ ਲਾਇ ॥੧੦॥
lines.transliteration: naanak har kee sevaa so kare jis le har lai ||10||
lines.translation: O Nanak, he alone serves the Lord, whom the Lord attaches to Himself. ||10||

structure: The shabad begins by giving service weight, fruit, and honor instead of treating it as leftover work.
From there it links guidance, Naam, and discovery through the Guru's Shabad.
The closing movement rests by stripping stubbornness of its authority and letting the Lord attach the servant.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens by calling service to the Lord fruitful and honorable. It travels through meeting the Guru, finding the Lord through the Shabad, and rejecting stubbornness as a path to discovery.
evidence.turn: From there it links guidance, Naam, and discovery through the Guru's Shabad.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who feels busy but inwardly aimless. Kept close, it reconnects usefulness, guidance, and purpose so the day is no longer just maintenance. Remember this: the path becomes visible when service turns fruitful.

title: God-consciousness is received, not staged
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 273
summary: This section opens by saying the God-conscious being knows God and loves the One alone. It keeps insisting that such stature is given by God Himself, which means greatness, purity, and fearlessness cannot be self-manufactured.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who feels unseen and tries to build spiritual worth through effort or image. Taken seriously, it returns identity to what God causes rather than what the self stages.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: let God, not image, decide what greatness is.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਕਾ ਬੇਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee braham kaa betaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being knows God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਏਕ ਸੰਗਿ ਹੇਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee ek sa(n)g hetaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is in love with the One alone.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਹੋਇ ਅਚਿੰਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai hoi achi(n)t ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is carefree.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਮੰਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa niramal ma(n)t ||
lines.translation: Pure are the Teachings of the God-conscious being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਿਸੁ ਕਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਆਪਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee jis karai prabh aap ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is made so by God Himself.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਬਡ ਪਰਤਾਪ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa badd parataap ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is gloriously great.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਦਰਸੁ ਬਡਭਾਗੀ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa dharas baddabhaagee paieeaai ||
lines.translation: The Darshan, the Blessed Vision of the God-conscious being, is obtained by great good fortune.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਉ ਬਲਿ ਬਲਿ ਜਾਈਐ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kau bal bal jaieeaai ||
lines.translation: To the God-conscious being, I make my life a sacrifice.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਉ ਖੋਜਹਿ ਮਹੇਸੁਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kau khojeh mahesur ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is sought by the great god Shiva.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਆਪਿ ਪਰਮੇਸੁਰ ॥੬॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee aap paramesur ||6||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the God-conscious being is Himself the Supreme Lord God. ||6||

structure: The shabad starts with intimate knowledge and singular love for God.
From there it treats purity and carefree living as fruit, not performance.
The closing movement rests by saying the God-conscious being is made by God, then lifted into true greatness.

evidence.coreClaim: This section opens by saying the God-conscious being knows God and loves the One alone. It keeps insisting that such stature is given by God Himself, which means greatness, purity, and fearlessness cannot be self-manufactured.
evidence.turn: From there it treats purity and carefree living as fruit, not performance.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person who feels unseen and tries to build spiritual worth through effort or image. Taken seriously, it returns identity to what God causes rather than what the self stages. Keep this in front of you: let God, not image, decide what greatness is.

title: Mercy remembered becomes living Naam
subtitle: Mundhaavanee Fifth Mehl
summary: The shabad opens in confession — I did not recognize what You did for me. It moves through unworthiness and pity received, then blooms when the True Guru is met and Naam makes body and mind green again.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who has gone numb to mercy or embarrassed by their own ingratitude. Stayed with honestly, it turns shame into gratitude and gratitude into renewed life in Naam.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: honest gratitude becomes the doorway to mercy and Naam.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਲੋਕ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: salok mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Shalok, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਤੋ ਨਾਹੀ ਮੈਨੋ ਜੋਗੁ ਕੀਤੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: teraa keetaa jaato naahee maino jog keetoiee ||
lines.translation: I have not appreciated what You have done for me, Lord; only You can make me worthy.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੈ ਨਿਰਗੁਣਿਆਰੇ ਕੋ ਗੁਣੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਆਪੇ ਤਰਸੁ ਪਇਓਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: mai niraguniaare ko gun naahee aape taras pioiee ||
lines.translation: I am unworthy - I have no worth or virtues at all. You have taken pity on me.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਰਸੁ ਪਇਆ ਮਿਹਰਾਮਤਿ ਹੋਈ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਸਜਣੁ ਮਿਲਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: taras piaa miharaamat hoiee satigur sajan miliaa ||
lines.translation: You took pity on me, and blessed me with Your Mercy, and I have met the True Guru, my Friend.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਤਾਂ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਤਨੁ ਮਨੁ ਥੀਵੈ ਹਰਿਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak naam milai taa(n) jeevaa(n) tan man theevai hariaa ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, if I am blessed with the Naam, I live, and my body and mind blossom forth. ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by telling the truth about unnoticed grace.
From there it deepens into confessed unworthiness and the Lord's pity.
The closing movement rests with the Guru's friendship and Naam making the whole being live again.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens in confession — I did not recognize what You did for me. It moves through unworthiness and pity received, then blooms when the True Guru is met and Naam makes body and mind green again.
evidence.turn: From there it deepens into confessed unworthiness and the Lord's pity.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who has gone numb to mercy or embarrassed by their own ingratitude. Stayed with honestly, it turns shame into gratitude and gratitude into renewed life in Naam. Keep this in front of you: honest gratitude becomes the doorway to mercy and Naam.

title: Holy company breaks the crowded heat inside
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 171
summary: The shabad begins with the body crowded by desire and anger, then shows what changes when the Holy Saint is actually met. It turns from the thorn of ego and wandering pain toward humility, sanctuary, and peace supported by Naam.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person living overheated, reactive, and internally crowded. Hold this shabad when anger and craving feel stronger than judgment, and it will make holy company feel like treatment rather than ornament.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: take the overheated self back from distance until Naam becomes support.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਪੂਰਬੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੪ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee poorabee mahalaa chauthhaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree Poorbee, Fourth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਾਮਿ ਕਰੋਧਿ ਨਗਰੁ ਬਹੁ ਭਰਿਆ ਮਿਲਿ ਸਾਧੂ ਖੰਡਲ ਖੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: kaam karodh nagar bahu bhariaa mil saadhoo kha(n)ddal kha(n)ddaa he ||
lines.translation: The body-village is filled to overflowing with sexual desire and anger, which were broken into bits when I met with the Holy Saint.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰਬਿ ਲਿਖਤ ਲਿਖੇ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਮਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਲਿਵ ਮੰਡਲ ਮੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: poorab likhat likhe gur paiaa man har liv ma(n)ddal ma(n)ddaa he ||1||
lines.translation: By pre-ordained destiny, I have met with the Guru. I have entered into the realm of the Lord's Love. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਸਾਧੂ ਅੰਜੁਲੀ ਪੁੰਨੁ ਵਡਾ ਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar saadhoo a(n)julee pu(n)n vaddaa he ||
lines.translation: Greet the Holy Saint with your palms pressed together; this is an act of great merit.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਡੰਡਉਤ ਪੁਨੁ ਵਡਾ ਹੇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar dda(n)ddaut pun vaddaa he ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Bow down before Him; this is a virtuous action indeed. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਕਤ ਹਰਿ ਰਸ ਸਾਦੁ ਨ ਜਾਨਿਆ ਤਿਨ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਹਉਮੈ ਕੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: saakat har ras saadh na jaaniaa tin a(n)tar haumai ka(n)ddaa he ||
lines.translation: The wicked shaaktas, the faithless cynics, do not know the taste of the Lord's sublime essence. The thorn of egotism is embedded deep within them.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਉ ਜਿਉ ਚਲਹਿ ਚੁਭੈ ਦੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਹਿ ਜਮਕਾਲੁ ਸਹਹਿ ਸਿਰਿ ਡੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: jiau jiau chaleh chubhai dhukh paaveh jamakaal saheh sir dda(n)ddaa he ||2||
lines.translation: The more they walk away, the deeper it sticks into them, and the more they suffer in pain, until finally, the Messenger of Death smashes his club against their heads. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਜਨ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਣੇ ਦੁਖੁ ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਵ ਖੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: har jan har har naam samaane dhukh janam maran bhav kha(n)ddaa he ||
lines.translation: The humble servants of the Lord are absorbed in the Name of the Lord, Har, Har. The pain of birth and the fear of death are eradicated.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਬਹੁ ਸੋਭ ਖੰਡ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: abinaasee purakh paiaa paramesar bahu sobh kha(n)dd brahama(n)ddaa he ||3||
lines.translation: They have obtained the Imperishable Supreme Being, the Transcendent Lord God, and they obtain great honor throughout all the worlds and realms. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮ ਗਰੀਬ ਮਸਕੀਨ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਤੇਰੇ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਖੁ ਰਾਖੁ ਵਡ ਵਡਾ ਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ham gareeb masakeen prabh tere har raakh raakh vadd vaddaa he ||
lines.translation: I am poor and meek, God, but I am Yours! Save me, please save me, O Greatest of the Great!

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਧਾਰੁ ਟੇਕ ਹੈ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੇ ਹੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਮੰਡਾ ਹੇ ॥੪॥੮॥੨੨॥੬੦॥
lines.transliteration: jan naanak naam adhaar Tek hai har naame hee sukh ma(n)ddaa he ||4||8||22||60||
lines.translation: Servant Nanak takes the Sustenance and Support of the Naam. In the Name of the Lord, he enjoys celestial peace. ||4||8||22||60||

structure: The shabad begins by naming the body as overcrowded with desire and anger until saintly company breaks the pattern.
From there it exposes ego as the thorn that hurts more the farther one walks from the Lord.
The closing movement rests in meek prayer and Naam as the real support of peace.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins with the body crowded by desire and anger, then shows what changes when the Holy Saint is actually met. It turns from the thorn of ego and wandering pain toward humility, sanctuary, and peace supported by Naam.
evidence.turn: From there it exposes ego as the thorn that hurts more the farther one walks from the Lord.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person living overheated, reactive, and internally crowded. Hold this shabad when anger and craving feel stronger than judgment, and it will make holy company feel like treatment rather than ornament. Keep this in front of you: take the overheated self back from distance until Naam becomes support.

title: Holy company washes deeper than self-scrubbing
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad opens by calling the sight of the saints a perfect cleansing bath. It travels through ego falling away, the One becoming visible everywhere, and the heart being irrigated with Naam.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person trying to clean themselves with effort while envy, ego, and the five passions keep returning. Kept close, it turns cleansing from private labor into grace received in holy company.
takeaway: Seek the company that washes the heart and turns it toward Naam.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਕੀ ਧੂਰਿ ਮਿਟੇ ਅਘ ਕੋਟ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t kee dhoor miTe agh koT ||
lines.translation: Millions of sins are wiped away by the dust of the feet of the Saints.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਤੇ ਛੋਟ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t prasaadh janam maran te chhoT ||1||
lines.translation: By the Grace of the Saints, one is released from birth and death. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਕਾ ਦਰਸੁ ਪੂਰਨ ਇਸਨਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t kaa dharas pooran isanaan ||
lines.translation: The Blessed Vision of the Saints is the perfect cleansing bath.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਤੇ ਜਪੀਐ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t kirapaa te japeeaai naam ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: By the Grace of the Saints, one comes to chant the Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਕੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਮਿਟਿਆ ਅਹੰਕਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t kai sa(n)g miTiaa aha(n)kaar ||
lines.translation: In the Society of the Saints, egotism is shed,

lines.gurmukhi: ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਆਵੈ ਸਭੁ ਏਕੰਕਾਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: dhirasaT aavai sabh eka(n)kaar ||2||
lines.translation: and the One Lord is seen everywhere. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਸੁਪ੍ਰਸੰਨ ਆਏ ਵਸਿ ਪੰਚਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t suprasa(n)n aae vas pa(n)chaa ||
lines.translation: By the pleasure of the Saints, the five passions are overpowered,

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਿਦੈ ਲੈ ਸੰਚਾ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)mrit naam ridhai lai sa(n)chaa ||3||
lines.translation: and the heart is irrigated with the Ambrosial Naam. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾ ਕਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰਮ ॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak jaa kaa pooraa karam ||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, one whose karma is perfect,

lines.transliteration: tis bheTe saadhoo ke charan ||4||46||115||
lines.translation: touches the feet of the Holy. ||4||46||115||

structure: The shabad begins by naming saintly presence itself as a complete cleansing.
From there it shows what that cleansing does: ego thins, the One is seen, and the passions lose ground.
The closing movement rests with perfect karma expressed as meeting the feet of the holy.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens by calling the sight of the saints a perfect cleansing bath. It travels through ego falling away, the One becoming visible everywhere, and the heart being irrigated with Naam.
evidence.turn: From there it shows what that cleansing does: ego thins, the One is seen, and the passions lose ground.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person trying to clean themselves with effort while envy, ego, and the five passions keep returning. Kept close, it turns cleansing from private labor into grace received in holy company. Seek the company that washes the heart and turns it toward Naam.

title: Honor the one through whom life arrives
subtitle: Raag Aasaa
summary: The shabad begins by tracing birth, friendship, marriage, and lineage through woman. It then asks how she can be called bad when kings themselves are born from her, and ends in radiant mouths that praise the Lord.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that has been shaped by casual contempt, inherited patriarchy, or speech that lowers women while depending on them. Taken seriously, it restores reverence, humility, and a truer social imagination.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: refuse to despise the one through whom human life comes.

lines.transliteration: mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡਿ ਜੰਮੀਐ ਭੰਡਿ ਨਿੰਮੀਐ ਭੰਡਿ ਮੰਗਣੁ ਵੀਆਹੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)dd ja(n)meeaai bha(n)dd ni(n)meeaai bha(n)dd ma(n)gan veeaahu ||
lines.translation: From woman, man is born; within woman, man is conceived; to woman he is engaged and married.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡਹੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਦੋਸਤੀ ਭੰਡਹੁ ਚਲੈ ਰਾਹੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)ddahu hovai dhosatee bha(n)ddahu chalai raahu ||
lines.translation: Woman becomes his friend; through woman, the future generations come.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡੁ ਮੁਆ ਭੰਡੁ ਭਾਲੀਐ ਭੰਡਿ ਹੋਵੈ ਬੰਧਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)dd muaa bha(n)dd bhaaleeaai bha(n)dd hovai ba(n)dhaan ||
lines.translation: When his woman dies, he seeks another woman; to woman he is bound.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਮੰਦਾ ਆਖੀਐ ਜਿਤੁ ਜੰਮਹਿ ਰਾਜਾਨ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau ma(n)dhaa aakheeaai jit ja(n)meh raajaan ||
lines.translation: So why call her bad? From her, kings are born.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡਹੁ ਹੀ ਭੰਡੁ ਊਪਜੈ ਭੰਡੈ ਬਾਝੁ ਨ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)ddahu hee bha(n)dd uoopajai bha(n)ddai baajh na koi ||
lines.translation: From woman, woman is born; without woman, there would be no one at all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਭੰਡੈ ਬਾਹਰਾ ਏਕੋ ਸਚਾ ਸੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak bha(n)ddai baaharaa eko sachaa soi ||
lines.translation: O Nanak, only the True Lord is without a woman.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਦਾ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ਭਾਗਾ ਰਤੀ ਚਾਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: jit mukh sadhaa saalaaheeaai bhaagaa ratee chaar ||
lines.translation: That mouth which praises the Lord continually is blessed and beautiful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇ ਮੁਖ ਊਜਲੇ ਤਿਤੁ ਸਚੈ ਦਰਬਾਰਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak te mukh uoojale tit sachai dharabaar ||2||
lines.translation: O Nanak, those faces shall be radiant in the Court of the True Lord. ||2||

structure: The shabad begins by naming how thoroughly human life is bound up with woman.
From there it confronts contempt directly and calls it irrational in the face of reality.
The closing movement rests by lifting the mouth that praises the Lord rather than degrading His creation.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by tracing birth, friendship, marriage, and lineage through woman. It then asks how she can be called bad when kings themselves are born from her, and ends in radiant mouths that praise the Lord.
evidence.turn: From there it confronts contempt directly and calls it irrational in the face of reality.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that has been shaped by casual contempt, inherited patriarchy, or speech that lowers women while depending on them. Taken seriously, it restores reverence, humility, and a truer social imagination. Keep this in front of you: refuse to despise the one through whom human life comes.

title: Hope in the Lord outlives the world's reach
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad begins by describing the one held so closely by the Lord that stain and worldly pressure cannot settle. It moves through freedom from anxiety and pain, then ends in the Guru who shows the Perfect Lord.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person living in anticipation of the next blow, opinion, or setback. Taken steadily, it relocates safety from changing circumstances to the One who keeps the heart.
takeaway: Let hope in the Lord outrank the world's reach.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕਉ ਤੁਮ ਭਏ ਸਮਰਥ ਅੰਗਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kau tum bhe samarath a(n)gaa ||
lines.translation: Those who have You on their side, O All-powerful Lord

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕਉ ਕਛੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਕਾਲੰਗਾ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: taa kau kachh naahee kaala(n)gaa ||1||
lines.translation: - no black stain can stick to them. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਾਧਉ ਜਾ ਕਉ ਹੈ ਆਸ ਤੁਮਾਰੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: maadhau jaa kau hai aas tumaaree ||
lines.translation: O Lord of wealth, those who place their hopes in You

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕਉ ਕਛੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੰਸਾਰੀ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: taa kau kachh naahee sa(n)saaree ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: - nothing of the world can touch them at all. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕੈ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kai hiradhai Thaakur hoi ||
lines.translation: Those whose hearts are filled with their Lord and Master

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕਉ ਸਹਸਾ ਨਾਹੀ ਕੋਇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: taa kau sahasaa naahee koi ||2||
lines.translation: - no anxiety can affect them. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕਉ ਤੁਮ ਦੀਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਧੀਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kau tum dheenee prabh dheer ||
lines.translation: Those, unto whom You give Your consolation, God

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕੈ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਪੀਰ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: taa kai nikaT na aavai peer ||3||
lines.translation: - pain does not even approach them. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਮੈ ਸੋ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak mai so gur paiaa ||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, I have found that Guru,

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਪੂਰਨ ਦੇਖਾਇਆ ॥੪॥੪੧॥੧੧੦॥
lines.transliteration: paarabraham pooran dhekhaiaa ||4||41||110||
lines.translation: who has shown me the Perfect, Supreme Lord God. ||4||41||110||

structure: The shabad begins by saying the world cannot finally mark the one supported by the Lord.
From there it widens that protection into freedom from anxiety and even approaching pain.
The closing movement rests in gratitude for the Guru who reveals the Perfect Lord behind that steadiness.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by describing the one held so closely by the Lord that stain and worldly pressure cannot settle. It moves through freedom from anxiety and pain, then ends in the Guru who shows the Perfect Lord.
evidence.turn: From there it widens that protection into freedom from anxiety and even approaching pain.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person living in anticipation of the next blow, opinion, or setback. Taken steadily, it relocates safety from changing circumstances to the One who keeps the heart. Let hope in the Lord outrank the world's reach.

title: Hukam is the atmosphere of everything
subtitle: Japji Sahib, Pauri 2
summary: The shabad starts by placing form, life, greatness, pain, blessing, and wandering inside Hukam. It keeps widening that field until nothing stands outside the Command and ego has nowhere left to boast.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who is still dividing life into acceptable turns and unacceptable ones. Stayed with, it enlarges reality beyond protest and makes humility possible inside every condition.
takeaway: Everything stands within Hukam, and ego thins when this is seen.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੁਕਮੀ ਹੋਵਨਿ ਆਕਾਰ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਨ ਕਹਿਆ ਜਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: hukamee hovan aakaar hukam na kahiaa jaiee ||
lines.translation: By His Command, bodies are created; His Command cannot be described.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੁਕਮੀ ਹੋਵਨਿ ਜੀਅ ਹੁਕਮਿ ਮਿਲੈ ਵਡਿਆਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: hukamee hovan jeea hukam milai vaddiaaiee ||
lines.translation: By His Command, souls come into being; by His Command, glory and greatness are obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੁਕਮੀ ਉਤਮੁ ਨੀਚੁ ਹੁਕਮਿ ਲਿਖਿ ਦੁਖ ਸੁਖ ਪਾਈਅਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: hukamee utam neech hukam likh dhukh sukh paie'eeh ||
lines.translation: By His Command, some are high and some are low; by His Written Command, pain and pleasure are obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਕਨਾ ਹੁਕਮੀ ਬਖਸੀਸ ਇਕਿ ਹੁਕਮੀ ਸਦਾ ਭਵਾਈਅਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: eikanaa hukamee bakhasees ik hukamee sadhaa bhavaie'eeh ||
lines.translation: Some, by His Command, are blessed and forgiven; others, by His Command, wander aimlessly forever.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹੁਕਮੈ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਹੁਕਮ ਨ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: hukamai a(n)dhar sabh ko baahar hukam na koi ||
lines.translation: Everyone is subject to His Command; no one is beyond His Command.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਹੁਕਮੈ ਜੇ ਬੁਝੈ ਤ ਹਉਮੈ ਕਹੈ ਨ ਕੋਇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak hukamai je bujhai ta haumai kahai na koi ||2||
lines.translation: O Nanak, one who understands His Command, does not speak in ego. ||2||

structure: The shabad starts with creation itself arising under Command.
From there it shows that status, suffering, forgiveness, and wandering all remain within the same Hukam.
The closing movement rests by saying understanding Hukam leaves ego with less to say.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by placing form, life, greatness, pain, blessing, and wandering inside Hukam. It keeps widening that field until nothing stands outside the Command and ego has nowhere left to boast.
evidence.turn: From there it shows that status, suffering, forgiveness, and wandering all remain within the same Hukam.
evidence.practicalImplication: This is for anyone who is still dividing life into acceptable turns and unacceptable ones. Stayed with, it enlarges reality beyond protest and makes humility possible inside every condition. Everything stands within Hukam, and ego thins when this is seen.

title: Human birth is a chance, not an ornament
subtitle: So Purakh
summary: The shabad refuses to flatter human life; it names it as a rare opening to meet the Lord while breath is still here. It moves from opportunity to urgency, pressing the hearer toward Naam, sangat, and a life that answers the chance it was given.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person busy enough to forget that life is more than maintenance and self-arrangement. Kept near, it turns a precious life from drift into response.
takeaway: Treat this life as a meeting, not an endless postponement.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਸਾ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: aasaa mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Aasaa, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਈ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਮਾਨੁਖ ਦੇਹੁਰੀਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhiee paraapat maanukh dhehureeaa ||
lines.translation: This human body has been given to you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: gobi(n)dh milan kee ieh teree bareeaa ||
lines.translation: This is your chance to meet the Lord of the Universe.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਵਰਿ ਕਾਜ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਿਤੈ ਨ ਕਾਮ ॥
lines.transliteration: avar kaaj terai kitai na kaam ||
lines.translation: Nothing else will work.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਭਜੁ ਕੇਵਲ ਨਾਮ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: mil saadhasa(n)gat bhaj keval naam ||1||
lines.translation: Join the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy; vibrate and meditate on the Jewel of the Naam. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰੰਜਾਮਿ ਲਾਗੁ ਭਵਜਲ ਤਰਨ ਕੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: sara(n)jaam laag bhavajal taran kai ||
lines.translation: Make every effort to cross over this terrifying world-ocean.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨਮੁ ਬ੍ਰਿਥਾ ਜਾਤ ਰੰਗਿ ਮਾਇਆ ਕੈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: janam birathaa jaat ra(n)g maiaa kai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: You are squandering this life uselessly in the love of Maya. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਪੁ ਤਪੁ ਸੰਜਮੁ ਧਰਮੁ ਨ ਕਮਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: jap tap sa(n)jam dharam na kamaiaa ||
lines.translation: I have not practiced meditation, self-discipline, self-restraint or righteous living.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੇਵਾ ਸਾਧ ਨ ਜਾਨਿਆ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: sevaa saadh na jaaniaa har raiyaa ||
lines.translation: I have not served the Holy, or the Lord, my King.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਮ ਨੀਚ ਕਰੰਮਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak ham neech kara(n)maa ||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, our actions are contemptible!

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰਣਿ ਪਰੇ ਕੀ ਰਾਖਹੁ ਸਰਮਾ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: saran pare kee raakhahu saramaa ||2||
lines.translation: O Lord, I seek Your Sanctuary; please, preserve my honor! ||2||

structure: The shabad begins by calling human life a given chance rather than a private possession.
From there it refuses distraction and delay by making the purpose of life explicit.
The closing movement rests by pressing the seeker toward remembrance and company that answer the chance well.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad refuses to flatter human life; it names it as a rare opening to meet the Lord while breath is still here. It moves from opportunity to urgency, pressing the hearer toward Naam, sangat, and a life that answers the chance it was given.
evidence.turn: From there it refuses distraction and delay by making the purpose of life explicit.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person busy enough to forget that life is more than maintenance and self-arrangement. Kept near, it turns a precious life from drift into response. Treat this life as a meeting, not an endless postponement.

title: Humble company ends the fight underneath the fight
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 52
summary: The shabad begins by saying that meeting the humble defeats the messenger of death. It pushes deeper through the Lord dwelling in the mind, worldly entanglements ending, and the Guru's grace becoming ambrosial Naam.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person whose heat, fear, or defensiveness keeps masquerading as strength. Keep this shabad close when you want to fight alone, and it will remind you that the company you enter is already shaping your courage.
takeaway: Move toward the humble until fear loses its command.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ਘਰੁ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa panjavaa ghar pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, Fifth Mehla, First House:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਮਿਲਿ ਭਾਈਆ ਕਟਿਅੜਾ ਜਮਕਾਲੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t janaa mil bhaieeaa kaTiaRaa jamakaal ||
lines.translation: Meeting with the humble beings, O Siblings of Destiny, the Messenger of Death is conquered.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਮਨਿ ਵੁਠਾ ਹੋਆ ਖਸਮੁ ਦਇਆਲੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sachaa saahib man vuThaa hoaa khasam dhiaal ||
lines.translation: The True Lord and Master has come to dwell within my mind; my Lord and Master has become Merciful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰਾ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਭੇਟਿਆ ਬਿਨਸਿਆ ਸਭੁ ਜੰਜਾਲੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: pooraa satigur bheTiaa binasiaa sabh ja(n)jaal ||1||
lines.translation: Meeting with the Perfect True Guru, all my worldly entanglements have ended. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੇਰੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰਾ ਹਉ ਤੁਧੁ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕੁਰਬਾਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: mere satiguraa hau tudh viTahu kurabaan ||
lines.translation: O my True Guru, I am a sacrifice to You.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੇਰੇ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਬਲਿਹਾਰਣੈ ਤੁਸਿ ਦਿਤਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: tere dharasan kau balihaaranai tus dhitaa a(n)mirat naam ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: I am a sacrifice to the Blessed Vision of Your Darshan. By the Pleasure of Your Will, You have blessed me with the Ambrosial Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨ ਤੂੰ ਸੇਵਿਆ ਭਾਉ ਕਰਿ ਸੇਈ ਪੁਰਖ ਸੁਜਾਨ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin too(n) seviaa bhaau kar seiee purakh sujaan ||
lines.translation: Those who have served You with love are truly wise.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਨਾ ਪਿਛੈ ਛੁਟੀਐ ਜਿਨ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: tinaa pichhai chhuTeeaai jin a(n)dhar naam nidhaan ||
lines.translation: Those who have the Treasure of the Naam within emancipate others as well as themselves.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਜੇਵਡੁ ਦਾਤਾ ਕੋ ਨਹੀ ਜਿਨਿ ਦਿਤਾ ਆਤਮ ਦਾਨੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: gur jevadd dhaataa ko nahee jin dhitaa aatam dhaan ||2||
lines.translation: There is no other Giver as great as the Guru, who has given the gift of the soul. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਏ ਸੇ ਪਰਵਾਣੁ ਹਹਿ ਜਿਨ ਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਸੁਭਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: aae se paravaan heh jin gur miliaa subhai ||
lines.translation: Blessed and acclaimed is the coming of those who have met the Guru with loving faith.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੇ ਸੇਤੀ ਰਤਿਆ ਦਰਗਹ ਬੈਸਣੁ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sache setee ratiaa dharageh baisan jai ||
lines.translation: Attuned to the True One, you shall obtain a place of honor in the Court of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਤੇ ਹਥਿ ਵਡਿਆਈਆ ਪੂਰਬਿ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਪਾਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: karate hath vaddiaaieeaa poorab likhiaa pai ||3||
lines.translation: Greatness is in the Hands of the Creator; it is obtained by pre-ordained destiny. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਸਚੁ ਕਰਣਹਾਰੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਸਚੁ ਟੇਕ ॥
lines.transliteration: sach karataa sach karanahaar sach saahib sach Tek ||
lines.translation: True is the Creator, True is the Doer. True is our Lord and Master, and True is His Support.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੋ ਸਚੁ ਵਖਾਣੀਐ ਸਚੋ ਬੁਧਿ ਬਿਬੇਕ ॥
lines.transliteration: sacho sach vakhaaneeaai sacho budh bibek ||
lines.translation: So speak the Truest of the True. Through the True One, an intuitive and discerning mind is obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰਬ ਨਿਰੰਤਰਿ ਰਵਿ ਰਹਿਆ ਜਪਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਜੀਵੈ ਏਕ ॥੪॥੨੮॥੯੮॥
lines.transliteration: sarab nira(n)tar rav rahiaa jap naanak jeevai ek ||4||28||98||
lines.translation: Nanak lives by chanting and meditating on the One, who is pervading within and contained amongst all. ||4||28||98||

structure: The shabad begins by giving humble company a strength stronger than death's intimidation.
From there it lets the Lord dwell within until entanglement begins to unravel.
The closing movement rests in gratitude for the Guru whose grace turns into ambrosial Naam.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by saying that meeting the humble defeats the messenger of death. It pushes deeper through the Lord dwelling in the mind, worldly entanglements ending, and the Guru's grace becoming ambrosial Naam.
evidence.turn: From there it lets the Lord dwell within until entanglement begins to unravel.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person whose heat, fear, or defensiveness keeps masquerading as strength. Keep this shabad close when you want to fight alone, and it will remind you that the company you enter is already shaping your courage. Move toward the humble until fear loses its command.

title: Learning without inward turning stays trapped in Maya
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: The shabad begins by criticizing scholars who read and shout while remaining attached to Maya. It pushes further by exposing teaching without contemplation and ends in the waste of a life spent repeating what was never inwardly recognized.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that hides inside religious language, intellect, or correction. Taken seriously, it strips away borrowed authority and asks whether the heart has actually turned.
takeaway: Knowledge without inward freedom still serves attachment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਲੋਕ ਮਃ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: salok mahalaa teejaa ||
lines.translation: Shalok, Third Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੰਡਿਤੁ ਪੜਿ ਪੜਿ ਉਚਾ ਕੂਕਦਾ ਮਾਇਆ ਮੋਹਿ ਪਿਆਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: pa(n)ddit paR paR uchaa kookadhaa maiaa moh piaar ||
lines.translation: The Pandits, the religious scholars, read and read, and shout out loud, but they are attached to the love of Maya.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਿ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਨ ਚੀਨਈ ਮਨਿ ਮੂਰਖੁ ਗਾਵਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tar braham na cheeniee man moorakh gaavaar ||
lines.translation: They do not recognize God within themselves-they are so foolish and ignorant!

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੂਜੈ ਭਾਇ ਜਗਤੁ ਪਰਬੋਧਦਾ ਨਾ ਬੂਝੈ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhoojai bhai jagat parabodhadhaa naa boojhai beechaar ||
lines.translation: In the love of duality, they try to teach the world, but they do not understand meditative contemplation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਰਥਾ ਜਨਮੁ ਗਵਾਇਆ ਮਰਿ ਜੰਮੈ ਵਾਰੋ ਵਾਰ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: birathaa janam gavaiaa mar ja(n)mai vaaro vaar ||1||
lines.translation: They lose their lives uselessly; they die, only to be re-born, over and over again. ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by exposing scholarship still chained to Maya.
From there it shows how easily teaching the world can become another form of duality.
The closing movement rests by naming the cost: a life spent repeating what was never inwardly known.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by criticizing scholars who read and shout while remaining attached to Maya. It pushes further by exposing teaching without contemplation and ends in the waste of a life spent repeating what was never inwardly recognized.
evidence.turn: From there it shows how easily teaching the world can become another form of duality.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that hides inside religious language, intellect, or correction. Taken seriously, it strips away borrowed authority and asks whether the heart has actually turned. Knowledge without inward freedom still serves attachment.

title: Let humility become the strength that does no harm
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 272
summary: This section keeps describing the God-conscious being as dust of all, kind to all, harmful to none, impartial, and nectar-bearing. It turns humility into a presence from which no injury comes.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who has started confusing hardness with spiritual seriousness. Stay with it when you are sharp; it retrains strength as kindness strong enough to bless whatever it touches.
takeaway: Call humble the one from whom no harm comes.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸਗਲ ਕੀ ਰੀਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sagal kee reenaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is the dust of all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਤਮ ਰਸੁ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਚੀਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: aatam ras braham giaanee cheenaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being knows the nature of the soul.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੀ ਸਭ ਊਪਰਿ ਮਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kee sabh uoopar miaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being shows kindness to all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਤੇ ਕਛੁ ਬੁਰਾ ਨ ਭਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee te kachh buraa na bhiaa ||
lines.translation: No evil comes from the God-conscious being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸਦਾ ਸਮਦਰਸੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sadhaa samadharasee ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is always impartial.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੀ ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਬਰਸੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kee dhirasaT a(n)mrit barasee ||
lines.translation: Nectar rains down from the glance of the God-conscious being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਬੰਧਨ ਤੇ ਮੁਕਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee ba(n)dhan te mukataa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is free from entanglements.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੀ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਜੁਗਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kee niramal jugataa ||
lines.translation: The lifestyle of the God-conscious being is spotlessly pure.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਭੋਜਨੁ ਗਿਆਨ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kaa bhojan giaan ||
lines.translation: Spiritual wisdom is the food of the God-conscious being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਧਿਆਨੁ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee kaa braham dhiaan ||3||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the God-conscious being is absorbed in God's meditation. ||3||

structure: The shabad starts with radical lowliness rather than spiritual self-importance.
From there it names kindness, impartiality, and harmlessness as marks of God-consciousness.
The closing movement rests by showing that such presence nourishes others like falling nectar.

evidence.coreClaim: This section keeps describing the God-conscious being as dust of all, kind to all, harmful to none, impartial, and nectar-bearing. It turns humility into a presence from which no injury comes.
evidence.turn: From there it names kindness, impartiality, and harmlessness as marks of God-consciousness.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person who has started confusing hardness with spiritual seriousness. Stay with it when you are sharp; it retrains strength as kindness strong enough to bless whatever it touches. Call humble the one from whom no harm comes.

title: Let the Name become your family
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 273
summary: This section opens by describing the God-conscious being as one who loves the One alone and lives in that nearness. It keeps narrowing support down to Naam, until even family, wakefulness, and permanence are redefined by it.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that is impressionable rootless, or easily claimed by whatever is nearest. Stayed with, it teaches a form of belonging that ego cannot counterfeit.
takeaway: Take the Name as support, family, and lasting nearness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਏਕੈ ਰੰਗ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai ekai ra(n)g ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being loves the One Lord alone.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਬਸੈ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਸੰਗ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai basai prabh sa(n)g ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being dwells with God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਨਾਮੁ ਆਧਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai naam aadhaar ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being takes the Naam as his Support.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਨਾਮੁ ਪਰਵਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai naam paravaar ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being has the Naam as his Family.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸਦਾ ਸਦ ਜਾਗਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sadhaa sadh jaagat ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being is awake and aware, forever and ever.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਅਹੰਬੁਧਿ ਤਿਆਗਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee aha(n)budh tiaagat ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being renounces his proud ego.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਮਨਿ ਪਰਮਾਨੰਦ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai man paramaana(n)dh ||
lines.translation: In the mind of the God-conscious being, there is supreme bliss.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਘਰਿ ਸਦਾ ਅਨੰਦ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai ghar sadhaa ana(n)dh ||
lines.translation: In the home of the God-conscious being, there is everlasting bliss.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਸੁਖ ਸਹਜ ਨਿਵਾਸ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee sukh sahaj nivaas ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being dwells in peaceful ease.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕਾ ਨਹੀ ਬਿਨਾਸ ॥੫॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee kaa nahee binaas ||5||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the God-conscious being shall never perish. ||5||

structure: The shabad starts with singular love rather than divided loyalty.
From there it turns support and family into what is received through Naam.
The closing movement rests by pairing wakefulness and the renunciation of pride with a life that does not perish.

evidence.coreClaim: This section opens by describing the God-conscious being as one who loves the One alone and lives in that nearness. It keeps narrowing support down to Naam, until even family, wakefulness, and permanence are redefined by it.
evidence.turn: From there it turns support and family into what is received through Naam.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that is impressionable rootless, or easily claimed by whatever is nearest. Stayed with, it teaches a form of belonging that ego cannot counterfeit. Take the Name as support, family, and lasting nearness.

title: The humble are kept close
subtitle: Raag Raamkalee · Ang 882
summary: The shabad opens with the Guru as great giver, planting the Lord within the heart. It carries the listener through hearing the Guru's teaching, exposing lesser cravings, and ends with the Lord holding His humble servant close like a cherished child.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose sense of worth keeps depending on attention, beauty, or riches. Stayed with gently, it turns worth into something received from being held near the Lord.
takeaway: Stay humble enough to be kept close and cherished by the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮਕਲੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੪ ॥
lines.transliteration: raamakalee mahalaa chauthhaa ||
lines.translation: Raamkalee, Fourth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਦਾਤਾ ਵਡਾ ਵਡ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਹੈ ਜਿਤੁ ਮਿਲਿਐ ਹਰਿ ਉਰ ਧਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: satagur dhaataa vaddaa vadd purakh hai jit miliaai har ur dhaare ||
lines.translation: The True Guru, the Great Giver, is the Great, Primal Being; meeting Him, the Lord is enshrined within the heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਅ ਦਾਨੁ ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਦੀਆ ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਮਾਰੇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: jeea dhaan gur poorai dheeaa har a(n)mirat naam samaare ||1||
lines.translation: The Perfect Guru has granted me the life of the soul; I meditate in remembrance on the Ambrosial Name of the Lord. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮ ਗੁਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੰਠਿ ਧਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: raam gur har har naam ka(n)Th dhaare ||
lines.translation: O Lord, the Guru has implanted the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, within my heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਕਥਾ ਸੁਣੀ ਮਨਿ ਭਾਈ ਧਨੁ ਧਨੁ ਵਡ ਭਾਗ ਹਮਾਰੇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh kathaa sunee man bhaiee dhan dhan vadd bhaag hamaare ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: As Gurmukh, I have heard His sermon, which pleases my mind; blessed, blessed is my great destiny. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੋਟਿ ਕੋਟਿ ਤੇਤੀਸ ਧਿਆਵਹਿ ਤਾ ਕਾ ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਪਾਵਹਿ ਪਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: koT koT tetees dhiaaveh taa kaa a(n)t na paaveh paare ||
lines.translation: Millions, three hundred thirty millions of gods meditate on Him, but they cannot find His end or limitation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਿਰਦੈ ਕਾਮ ਕਾਮਨੀ ਮਾਗਹਿ ਰਿਧਿ ਮਾਗਹਿ ਹਾਥੁ ਪਸਾਰੇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: hiradhai kaam kaamanee maageh ridh maageh haath pasaare ||2||
lines.translation: With sexual urges in their hearts, they beg for beautiful women; stretching out their hands, they beg for riches. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਜਪਿ ਜਪੁ ਵਡਾ ਵਡੇਰਾ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਰਖਉ ਉਰਿ ਧਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: har jas jap jap vaddaa vadderaa gurmukh rakhau ur dhaare ||
lines.translation: One who chants the Praises of the Lord is the greatest of the great; the Gurmukh keeps the Lord clasped to his heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੇ ਵਡ ਭਾਗ ਹੋਵਹਿ ਤਾ ਜਪੀਐ ਹਰਿ ਭਉਜਲੁ ਪਾਰਿ ਉਤਾਰੇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: je vadd bhaag hoveh taa japeeaai har bhaujal paar utaare ||3||
lines.translation: If one is blessed with high destiny, he meditates on the Lord, who carries him across the terrifying world-ocean. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਜਨ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਨ ਹੈ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੰਠਿ ਜਨ ਧਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: har jan nikaT nikaT har jan hai har raakhai ka(n)Th jan dhaare ||
lines.translation: The Lord is close to His humble servant, and His humble servant is close to the Lord; He keeps His humble servant clasped to His Heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਪਿਤਾ ਮਾਤਾ ਹੈ ਹਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਹਮ ਬਾਰਿਕ ਹਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਰੇ ॥੪॥੬॥੧੮॥
lines.transliteration: naanak pitaa maataa hai har prabh ham baarik har pratipaare ||4||6||18||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the Lord God is our father and mother. I am His child; the Lord cherishes me. ||4||6||18||

structure: The shabad begins by making the Guru the giver of inward life and remembrance.
From there it contrasts that gift with the restless begging of desire and wealth.
The closing movement rests with the Lord as father and mother, keeping the humble servant close.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens with the Guru as great giver, planting the Lord within the heart. It carries the listener through hearing the Guru's teaching, exposing lesser cravings, and ends with the Lord holding His humble servant close like a cherished child.
evidence.turn: From there it contrasts that gift with the restless begging of desire and wealth.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whose sense of worth keeps depending on attention, beauty, or riches. Stayed with gently, it turns worth into something received from being held near the Lord. Stay humble enough to be kept close and cherished by the Lord.

title: Love fills the minds and bodies of the devoted
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: The shabad begins with love rising inside the mind and body as a real hunger for darshan and holy company. It asks for one mercy only, the grace to chant Naam, and ends by widening the heart into the Lord's presence everywhere.
whyItMatters: This one speaks to the person who feels unworthy, guarded, or tired of being hard on themselves. Kept close, it makes yearning honest again and shows that mercy often arrives through saintly company and the simple grace to remember.
takeaway: Ask for the grace to remember, and let love soften the guarded heart.
