lines.translation: My troubles, conflicts, fears, doubts and pains have been dispelled;

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਸਮਰਾਥਾ ॥੮॥੯॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak meraa gur samaraathaa ||8||9||
lines.translation: says Nanak, my Guru is All-powerful. ||8||9||

structure: The shabad makes remembrance intimate: the Guru is named with every breath.
From there it shows service and humility washing old ego and teaching the way of the One.
It finally lands in rescue, friendship, love, and the confidence that the Guru is powerful enough to hold you.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins with breath-by-breath remembrance of the Guru as life and wealth. It moves through service, the washing of ego, rescue from inner fire, and finally rests in the certainty that the Guru is powerful enough to carry the soul.
evidence.turn: From there it shows service and humility washing old ego and teaching the way of the One.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who feels restless, isolated, or afraid that faith will collapse under pressure. Kept close, it turns remembrance from duty into lifeline, and lets gratitude steady what fear keeps shaking. Keep returning to the Guru as breath, wealth, and shelter.

title: Remember together, not in isolation
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 17
summary: The shabad begins by calling spiritual companions close and asking them to speak of the Lord together. It carries the listener through humility, sweet speech, and the Guru's Shabad, then ends with the True King drawing the heart into Himself.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose remembrance has gone flat in private heaviness. Held warmly, it turns companionship into a place where gratitude, virtue, and shared remembrance can breathe again.
takeaway: Holy company teaches the heart how to remember well.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਵਹੁ ਭੈਣੇ ਗਲਿ ਮਿਲਹ ਅੰਕਿ ਸਹੇਲੜੀਆਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: aavahu bhaine gal mileh a(n)k sahelaReeaaeh ||
lines.translation: Come, my dear sisters and spiritual companions; hug me close in your embrace.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਲਿ ਕੈ ਕਰਹ ਕਹਾਣੀਆ ਸੰਮ੍ਰਥ ਕੰਤ ਕੀਆਹ ॥
lines.transliteration: mil kai kareh kahaaneeaa sa(n)mrath ka(n)t keeaaeh ||
lines.translation: Let's join together, and tell stories of our All-powerful Husband Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਚੇ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਸਭਿ ਗੁਣ ਅਉਗਣ ਸਭਿ ਅਸਾਹ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: saache saahib sabh gun aaugan sabh asaeh ||1||
lines.translation: All Virtues are in our True Lord and Master; we are utterly without virtue. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਤਾ ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਤੇਰੈ ਜੋਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: karataa sabh ko terai jor ||
lines.translation: O Creator Lord, all are in Your Power.

lines.gurmukhi: ਏਕੁ ਸਬਦੁ ਬੀਚਾਰੀਐ ਜਾ ਤੂ ਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਹੋਰਿ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: ek sabadh beechaareeaai jaa too taa kiaa hor ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: I dwell upon the One Word of the Shabad. You are mine-what else do I need? ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾਇ ਪੁਛਹੁ ਸੋਹਾਗਣੀ ਤੁਸੀ ਰਾਵਿਆ ਕਿਨੀ ਗੁਣਂੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: jai puchhahu sohaaganee tusee raaviaa kinee guna(n)ee ||
lines.translation: Go, and ask the happy soul-brides, ""By what virtuous qualities do you enjoy your Husband Lord?""

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਹਜਿ ਸੰਤੋਖਿ ਸੀਗਾਰੀਆ ਮਿਠਾ ਬੋਲਣੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: sahaj sa(n)tokh seegaareeaa miThaa bolanee ||
lines.translation: "We are adorned with intuitive ease, contentment and sweet words.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਿਰੁ ਰੀਸਾਲੂ ਤਾ ਮਿਲੈ ਜਾ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਸੁਣੀ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: pir reesaaloo taa milai jaa gur kaa sabadh sunee ||2||
lines.translation: We meet with our Beloved, the Source of Joy, when we listen to the Word of the Guru's Shabad.""||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੇਤੀਆ ਤੇਰੀਆ ਕੁਦਰਤੀ ਕੇਵਡ ਤੇਰੀ ਦਾਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: keteeaa tereeaa kudharatee kevadd teree dhaat ||
lines.translation: You have so many Creative Powers, Lord; Your Bountiful Blessings are so Great.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੇਤੇ ਤੇਰੇ ਜੀਅ ਜੰਤ ਸਿਫਤਿ ਕਰਹਿ ਦਿਨੁ ਰਾਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: kete tere jeea ja(n)t sifat kareh dhin raat ||
lines.translation: So many of Your beings and creatures praise You day and night.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੇਤੇ ਤੇਰੇ ਰੂਪ ਰੰਗ ਕੇਤੇ ਜਾਤਿ ਅਜਾਤਿ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: kete tere roop ra(n)g kete jaat ajaat ||3||
lines.translation: You have so many forms and colors, so many classes, high and low. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਸਚੁ ਊਪਜੈ ਸਚ ਮਹਿ ਸਾਚਿ ਸਮਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: sach milai sach uoopajai sach meh saach samai ||
lines.translation: Meeting the True One, Truth wells up. The truthful are absorbed into the True Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਰਤਿ ਹੋਵੈ ਪਤਿ ਊਗਵੈ ਗੁਰਬਚਨੀ ਭਉ ਖਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: surat hovai pat uoogavai gurbachanee bhau khai ||
lines.translation: Intuitive understanding is obtained and one is welcomed with honor, through the Guru's Word, filled with the Fear of God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚਾ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੁ ਆਪੇ ਲਏ ਮਿਲਾਇ ॥੪॥੧੦॥
lines.transliteration: naanak sachaa paatisaahu aape le milai ||4||10||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the True King absorbs us into Himself. ||4||10||

structure: The shabad opens in embrace and shared storytelling rather than private striving.
From there it learns from the happy soul-brides that ease, contentment, and sweet speech prepare true meeting.
The closing movement rests in the True King's power to absorb the truthful into Himself.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by calling spiritual companions close and asking them to speak of the Lord together. It carries the listener through humility, sweet speech, and the Guru's Shabad, then ends with the True King drawing the heart into Himself.
evidence.turn: From there it learns from the happy soul-brides that ease, contentment, and sweet speech prepare true meeting.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whose remembrance has gone flat in private heaviness. Held warmly, it turns companionship into a place where gratitude, virtue, and shared remembrance can breathe again. Holy company teaches the heart how to remember well.

title: Remembrance settles the body
subtitle: Raag Gauree
summary: The piece opens with remembrance repeated until peace reaches the body and anguish begins to loosen. It broadens into praise of the One Word behind scripture and ends by longing for the company of those who truly yearn for Darshan.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone whose worry has moved into the chest, gut, and shoulders. Kept near, it gives simran a bodily honesty instead of leaving it as decorative language.
takeaway: Carry remembrance into the body before worry settles there.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਸਟਪਦੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: asaTapadhee ||
lines.translation: Ashtapadee:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਮਰਉ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: simarau simar simar sukh paavau ||
lines.translation: Meditate, meditate, meditate in remembrance of Him, and find peace.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਲਿ ਕਲੇਸ ਤਨ ਮਾਹਿ ਮਿਟਾਵਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: kal kales tan maeh miTaavau ||
lines.translation: Worry and anguish shall be dispelled from your body.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਮਰਉ ਜਾਸੁ ਬਿਸੁੰਭਰ ਏਕੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: simarau jaas bisu(n)bhar ekai ||
lines.translation: Remember in praise the One who pervades the whole Universe.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਤ ਅਗਨਤ ਅਨੇਕੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: naam japat aganat anekai ||
lines.translation: His Name is chanted by countless people, in so many ways.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬੇਦ ਪੁਰਾਨ ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਸੁਧਾਖੵਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: bedh puraan si(n)mirat sudhaakhayer ||
lines.translation: The Vedas, the Puraanas and the Simritees, the purest of utterances,

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੀਨੇ ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮ ਇਕ ਆਖੵਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: keene raam naam ik aakhayer ||
lines.translation: were created from the One Word of the Name of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਨਕਾ ਏਕ ਜਿਸੁ ਜੀਅ ਬਸਾਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: kinakaa ek jis jeea basaavai ||
lines.translation: That one, in whose soul the One Lord dwells

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕੀ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਗਨੀ ਨ ਆਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: taa kee mahimaa ganee na aavai ||
lines.translation: the praises of his glory cannot be recounted.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਾਂਖੀ ਏਕੈ ਦਰਸ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ॥
lines.transliteration: kaa(n)khee ekai dharas tuhaaro ||
lines.translation: Those who yearn only for the blessing of Your Darshan

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਉਨ ਸੰਗਿ ਮੋਹਿ ਉਧਾਰੋ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak un sa(n)g moh udhaaro ||1||
lines.translation: Nanak: save me along with them! ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by linking repeated remembrance directly to peace and the easing of anguish in the body.
From there it magnifies the Name by placing scripture and glory beneath the One Word of the Lord.
The closing movement rests with longing for the company of those whose hearts want only His Darshan.

evidence.coreClaim: The piece opens with remembrance repeated until peace reaches the body and anguish begins to loosen. It broadens into praise of the One Word behind scripture and ends by longing for the company of those who truly yearn for Darshan.
evidence.turn: From there it magnifies the Name by placing scripture and glory beneath the One Word of the Lord.
evidence.practicalImplication: This is for anyone whose worry has moved into the chest, gut, and shoulders. Kept near, it gives simran a bodily honesty instead of leaving it as decorative language. Carry remembrance into the body before worry settles there.

title: Restlessness reveals what the heart still loves
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 170
summary: The shabad begins with a mind that will not stay still for an instant. It turns through the Guru's gift of Naam and quiet, then exposes false aims in hearts lacking love for the Lord.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person mistaking movement for aliveness. Taken seriously, it shows restlessness as a love problem before it is merely an attention problem.
takeaway: Love for the Lord gathers what distraction keeps scattering.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਪੂਰਬੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੪ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee poorabee mahalaa chauthhaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree Poorbee, Fourth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਹੁ ਮਨੂਆ ਖਿਨੁ ਨ ਟਿਕੈ ਬਹੁ ਰੰਗੀ ਦਹ ਦਹ ਦਿਸਿ ਚਲਿ ਚਲਿ ਹਾਢੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: eih manooaa khin na Tikai bahu ra(n)gee dheh dheh dhis chal chal haadde ||
lines.translation: This mind does not hold still, even for an instant. Distracted by all sorts of distractions, it wanders around aimlessly in the ten directions.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਪਾਇਆ ਵਡਭਾਗੀ ਹਰਿ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੁ ਦੀਆ ਮਨੁ ਠਾਢੇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: gur pooraa paiaa vaddabhaagee har ma(n)tr dheeaa man Thaadde ||1||
lines.translation: I have found the Perfect Guru, through great good fortune; He has given me the Mantra of the Lord's Name, and my mind has become quiet and tranquil. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮ ਹਮ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਲਾਲੇ ਕਾਂਢੇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: raam ham satigur laale kaa(n)dde ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: O Lord, I am the slave of the True Guru. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮਰੈ ਮਸਤਕਿ ਦਾਗੁ ਦਗਾਨਾ ਹਮ ਕਰਜ ਗੁਰੂ ਬਹੁ ਸਾਢੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: hamarai masatak dhaag dhagaanaa ham karaj guroo bahu saadde ||
lines.translation: My forehead has been branded with His brand; I owe such a great debt to the Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਰਉਪਕਾਰੁ ਪੁੰਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਕੀਆ ਭਉ ਦੁਤਰੁ ਤਾਰਿ ਪਰਾਢੇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: paraupakaar pu(n)n bahu keeaa bhau dhutar taar paraadde ||2||
lines.translation: He has been so generous and kind to me; He has carried me across the treacherous and terrifying world-ocean. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰਿਦੈ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਹੀ ਤਿਨ ਕੂਰੇ ਗਾਢਨ ਗਾਢੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin kau preet ridhai har naahee tin koore gaaddan gaadde ||
lines.translation: Those who do not have love for the Lord within their hearts, harbor only false intentions and goals.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਉ ਪਾਣੀ ਕਾਗਦੁ ਬਿਨਸਿ ਜਾਤ ਹੈ ਤਿਉ ਮਨਮੁਖ ਗਰਭਿ ਗਲਾਢੇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: jiau paanee kaagadh binas jaat hai tiau manmukh garabh galaadde ||3||
lines.translation: As paper breaks down and dissolves in water, the self-willed manmukh wastes away in arrogant pride. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮ ਜਾਨਿਆ ਕਛੂ ਨ ਜਾਨਹ ਆਗੈ ਜਿਉ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਖੈ ਤਿਉ ਠਾਢੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ham jaaniaa kachhoo na jaaneh aagai jiau har raakhai tiau Thaadde ||
lines.translation: I know nothing, and I do not know the future; as the Lord keeps me, so do I stand.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮ ਭੂਲ ਚੂਕ ਗੁਰ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਕੁਤਰੇ ਕਾਢੇ ॥੪॥੭॥੨੧॥੫੯॥
lines.transliteration: ham bhool chook gur kirapaa dhaarahu jan naanak kutare kaadde ||4||7||21||59||
lines.translation: For my failings and mistakes, O Guru, grant me Your Grace; servant Nanak is Your obedient dog. ||4||7||21||59||

structure: The shabad starts with the mind wandering in ten directions and unable to settle.
From there it receives Naam and quiet from the Guru instead of trying to manufacture calm.
The closing movement rests by exposing false goals as the fruit of a heart still lacking love for the Lord.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins with a mind that will not stay still for an instant. It turns through the Guru's gift of Naam and quiet, then exposes false aims in hearts lacking love for the Lord.
evidence.turn: From there it receives Naam and quiet from the Guru instead of trying to manufacture calm.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person mistaking movement for aliveness. Taken seriously, it shows restlessness as a love problem before it is merely an attention problem. Love for the Lord gathers what distraction keeps scattering.

title: Sanctuary for a mind under assault
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 205
summary: The shabad opens with a direct cry to the Father God for rescue. It carries the listener through the five thieves attacking the being, the sanctuary of the Saadh Sangat, and ends when divine light dawns in the mind.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who is already afraid and no longer able to pretend control. Kept sincere, it gives fear a cleaner movement than panic: cry out, take shelter, and wait for light.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: call for shelter before fear becomes your only voice.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਖੁ ਪਿਤਾ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮੇਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: raakh pitaa prabh mere ||
lines.translation: Save me, O My Father God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੋਹਿ ਨਿਰਗੁਨੁ ਸਭ ਗੁਨ ਤੇਰੇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: moh niragun sabh gun tere ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: I am worthless and without virtue; all virtues are Yours. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੰਚ ਬਿਖਾਦੀ ਏਕੁ ਗਰੀਬਾ ਰਾਖਹੁ ਰਾਖਨਹਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: pa(n)ch bikhaadhee ek gareebaa raakhahu raakhanahaare ||
lines.translation: The five vicious thieves are assaulting my poor being; save me, O Savior Lord!

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੇਦੁ ਕਰਹਿ ਅਰੁ ਬਹੁਤੁ ਸੰਤਾਵਹਿ ਆਇਓ ਸਰਨਿ ਤੁਹਾਰੇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: khedh kareh ar bahut sa(n)taaveh aaio saran tuhaare ||1||
lines.translation: They are tormenting and torturing me. I have come, seeking Your Sanctuary. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਕਰਿ ਹਾਰਿਓ ਅਨਿਕ ਬਹੁ ਭਾਤੀ ਛੋਡਹਿ ਕਤਹੂੰ ਨਾਹੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar kar haario anik bahu bhaatee chhoddeh katahoo(n) naahee ||
lines.translation: Trying all sorts of things, I have grown weary, but still, they will not leave me alone.

lines.gurmukhi: ਏਕ ਬਾਤ ਸੁਨਿ ਤਾਕੀ ਓਟਾ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਿਟਿ ਜਾਹੀ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: ek baat sun taakee oTaa saadhasa(n)g miT jaahee ||2||
lines.translation: But I have heard that they can be rooted out, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy; and so I seek their Shelter. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਸੰਤ ਮਿਲੇ ਮੋਹਿ ਤਿਨ ਤੇ ਧੀਰਜੁ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar kirapaa sa(n)t mile moh tin te dheeraj paiaa ||
lines.translation: In their Mercy, the Saints have met me, and from them, I have obtained satisfaction.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤੀ ਮੰਤੁ ਦੀਓ ਮੋਹਿ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਕਮਾਇਆ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)tee ma(n)t dheeo moh nirabhau gur kaa sabadh kamaiaa ||3||
lines.translation: The Saints have given me the Mantra of the Fearless Lord, and now I practice the Word of the Guru's Shabad. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਤਿ ਲਏ ਓਇ ਮਹਾ ਬਿਖਾਦੀ ਸਹਜ ਸੁਹੇਲੀ ਬਾਣੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeet le oi mahaa bikhaadhee sahaj suhelee baanee ||
lines.translation: I have now conquered those terrible evil-doers, and my speech is now sweet and sublime.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਮਨਿ ਭਇਆ ਪਰਗਾਸਾ ਪਾਇਆ ਪਦੁ ਨਿਰਬਾਣੀ ॥੪॥੪॥੧੨੫॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak man bhiaa paragaasaa paiaa padh nirabaanee ||4||4||125||
lines.translation: Says Nanak, the Divine Light has dawned within my mind; I have obtained the state of Nirvaanaa. ||4||4||125||

structure: The shabad opens without bravado, asking the Father directly for rescue.
From there it names the assault honestly and turns toward sanctuary rather than self-sufficiency.
The closing movement rests with the mind lit from within after company, grace, and shelter have done their work.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens with a direct cry to the Father God for rescue. It carries the listener through the five thieves attacking the being, the sanctuary of the Saadh Sangat, and ends when divine light dawns in the mind.
evidence.turn: From there it names the assault honestly and turns toward sanctuary rather than self-sufficiency.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who is already afraid and no longer able to pretend control. Kept sincere, it gives fear a cleaner movement than panic: cry out, take shelter, and wait for light. Keep this in front of you: call for shelter before fear becomes your only voice.

title: Roaming ends where holy company cools the heart
subtitle: Raag Maajh · Ang 98
summary: The shabad opens in relentless searching through forests, philosophies, rituals, and yogic techniques. It turns only when mercy brings true company, and then the mind and body finally cool.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person trapped in spiritual roaming, method-switching, and never-arriving effort. Taken seriously, it says peace is not found by multiplying techniques but by mercy and true company.
takeaway: Bring your searching to holy company and let it cool there.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਾਝ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: maajh mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Maajh, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਖੋਜਤ ਖੋਜਤ ਦਰਸਨ ਚਾਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: khojat khojat dharasan chaahe ||
lines.translation: I have searched and searched, seeking the Blessed Vision of His Darshan.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਾਤਿ ਭਾਤਿ ਬਨ ਬਨ ਅਵਗਾਹੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhaat bhaat ban ban avagaahe ||
lines.translation: I travelled through all sorts of woods and forests.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਰਗੁਣੁ ਸਰਗੁਣੁ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਮੇਰਾ ਕੋਈ ਹੈ ਜੀਉ ਆਣਿ ਮਿਲਾਵੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: niragun saragun har har meraa koiee hai jeeau aan milaavai jeeau ||1||
lines.translation: My Lord, Har, Har, is both absolute and related, unmanifest and manifest; is there anyone who can come and unite me with Him? ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਖਟੁ ਸਾਸਤ ਬਿਚਰਤ ਮੁਖਿ ਗਿਆਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: khaT saasat bicharat mukh giaanaa ||
lines.translation: People recite from memory the wisdom of the six schools of philosophy;

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਜਾ ਤਿਲਕੁ ਤੀਰਥ ਇਸਨਾਨਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: poojaa tilak teerath isanaanaa ||
lines.translation: they perform worship services, wear ceremonial religious marks on their foreheads, and take ritual cleansing baths at sacred shrines of pilgrimage.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਵਲੀ ਕਰਮ ਆਸਨ ਚਉਰਾਸੀਹ ਇਨ ਮਹਿ ਸਾਂਤਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: nivalee karam aasan chauraaseeh in meh saa(n)t na aavai jeeau ||2||
lines.translation: They perform the inner cleansing practice with water and adopt the eighty-four Yogic postures; but still, they find no peace in any of these. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਿਕ ਬਰਖ ਕੀਏ ਜਪ ਤਾਪਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: anik barakh ke'ee jap taapaa ||
lines.translation: They chant and meditate, practicing austere self-discipline for years and years;

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਵਨੁ ਕੀਆ ਧਰਤੀ ਭਰਮਾਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: gavan keeaa dharatee bharamaataa ||
lines.translation: they wander on journeys all over the earth;

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਕੁ ਖਿਨੁ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਸਾਂਤਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਜੋਗੀ ਬਹੁੜਿ ਬਹੁੜਿ ਉਠਿ ਧਾਵੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: eik khin hiradhai saa(n)t na aavai jogee bahuR bahuR uTh dhaavai jeeau ||3||
lines.translation: and yet, their hearts are not at peace, even for an instant. The Yogi rises up and goes out, over and over again. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਮੋਹਿ ਸਾਧੁ ਮਿਲਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar kirapaa moh saadh milaiaa ||
lines.translation: By His Mercy, I have met the Holy Saint.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਸੀਤਲੁ ਧੀਰਜੁ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: man tan seetal dheeraj paiaa ||
lines.translation: My mind and body have been cooled and soothed; I have been blessed with patience and composure.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ ਬਸਿਆ ਘਟ ਭੀਤਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਮੰਗਲੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਗਾਵੈ ਜੀਉ ॥੪॥੫॥੧੨॥
lines.transliteration: prabh abinaasee basiaa ghaT bheetar har ma(n)gal naanak gaavai jeeau ||4||5||12||
lines.translation: The Immortal Lord God has come to dwell within my heart. Nanak sings the songs of joy to the Lord. ||4||5||12||

structure: The shabad starts with a sincere search that still cannot bring the Lord near.
From there it exhausts religious systems and bodily disciplines until their inability to give peace is obvious.
The closing movement rests in mercy, holy company, and the Lord dwelling within a cooled heart.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens in relentless searching through forests, philosophies, rituals, and yogic techniques. It turns only when mercy brings true company, and then the mind and body finally cool.
evidence.turn: From there it exhausts religious systems and bodily disciplines until their inability to give peace is obvious.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person trapped in spiritual roaming, method-switching, and never-arriving effort. Taken seriously, it says peace is not found by multiplying techniques but by mercy and true company. Bring your searching to holy company and let it cool there.

title: Service without reward reaches the Master
subtitle: Raag Gauree
summary: The shabad starts by defining the servant who lives in the Guru's household — obedient, unadvertised, and absorbed in Naam. It comes to a sharp center where selfless service without reward reaches the Lord Himself.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person doing good while keeping one eye on recognition. Lived with faithfully, it purifies service by taking self-display and reward out of the center.
takeaway: Service becomes true when the self stops asking to be seen.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਸੇਵਕੁ ਜੋ ਰਹੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai gireh sevak jo rahai ||
lines.translation: That selfless servant, who lives in the Guru's household,

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਆਗਿਆ ਮਨ ਮਹਿ ਸਹੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kee aagiaa man meh sahai ||
lines.translation: is to obey the Guru's Commands with all his mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਸ ਕਉ ਕਰਿ ਕਛੁ ਨ ਜਨਾਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: aapas kau kar kachh na janaavai ||
lines.translation: He is not to call attention to himself in any way.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਿਦੈ ਸਦ ਧਿਆਵੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: har har naam ridhai sadh dhiaavai ||
lines.translation: He is to meditate constantly within his heart on the Name of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਬੇਚੈ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਪਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: man bechai satigur kai paas ||
lines.translation: One who sells his mind to the True Guru

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਸੁ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੇ ਕਾਰਜ ਰਾਸਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: tis sevak ke kaaraj raas ||
lines.translation: that humble servant's affairs are resolved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੇਵਾ ਕਰਤ ਹੋਇ ਨਿਹਕਾਮੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: sevaa karat hoi nihakaamee ||
lines.translation: One who performs selfless service, without thought of reward,

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਸ ਕਉ ਹੋਤ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਸੁਆਮੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: tis kau hot paraapat suaamee ||
lines.translation: shall attain his Lord and Master.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਪੁਨੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਜਿਸੁ ਆਪਿ ਕਰੇਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: apunee kirapaa jis aap karei ||
lines.translation: One whom the Lord Himself blesses with His Grace

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਸੋ ਸੇਵਕੁ ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਮਤਿ ਲੇਇ ॥੪॥੫॥
lines.transliteration: naanak so sevak gur kee mat lei ||4||5||
lines.translation: O Nanak, is the selfless servant who lives the Guru's wisdom. ||4||5||

structure: The shabad begins by describing the servant who lives under the Guru's command rather than personal image.
From there it sells the mind to the Guru and lets affairs be resolved there instead of in self-importance.
The closing movement rests with selfless service drawing the servant into the Lord and the Guru's teaching.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad starts by defining the servant who lives in the Guru's household — obedient, unadvertised, and absorbed in Naam. It comes to a sharp center where selfless service without reward reaches the Lord Himself.
evidence.turn: From there it sells the mind to the Guru and lets affairs be resolved there instead of in self-importance.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person doing good while keeping one eye on recognition. Lived with faithfully, it purifies service by taking self-display and reward out of the center. Service becomes true when the self stops asking to be seen.

title: Do not let speech carry filth
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 15
summary: The shabad begins by describing greed, falsehood, slander, and anger as degrading forms of speech and appetite. It then asks a harder question: what words actually bring honor at the Lord's Door?
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose hurt, sharpness, or cleverness keeps leaking out through the mouth. Stayed with honestly, it makes speech answerable to honor, not impulse.
takeaway: Keep only the speech that can stand at God's Door.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਲਬੁ ਕੁਤਾ ਕੂੜੁ ਚੂਹੜਾ ਠਗਿ ਖਾਧਾ ਮੁਰਦਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: lab kutaa kooR choohaRaa Thag khaadhaa muradhaar ||
lines.translation: Greed is a dog; falsehood is a filthy street-sweeper. Cheating is eating a rotting carcass.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਰ ਨਿੰਦਾ ਪਰ ਮਲੁ ਮੁਖ ਸੁਧੀ ਅਗਨਿ ਕ੍ਰੋਧੁ ਚੰਡਾਲੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: par ni(n)dhaa par mal mukh sudhee agan karodh cha(n)ddaal ||
lines.translation: Slandering others is putting the filth of others into your own mouth. The fire of anger is the outcaste who burns dead bodies at the crematorium.

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਸ ਕਸ ਆਪੁ ਸਲਾਹਣਾ ਏ ਕਰਮ ਮੇਰੇ ਕਰਤਾਰ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: ras kas aap salaahanaa e karam mere karataar ||1||
lines.translation: I am caught in these tastes and flavors, and in self-conceited praise. These are my actions, O my Creator! ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਾਬਾ ਬੋਲੀਐ ਪਤਿ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: baabaa boleeaai pat hoi ||
lines.translation: O Baba, speak only that which will bring you honor.

lines.gurmukhi: ਊਤਮ ਸੇ ਦਰਿ ਊਤਮ ਕਹੀਅਹਿ ਨੀਚ ਕਰਮ ਬਹਿ ਰੋਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: uootam se dhar uootam kahe'eeh neech karam beh roi ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: They alone are good, who are judged good at the Lord's Door. Those with bad karma can only sit and weep. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਸੁ ਸੁਇਨਾ ਰਸੁ ਰੁਪਾ ਕਾਮਣਿ ਰਸੁ ਪਰਮਲ ਕੀ ਵਾਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: ras suinaa ras rupaa kaaman ras paramal kee vaas ||
lines.translation: The pleasures of gold and silver, the pleasures of women, the pleasure of the fragrance of sandalwood,

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਸੁ ਘੋੜੇ ਰਸੁ ਸੇਜਾ ਮੰਦਰ ਰਸੁ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਸੁ ਮਾਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: ras ghoRe ras sejaa ma(n)dhar ras meeThaa ras maas ||
lines.translation: the pleasure of horses, the pleasure of a soft bed in a palace, the pleasure of sweet treats and the pleasure of hearty meals

lines.gurmukhi: ਏਤੇ ਰਸ ਸਰੀਰ ਕੇ ਕੈ ਘਟਿ ਨਾਮ ਨਿਵਾਸੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: ete ras sareer ke kai ghaT naam nivaas ||2||
lines.translation: -these pleasures of the human body are so numerous; how can the Naam, the Name of the Lord, find its dwelling in the heart? ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਤੁ ਬੋਲਿਐ ਪਤਿ ਪਾਈਐ ਸੋ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਪਰਵਾਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: jit boliaai pat paieeaai so boliaa paravaan ||
lines.translation: Those words are acceptable, which, when spoken, bring honor.

lines.gurmukhi: ਫਿਕਾ ਬੋਲਿ ਵਿਗੁਚਣਾ ਸੁਣਿ ਮੂਰਖ ਮਨ ਅਜਾਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: fikaa bol viguchanaa sun moorakh man ajaan ||
lines.translation: Harsh words bring only grief. Listen, O foolish and ignorant mind!

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਤਿਸੁ ਭਾਵਹਿ ਸੇ ਭਲੇ ਹੋਰਿ ਕਿ ਕਹਣ ਵਖਾਣ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: jo tis bhaaveh se bhale hor k kahan vakhaan ||3||
lines.translation: Those who are pleasing to Him are good. What else is there to be said? ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਨ ਮਤਿ ਤਿਨ ਪਤਿ ਤਿਨ ਧਨੁ ਪਲੈ ਜਿਨ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਰਹਿਆ ਸਮਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: tin mat tin pat tin dhan palai jin hiradhai rahiaa samai ||
lines.translation: Wisdom, honor and wealth are in the laps of those whose hearts remain permeated with the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਨ ਕਾ ਕਿਆ ਸਾਲਾਹਣਾ ਅਵਰ ਸੁਆਲਿਉ ਕਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: tin kaa kiaa saalaahanaa avar suaaliau kai ||
lines.translation: What praise can be offered to them? What other adornments can be bestowed upon them?

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਨਦਰੀ ਬਾਹਰੇ ਰਾਚਹਿ ਦਾਨਿ ਨ ਨਾਇ ॥੪॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: naanak nadharee baahare raacheh dhaan na nai ||4||4||
lines.translation: O Nanak, those who lack the Lord's Glance of Grace cherish neither charity nor the Lord's Name. ||4||4||

structure: The shabad begins by making moral corruption sound disgusting enough to stop glamorizing it.
From there it asks which words bring honor and exposes how bodily pleasures crowd out Naam.
The closing movement rests by approving only the speech pleasing to Him and warning that harsh words return as grief.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by describing greed, falsehood, slander, and anger as degrading forms of speech and appetite. It then asks a harder question: what words actually bring honor at the Lord's Door?
evidence.turn: From there it asks which words bring honor and exposes how bodily pleasures crowd out Naam.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whose hurt, sharpness, or cleverness keeps leaking out through the mouth. Stayed with honestly, it makes speech answerable to honor, not impulse. Keep only the speech that can stand at God's Door.

title: Why waver under a merciful Creator
subtitle: Raag Tilang
summary: The shabad begins by naming the Lord's mercy twice and grounding life in His gifts. It then asks why the mortal wavers when the One who created also nourishes, protects, and cherishes every heart.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that spirals over provision, safety, or the future. Taken steadily, it pulls the mind back under mercy and teaches trust while breath remains.
takeaway: The Creator's mercy is steadier than your wavering.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਿਲੰਗ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ਘਰੁ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: tila(n)g mahalaa panjavaa ghar teejaa ||
lines.translation: Tilang, Fifth Mehla, Third House:

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਹਰਵਾਨੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਮਿਹਰਵਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: miharavaan saahib miharavaan ||
lines.translation: Merciful, the Lord Master is Merciful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਿਹਰਵਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: saahib meraa miharavaan ||
lines.translation: My Lord Master is Merciful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਅ ਸਗਲ ਕਉ ਦੇਇ ਦਾਨੁ ॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeea sagal kau dhei dhaan || rahaau ||
lines.translation: He gives His gifts to all beings. ||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂ ਕਾਹੇ ਡੋਲਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀਆ ਤੁਧੁ ਰਾਖੈਗਾ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: too kaahe ddoleh praaneeaa tudh raakhaigaa sirajanahaar ||
lines.translation: Why do you waver, O mortal being? The Creator Lord Himself shall protect you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਪੈਦਾਇਸਿ ਤੂ ਕੀਆ ਸੋਈ ਦੇਇ ਆਧਾਰੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: jin paidhais too keeaa soiee dhei aadhaar ||1||
lines.translation: He who created you, will also give you nourishment. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਉਪਾਈ ਮੇਦਨੀ ਸੋਈ ਕਰਦਾ ਸਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin upaiee medhanee soiee karadhaa saar ||
lines.translation: The One who created the world, takes care of it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਘਟਿ ਘਟਿ ਮਾਲਕੁ ਦਿਲਾ ਕਾ ਸਚਾ ਪਰਵਦਗਾਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: ghaT ghaT maalak dhilaa kaa sachaa paravadhagaar ||2||
lines.translation: In each and every heart and mind, the Lord is the True Cherisher. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਕੀਤਾ ਤਿਸਹਿ ਨ ਜਾਨਈ ਮਨਮੁਖਿ ਪਚਿ ਮੁਏ ਗਵਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin keetaa tiseh na jaanee manamukh pach mue gavaar ||
lines.translation: The self-willed fools do not know the One who created them; they rot away and die.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਵਣ ਜਾਣਾ ਨਾ ਥੀਐ ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਦਰਬਾਰ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: aavan jaanaa na theeaai poore gur dharabaar ||3||
lines.translation: The cycle of coming and going in reincarnation is ended, in the Court of the Perfect Guru. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂ ਕਾਹੇ ਡੋਲਹਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀਆ ਵੇਪਰਵਾਹੁ ਰਖੈਗਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: too kaahe ddoleh praaneeaa veparavaahu rakhaigaa ||
lines.translation: Why do you waver, O mortal being? The Lord who needs no care will care for you.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸੁ ਚਰਨੀ ਲਾਗਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਪਰਬਤੁ ਠਹਰੈਗਾ ॥੪॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak dhaas charanee laagaa saahib parabat Thaharaiagaa ||4||1||
lines.translation: Servant Nanak falls at His Feet; the Lord and Master stands firm like a mountain. ||4||1||

structure: The shabad starts with mercy as the atmosphere of the Lord's relation to creation.
From there it asks the trembling heart why it doubts the care of the One who made it.
The closing movement rests in breath-by-breath devotion and a prayer to find peace through mercy.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by naming the Lord's mercy twice and grounding life in His gifts. It then asks why the mortal wavers when the One who created also nourishes, protects, and cherishes every heart.
evidence.turn: From there it asks the trembling heart why it doubts the care of the One who made it.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that spirals over provision, safety, or the future. Taken steadily, it pulls the mind back under mercy and teaches trust while breath remains. The Creator's mercy is steadier than your wavering.

title: Steady service begins healing long separation
subtitle: Raag Maajh · Ang 136
summary: The shabad opens with day-and-night service, remembrance, and sweet speech offered from sanctuary. It travels through the sorrow of separation, the need for mercy, and ends with the yearning to be united with the Lord through the Guru's feet.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose longing has become dramatic, weary, or spiritually dry. Taken steadily, it keeps longing honest by turning it into service, prayer, and saintly humility.
takeaway: Stay in service and remembrance until separation begins healing.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਾਝ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ਦਿਨ ਰੈਣਿ
lines.transliteration: maajh mahalaa panjavaa dhin rain
lines.translation: Maajh, Fifth Mehla: Day And Night:

lines.gurmukhi: ੴ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: ikOankaar satigur prasaadh ||
lines.translation: One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੇਵੀ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਆਪਣਾ ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰੀ ਦਿਨ ਸਭਿ ਰੈਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: sevee satigur aapanaa har simaree dhin sabh rain ||
lines.translation: I serve my True Guru, and meditate on Him all day and night.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪੁ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਸਰਣੀ ਪਵਾਂ ਮੁਖਿ ਬੋਲੀ ਮਿਠੜੇ ਵੈਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: aap tiaag saranee pavaa(n) mukh bolee miThaRe vain ||
lines.translation: Renouncing selfishness and conceit, I seek His Sanctuary, and speak sweet words to Him.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨਮ ਜਨਮ ਕਾ ਵਿਛੁੜਿਆ ਹਰਿ ਮੇਲਹੁ ਸਜਣੁ ਸੈਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: janam janam kaa vichhuRiaa har melahu sajan sain ||
lines.translation: Through countless lifetimes and incarnations, I was separated from Him. O Lord, you are my Friend and Companion-please unite me with Yourself.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਜੀਅ ਹਰਿ ਤੇ ਵਿਛੁੜੇ ਸੇ ਸੁਖਿ ਨ ਵਸਨਿ ਭੈਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo jeea har te vichhuRe se sukh na vasan bhain ||
lines.translation: Those who are separated from the Lord do not dwell in peace, O sister.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਪਿਰ ਬਿਨੁ ਚੈਨੁ ਨ ਪਾਈਐ ਖੋਜਿ ਡਿਠੇ ਸਭਿ ਗੈਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: har pir bin chain na paieeaai khoj ddiThe sabh gain ||
lines.translation: Without their Husband Lord, they find no comfort. I have searched and seen all realms.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪ ਕਮਾਣੈ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਦੋਸੁ ਨ ਕਾਹੂ ਦੇਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: aap kamaanai vichhuRee dhos na kaahoo dhen ||
lines.translation: My own evil actions have kept me separate from Him; why should I accuse anyone else?

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਰਾਖਿ ਲੇਹੁ ਹੋਰੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਕਰਣ ਕਰੇਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar kirapaa prabh raakh leh hor naahee karan karen ||
lines.translation: Bestow Your Mercy, God, and save me! No one else can bestow Your Mercy.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਤੁਧੁ ਵਿਣੁ ਖਾਕੂ ਰੂਲਣਾ ਕਹੀਐ ਕਿਥੈ ਵੈਣ ॥
lines.transliteration: har tudh vin khaakoo roolanaa kaheeaai kithai vain ||
lines.translation: Without You, Lord, we roll around in the dust. Unto whom should we utter our cries of distress?

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਕੀ ਬੇਨੰਤੀਆ ਹਰਿ ਸੁਰਜਨੁ ਦੇਖਾ ਨੈਣ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak kee bena(n)teeaa har surajan dhekhaa nain ||1||
lines.translation: This is Nanak's prayer: ""May my eyes behold the Lord, the Angelic Being.""||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਅ ਕੀ ਬਿਰਥਾ ਸੋ ਸੁਣੇ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਮ੍ਰਿਥ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਅਪਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeea kee birathaa so sune har sa(n)mrith purakh apaar ||
lines.translation: The Lord hears the anguish of the soul; He is the All-powerful and Infinite Primal Being.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਰਣਿ ਜੀਵਣਿ ਆਰਾਧਣਾ ਸਭਨਾ ਕਾ ਆਧਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: maran jeevan aaraadhanaa sabhanaa kaa aadhaar ||
lines.translation: In death and in life, worship and adore the Lord, the Support of all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਸੁਰੈ ਪੇਈਐ ਤਿਸੁ ਕੰਤ ਕੀ ਵਡਾ ਜਿਸੁ ਪਰਵਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sasurai peieeaai tis ka(n)t kee vaddaa jis paravaar ||
lines.translation: In this world and in the next, the soul-bride belongs to her Husband Lord, who has such a vast family.

lines.gurmukhi: ਊਚਾ ਅਗਮ ਅਗਾਧਿ ਬੋਧ ਕਿਛੁ ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਪਾਰਾਵਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: uoochaa agam agaadh bodh kichh a(n)t na paaraavaar ||
lines.translation: He is Lofty and Inaccessible. His Wisdom is Unfathomable.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੇਵਾ ਸਾ ਤਿਸੁ ਭਾਵਸੀ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਹੋਇ ਛਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sevaa saa tis bhaavasee sa(n)taa kee hoi chhaar ||
lines.translation: He has no end or limitation. That service is pleasing to Him, which makes one humble, like the dust of the feet of the Saints.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੀਨਾ ਨਾਥ ਦੈਆਲ ਦੇਵ ਪਤਿਤ ਉਧਾਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: dheenaa naath dhaiaal dhev patit udhaaranahaar ||
lines.translation: He is the Patron of the poor, the Merciful, Luminous Lord, the Redeemer of sinners.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਦਿ ਜੁਗਾਦੀ ਰਖਦਾ ਸਚੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਕਰਤਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: aadh jugaadhee rakhadhaa sach naam karataar ||
lines.translation: From the very beginning, and throughout the ages, the True Name of the Creator has been our Saving Grace.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੀਮਤਿ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਜਾਣਈ ਕੋ ਨਾਹੀ ਤੋਲਣਹਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: keemat koi na jaaniee ko naahee tolanahaar ||
lines.translation: No one can know His Value; no one can weigh it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਤਨ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਵਸਿ ਰਹੇ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਹੀ ਸੁਮਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: man tan a(n)tar vas rahe naanak nahee sumaar ||
lines.translation: He dwells deep within the mind and body. O Nanak, He cannot be measured.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦਿਨੁ ਰੈਣਿ ਜਿ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੰਉ ਸੇਵਦੇ ਤਿਨ ਕੈ ਸਦ ਬਲਿਹਾਰ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: dhin rain j prabh ka(n)au sevadhe tin kai sadh balihaar ||2||
lines.translation: I am forever a sacrifice to those who serve God, day and night. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਅਰਾਧਨਿ ਸਦ ਸਦਾ ਸਭਨਾ ਕਾ ਬਖਸਿੰਦੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t araadhan sadh sadhaa sabhanaa kaa bakhasi(n)dh ||
lines.translation: The Saints worship and adore Him forever and ever; He is the Forgiver of all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਉ ਪਿੰਡੁ ਜਿਨਿ ਸਾਜਿਆ ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਦਿਤੀਨੁ ਜਿੰਦੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeeau pi(n)dd jin saajiaa kar kirapaa dhiteen ji(n)dh ||
lines.translation: He fashioned the soul and the body, and by His Kindness, He bestowed the soul.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਆਰਾਧੀਐ ਜਪੀਐ ਨਿਰਮਲ ਮੰਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur sabadhee aaraadheeaai japeeaai niramal ma(n)t ||
lines.translation: Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, worship and adore Him, and chant His Pure Mantra.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕੀਮਤਿ ਕਹਣੁ ਨ ਜਾਈਐ ਪਰਮੇਸੁਰੁ ਬੇਅੰਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: keemat kahan na jaieeaai paramesur bea(n)t ||
lines.translation: His Value cannot be evaluated. The Transcendent Lord is endless.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਮਨਿ ਵਸੈ ਨਰਾਇਣੋ ਸੋ ਕਹੀਐ ਭਗਵੰਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: jis man vasai naraino so kaheeaai bhagava(n)t ||
lines.translation: That one, within whose mind the Lord abides, is said to be most fortunate.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੀਅ ਕੀ ਲੋਚਾ ਪੂਰੀਐ ਮਿਲੈ ਸੁਆਮੀ ਕੰਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeea kee lochaa pooreeaai milai suaamee ka(n)t ||
lines.translation: The soul's desires are fulfilled, upon meeting the Master, our Husband Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕੁ ਜੀਵੈ ਜਪਿ ਹਰੀ ਦੋਖ ਸਭੇ ਹੀ ਹੰਤੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak jeevai jap haree dhokh sabhe hee ha(n)t ||
lines.translation: Nanak lives by chanting the Lord's Name; all sorrows have been erased.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦਿਨੁ ਰੈਣਿ ਜਿਸੁ ਨ ਵਿਸਰੈ ਸੋ ਹਰਿਆ ਹੋਵੈ ਜੰਤੁ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: dhin rain jis na visarai so hariaa hovai ja(n)t ||3||
lines.translation: One who does not forget Him, day and night, is continually rejuvenated. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰਬ ਕਲਾ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਪੂਰਣੋ ਮੰਞੁ ਨਿਮਾਣੀ ਥਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: sarab kalaa prabh poorano ma(n)n(j) nimaanee thaau ||
lines.translation: God is overflowing with all powers. I have no honor-He is my resting place.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਓਟ ਗਹੀ ਮਨ ਅੰਦਰੇ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਨਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: har oT gahee man a(n)dhare jap jap jeevaa(n) naau ||
lines.translation: I have grasped the Support of the Lord within my mind; I live by chanting and meditating on His Name.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਪਣੀ ਜਨ ਧੂੜੀ ਸੰਗਿ ਸਮਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: kar kirapaa prabh aapanee jan dhooRee sa(n)g samaau ||
lines.translation: Grant Your Grace, God, and bless me, that I may merge into the dust of the feet of the humble.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਉ ਤੂੰ ਰਾਖਹਿ ਤਿਉ ਰਹਾ ਤੇਰਾ ਦਿਤਾ ਪੈਨਾ ਖਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: jiau too(n) raakheh tiau rahaa teraa dhitaa painaa khaau ||
lines.translation: As You keep me, so do I live. I wear and eat whatever You give me.

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਦਮੁ ਸੋਈ ਕਰਾਇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਿ ਸਾਧੂ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: audham soiee karai prabh mil saadhoo gun gaau ||
lines.translation: May I make the effort, O God, to sing Your Glorious Praises in the Company of the Holy.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੂਜੀ ਜਾਇ ਨ ਸੁਝਈ ਕਿਥੈ ਕੂਕਣ ਜਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhoojee jai na sujhiee kithai kookan jaau ||
lines.translation: I can conceive of no other place; where could I go to lodge a complaint?

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਗਿਆਨ ਬਿਨਾਸਨ ਤਮ ਹਰਣ ਊਚੇ ਅਗਮ ਅਮਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: agiaan binaasan tam haran uooche agam amaau ||
lines.translation: You are the Dispeller of ignorance, the Destroyer of darkness, O Lofty, Unfathomable and Unapproachable Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਵਿਛੁੜਿਆ ਹਰਿ ਮੇਲੀਐ ਨਾਨਕ ਏਹੁ ਸੁਆਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: man vichhuRiaa har meleeaai naanak eh suaau ||
lines.translation: Please unite this separated one with Yourself; this is Nanak's yearning.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰਬ ਕਲਿਆਣਾ ਤਿਤੁ ਦਿਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਪਰਸੀ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਪਾਉ ॥੪॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: sarab kaliaanaa tit dhin har parasee gur ke paau ||4||1||
lines.translation: That day shall bring every joy, O Lord, when I take to the Feet of the Guru. ||4||1||

structure: The shabad starts with service and remembrance as the form longing takes when it is honest.
From there it refuses to blame others for separation and asks mercy to do what self-effort cannot.
The closing movement rests in saintly dust, the Guru's feet, and the hope of real union with the Beloved.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens with day-and-night service, remembrance, and sweet speech offered from sanctuary. It travels through the sorrow of separation, the need for mercy, and ends with the yearning to be united with the Lord through the Guru's feet.
evidence.turn: From there it refuses to blame others for separation and asks mercy to do what self-effort cannot.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whose longing has become dramatic, weary, or spiritually dry. Taken steadily, it keeps longing honest by turning it into service, prayer, and saintly humility. Stay in service and remembrance until separation begins healing.

title: Stop roaming where the One is already near
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: The pauree begins by challenging the wandering search directly and turning the seeker inward. It then sends the heart into Saadh Sangat, where ego is torn down and peace becomes possible.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person exhausted by spiritual roaming, method-switching, or lonely searching. Kept near, it makes company and inward turning feel more trustworthy than the next forest.
takeaway: Search inwardly and let Sangat tear down the proud mound.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਉੜੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: pauRee ||
lines.translation: Pauree:

lines.gurmukhi: ਢਢਾ ਢੂਢਤ ਕਹ ਫਿਰਹੁ ਢੂਢਨੁ ਇਆ ਮਨ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddaddaa ddooddat keh firahu ddooddan iaa man maeh ||
lines.translation: DHADHA: Where are you going, wandering and searching? Search instead within your own mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਗਿ ਤੁਹਾਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਬਸੈ ਬਨੁ ਬਨੁ ਕਹਾ ਫਿਰਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)g tuhaarai prabh basai ban ban kahaa firaeh ||
lines.translation: God is with you, so why do you wander around from forest to forest?

lines.gurmukhi: ਢੇਰੀ ਢਾਹਹੁ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਅਹੰਬੁਧਿ ਬਿਕਰਾਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: dderee ddaahahu saadhasa(n)g aha(n)budh bikaraal ||
lines.translation: In the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, tear down the mound of your frightful, egotistical pride.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਹੁ ਸਹਜੇ ਬਸਹੁ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਿ ਨਿਹਾਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: sukh paavahu sahaje basahu dharasan dhekh nihaal ||
lines.translation: You shall find peace, and abide in intuitive bliss; gazing upon the Blessed Vision of God's Darshan, you shall be delighted.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢੇਰੀ ਜਾਮੈ ਜਮਿ ਮਰੈ ਗਰਭ ਜੋਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਪਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: dderee jaamai jam marai garabh jon dhukh pai ||
lines.translation: One who has such a mound as this, dies and suffers the pain of reincarnation through the womb.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੋਹ ਮਗਨ ਲਪਟਤ ਰਹੈ ਹਉ ਹਉ ਆਵੈ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: moh magan lapaTat rahai hau hau aavai jai ||
lines.translation: One who is intoxicated by emotional attachment, entangled in egotism, selfishness and conceit, shall continue coming and going in reincarnation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਢਹਤ ਢਹਤ ਅਬ ਢਹਿ ਪਰੇ ਸਾਧ ਜਨਾ ਸਰਨਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ddahat ddahat ab ddeh pare saadh janaa saranai ||
lines.translation: Slowly and steadily, I have now surrendered to the Holy Saints; I have come to their Sanctuary.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖ ਕੇ ਫਾਹੇ ਕਾਟਿਆ ਨਾਨਕ ਲੀਏ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੩੦॥
lines.transliteration: dhukh ke faahe kaaTiaa naanak le'ee samai ||30||
lines.translation: God has cut away the noose of my pain; O Nanak, He has merged me into Himself. ||30||

structure: The shabad begins by confronting wandering instead of admiring it.
From there it turns the seeker toward inner search and the company of the holy.
The closing movement rests by linking peace and delight to the breaking of egotistical pride.

evidence.coreClaim: The pauree begins by challenging the wandering search directly and turning the seeker inward. It then sends the heart into Saadh Sangat, where ego is torn down and peace becomes possible.
evidence.turn: From there it turns the seeker toward inner search and the company of the holy.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person exhausted by spiritual roaming, method-switching, or lonely searching. Kept near, it makes company and inward turning feel more trustworthy than the next forest. Search inwardly and let Sangat tear down the proud mound.

title: Pain tells the truth comfort hides
subtitle: Raag Aasaa
summary: The shabad begins by reversing ordinary judgment — suffering can be medicine, while pleasure can become disease when it dulls desire for God. It then yields agency back to the Creator and widens into praise of the One whose light fills everything.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that clings to comfort, resenting pain, or numbing every discomfort on contact. Held wisely, it changes pain from meaningless interruption into an unwanted but revealing teacher.
takeaway: Let pain reveal what comfort keeps covering.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਲੋਕੁ ਮਃ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: salok mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Shalok, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖੁ ਦਾਰੂ ਸੁਖੁ ਰੋਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਜਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਤਾਮਿ ਨ ਹੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhukh dhaaroo sukh rog bhiaa jaa sukh taam na hoiee ||
lines.translation: Suffering is the medicine, and pleasure the disease, because where there is pleasure, there is no desire for God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਕਰਤਾ ਕਰਣਾ ਮੈ ਨਾਹੀ ਜਾ ਹਉ ਕਰੀ ਨ ਹੋਈ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) karataa karanaa mai naahee jaa hau karee na hoiee ||1||
lines.translation: You are the Creator Lord; I can do nothing. Even if I try, nothing happens. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਲਿਹਾਰੀ ਕੁਦਰਤਿ ਵਸਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: balihaaree kudharat vasiaa ||
lines.translation: I am a sacrifice to Your almighty creative power which is pervading everywhere.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੇਰਾ ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਜਾਈ ਲਖਿਆ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: teraa a(n)t na jaiee lakhiaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Your limits cannot be known. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾਤਿ ਮਹਿ ਜੋਤਿ ਜੋਤਿ ਮਹਿ ਜਾਤਾ ਅਕਲ ਕਲਾ ਭਰਪੂਰਿ ਰਹਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaat meh jot jot meh jaataa akal kalaa bharapoor rahiaa ||
lines.translation: Your Light is in Your creatures, and Your creatures are in Your Light; Your almighty power is pervading everywhere.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਸਿਫਤਿ ਸੁਆਲਿੑਉ ਜਿਨਿ ਕੀਤੀ ਸੋ ਪਾਰਿ ਪਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) sachaa saahib sifat suaali(h)au jin keetee so paar piaa ||
lines.translation: You are the True Lord and Master; Your Praise is so beautiful. One who sings it, is carried across.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਕਰਤੇ ਕੀਆ ਬਾਤਾ ਜੋ ਕਿਛੁ ਕਰਣਾ ਸੁ ਕਰਿ ਰਹਿਆ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak karate keeaa baataa jo kichh karanaa su kar rahiaa ||2||
lines.translation: Nanak speaks the stories of the Creator Lord; whatever He is to do, He does. ||2||

structure: The shabad starts with the startling reversal of suffering as medicine and pleasure as disease.
From there it gives up control and admits the Creator's will is doing what your effort cannot.
The closing movement rests in praise, light, and trust in the One whose work runs through everything.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by reversing ordinary judgment — suffering can be medicine, while pleasure can become disease when it dulls desire for God. It then yields agency back to the Creator and widens into praise of the One whose light fills everything.
evidence.turn: From there it gives up control and admits the Creator's will is doing what your effort cannot.
evidence.practicalImplication: This shabad speaks to the part of us that clings to comfort, resenting pain, or numbing every discomfort on contact. Held wisely, it changes pain from meaningless interruption into an unwanted but revealing teacher. Let pain reveal what comfort keeps covering.

title: Peace shows up in speech and gait
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 31
summary: The shabad opens by exposing ritual performed from self-will as the misery of an unwanted bride. It directs the heart toward saintly company and one-pointed Naam, then shows the fruit plainly: sweet speech, humble walking, and peace within.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose devotional language still outruns their conduct. Kept close, it lets peace become visible in tone, pace, and the body's way of moving through the world.
takeaway: When remembrance is real, it reaches the mouth and the walk.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰੀਰਾਗੁ ਮਹਲਾ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: sireeraag mahalaa teejaa ||
lines.translation: Siree Raag, Third Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਮੁਖ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਵਣੇ ਜਿਉ ਦੋਹਾਗਣਿ ਤਨਿ ਸੀਗਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: manmukh karam kamaavane jiau dhohaagan tan seegaar ||
lines.translation: The self-willed manmukh performs religious rituals, like the unwanted bride decorating her body.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੇਜੈ ਕੰਤੁ ਨ ਆਵਈ ਨਿਤ ਨਿਤ ਹੋਇ ਖੁਆਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sejai ka(n)t na aaviee nit nit hoi khuaar ||
lines.translation: Her Husband Lord does not come to her bed; day after day, she grows more and more miserable.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਿਰ ਕਾ ਮਹਲੁ ਨ ਪਾਵਈ ਨਾ ਦੀਸੈ ਘਰੁ ਬਾਰੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: pir kaa mahal na paaviee naa dheesai ghar baar ||1||
lines.translation: She does not attain the Mansion of His Presence; she does not find the door to His House. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਾਈ ਰੇ ਇਕ ਮਨਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhaiee re ik man naam dhiaai ||
lines.translation: O Siblings of Destiny, meditate on the Naam with one-pointed mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤਾ ਸੰਗਤਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਰਹੈ ਜਪਿ ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)taa sa(n)gat mil rahai jap raam naam sukh pai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Remain united with the Society of the Saints; chant the Name of the Lord, and find peace. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਸਦਾ ਸੋਹਾਗਣੀ ਪਿਰੁ ਰਾਖਿਆ ਉਰ ਧਾਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh sadhaa sohaaganee pir raakhiaa ur dhaar ||
lines.translation: The Gurmukh is the happy and pure soul-bride forever. She keeps her Husband Lord enshrined within her heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਠਾ ਬੋਲਹਿ ਨਿਵਿ ਚਲਹਿ ਸੇਜੈ ਰਵੈ ਭਤਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: miThaa boleh niv chaleh sejai ravai bhataar ||
lines.translation: Her speech is sweet, and her way of life is humble. She enjoys the Bed of her Husband Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋਭਾਵੰਤੀ ਸੋਹਾਗਣੀ ਜਿਨ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਹੇਤੁ ਅਪਾਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: sobhaava(n)tee sohaaganee jin gur kaa het apaar ||2||
lines.translation: The happy and pure soul-bride is noble; she has infinite love for the Guru. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੈ ਭਾਗਿ ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਜਾ ਭਾਗੈ ਕਾ ਉਦਉ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: poorai bhaag satagur milai jaa bhaagai kaa udhau hoi ||
lines.translation: By perfect good fortune, one meets the True Guru, when one's destiny is awakened.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਹੁ ਦੁਖੁ ਭ੍ਰਮੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tarahu dhukh bhram kaTeeaai sukh paraapat hoi ||
lines.translation: Suffering and doubt are cut out from within, and peace is obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਭਾਣੈ ਜੋ ਚਲੈ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਪਾਵੈ ਕੋਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bhaanai jo chalai dhukh na paavai koi ||3||
lines.translation: One who walks in harmony with the Guru's Will shall not suffer in pain. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਭਾਣੇ ਵਿਚਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹੈ ਸਹਜੇ ਪਾਵੈ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur ke bhaane vich a(n)mrit hai sahaje paavai koi ||
lines.translation: The Amrit, the Ambrosial Nectar, is in the Guru's Will. With intuitive ease, it is obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਾ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਤਿਨ ਪੀਆ ਹਉਮੈ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਖੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jinaa paraapat tin peeaa haumai vichahu khoi ||
lines.translation: Those who are destined to have it, drink it in; their egotism is eradicated from within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਸਚਿ ਮਿਲਾਵਾ ਹੋਇ ॥੪॥੧੩॥੪੬॥
lines.transliteration: naanak gurmukh naam dhiaaieeaai sach milaavaa hoi ||4||13||46||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the Gurmukh meditates on the Naam, and is united with the True Lord. ||4||13||46||

structure: The shabad begins by exposing performative religiosity as intimate misery rather than holiness.
From there it roots peace in saintly company, one-pointed Naam, and love for the Guru.
The closing movement rests with the Guru's Will as ambrosia and egotism dying where peace becomes embodied.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens by exposing ritual performed from self-will as the misery of an unwanted bride. It directs the heart toward saintly company and one-pointed Naam, then shows the fruit plainly: sweet speech, humble walking, and peace within.
evidence.turn: From there it roots peace in saintly company, one-pointed Naam, and love for the Guru.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person whose devotional language still outruns their conduct. Kept close, it lets peace become visible in tone, pace, and the body's way of moving through the world. When remembrance is real, it reaches the mouth and the walk.

title: The brave war is the one against inner ego
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: The shabad opens by redefining courage — the real warrior subdues the vicious ego within. It then contrasts that inward bravery with the ugliness of egotistical living and comes to rest in Naam as the difference between pain and a redeemed life.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who still calls aggression strength or mistakes self-protection for courage. Keep this shabad after conflict or self-inflation, and it will move the battle back to the actual enemy.
takeaway: Remember this: measure courage by how deeply ego is subdued.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਲੋਕ ਮਃ ੩ ॥
lines.transliteration: salok mahalaa teejaa ||
lines.translation: Shalok, Third Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਸੋ ਸੂਰਾ ਵਰੀਆਮੁ ਜਿਨਿ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਦੁਸਟੁ ਅਹੰਕਰਣੁ ਮਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak so sooraa vareeaam jin vichahu dhusaT aha(n)karan maariaa ||
lines.translation: O Nanak, he is a brave warrior, who conquers and subdues his vicious inner ego.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਲਾਹਿ ਜਨਮੁ ਸਵਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh naam saalaeh janam savaariaa ||
lines.translation: Praising the Naam, the Name of the Lord, the Gurmukhs redeem their lives.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਿ ਹੋਆ ਸਦਾ ਮੁਕਤੁ ਸਭੁ ਕੁਲੁ ਨਿਸਤਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: aap hoaa sadhaa mukat sabh kul nisataariaa ||
lines.translation: They themselves are liberated forever, and they save all their ancestors.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋਹਨਿ ਸਚਿ ਦੁਆਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: sohan sach dhuaar naam piaariaa ||
lines.translation: Those who love the Naam look beauteous at the Gate of Truth.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਮੁਖ ਮਰਹਿ ਅਹੰਕਾਰਿ ਮਰਣੁ ਵਿਗਾੜਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: manmukh mareh aha(n)kaar maran vigaaRiaa ||
lines.translation: The self-willed manmukhs die in egotism-even their death is painfully ugly.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭੋ ਵਰਤੈ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਵਿਚਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabho varatai hukam kiaa kareh vichaariaa ||
lines.translation: Everything happens according to the Lord's Will; what can the poor people do?

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਹੁ ਦੂਜੈ ਲਗਿ ਖਸਮੁ ਵਿਸਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: aapahu dhoojai lag khasam visaariaa ||
lines.translation: Attached to self-conceit and duality, they have forgotten their Lord and Master.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬਿਨੁ ਨਾਵੈ ਸਭੁ ਦੁਖੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਵਿਸਾਰਿਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak bin naavai sabh dhukh sukh visaariaa ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, without the Name, everything is painful, and happiness is forgotten. ||1||

structure: The shabad begins by calling the conqueror of inner ego the true warrior.
From there it contrasts Gurmukh praise and liberation with the painful disfigurement of egotistical living.
The closing movement rests by saying life without Naam forgets happiness itself.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens by redefining courage — the real warrior subdues the vicious ego within. It then contrasts that inward bravery with the ugliness of egotistical living and comes to rest in Naam as the difference between pain and a redeemed life.
evidence.turn: From there it contrasts Gurmukh praise and liberation with the painful disfigurement of egotistical living.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person who still calls aggression strength or mistakes self-protection for courage. Keep this shabad after conflict or self-inflation, and it will move the battle back to the actual enemy. Remember this: measure courage by how deeply ego is subdued.

title: The day is shrinking; spend it well
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 205
summary: The shabad opens with time diminishing day and night and immediately urges the mind toward the Guru. It turns the shrinking day into an argument for serving saints, earning Naam, and buying what you came here to buy.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person living as if later were still guaranteed. Held clearly, it forces time, purpose, and profit back into the same conversation.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: choose the remaining day for the profit of Naam.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਉਧ ਘਟੈ ਦਿਨਸੁ ਰੈਨਾਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: aaudh ghaTai dhinas rainaare ||
lines.translation: This life is diminishing, day and night.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨ ਗੁਰ ਮਿਲਿ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰੇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: man gur mil kaaj savaare ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Meeting with the Guru, your affairs shall be resolved. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਉ ਬੇਨੰਤੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ਸੰਤ ਟਹਲ ਕੀ ਬੇਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: karau bena(n)tee sunahu mere meetaa sa(n)t Tahal kee belaa ||
lines.translation: Listen, my friends, I beg of you: now is the time to serve the Saints!

lines.gurmukhi: ਈਹਾ ਖਾਟਿ ਚਲਹੁ ਹਰਿ ਲਾਹਾ ਆਗੈ ਬਸਨੁ ਸੁਹੇਲਾ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: e'eehaa khaaT chalahu har laahaa aagai basan suhelaa ||1||
lines.translation: In this world, earn the profit of the Lord's Name, and hereafter, you shall dwell in peace. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਹੁ ਸੰਸਾਰੁ ਬਿਕਾਰੁ ਸਹਸੇ ਮਹਿ ਤਰਿਓ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: eih sa(n)saar bikaar sahase meh tario braham giaanee ||
lines.translation: This world is engrossed in corruption and cynicism. Only those who know God are saved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸਹਿ ਜਗਾਇ ਪੀਆਏ ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਅਕਥ ਕਥਾ ਤਿਨਿ ਜਾਨੀ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: jiseh jagai peeaae har ras akath kathaa tin jaanee ||2||
lines.translation: Those who are awakened by the Lord to drink in this sublime essence, come to know the Unspoken Speech of the Lord. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕਉ ਆਏ ਸੋਈ ਵਿਹਾਝਹੁ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਤੇ ਮਨਹਿ ਬਸੇਰਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kau aae soiee vihaajhahu har gur te maneh baseraa ||
lines.translation: Purchase only that for which you have come into the world, and through the Guru, the Lord shall dwell within your mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਮਹਲੁ ਪਾਵਹੁ ਸੁਖ ਸਹਜੇ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਨ ਹੋਇਗੋ ਫੇਰਾ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: nij ghar mahal paavahu sukh sahaje bahur na hoigo feraa ||3||
lines.translation: Within the home of your own inner being, you shall obtain the Mansion of the Lord's Presence with intuitive ease. You shall not be consigned again to the wheel of reincarnation. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਜਾਮੀ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ਸਰਧਾ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਪੂਰੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tarajaamee purakh bidhaate saradhaa man kee poore ||
lines.translation: O Inner-knower, Searcher of hearts, Primal Being, Architect of Destiny: please fulfill this yearning of my mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕੁ ਦਾਸੁ ਇਹੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਮਾਗੈ ਮੋ ਕਉ ਕਰਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਧੂਰੇ ॥੪॥੩॥੧੨੪॥
lines.transliteration: naanak dhaas ihee sukh maagai mo kau kar sa(n)tan kee dhoore ||4||3||124||
lines.translation: Nanak, Your slave, begs for this happiness: let me be the dust of the feet of the Saints. ||4||3||124||

structure: The shabad begins by refusing the illusion that life is standing still.
From there it urges service to saints and the earning of the Lord's profit while there is still time.
The closing movement rests in the prayer to become saintly dust and dwell where reincarnation no longer returns.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens with time diminishing day and night and immediately urges the mind toward the Guru. It turns the shrinking day into an argument for serving saints, earning Naam, and buying what you came here to buy.
evidence.turn: From there it urges service to saints and the earning of the Lord's profit while there is still time.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person living as if later were still guaranteed. Held clearly, it forces time, purpose, and profit back into the same conversation. Keep this in front of you: choose the remaining day for the profit of Naam.

title: The deeper union is not found by roaming
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 154
summary: The shabad begins by naming the ordinary states the mind circles within. It then declares that the fourth state, union with the Lord, is known only through the True Guru and crossed into by devotion and service.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person exhausted by movement, method, and spiritual curiosity that never lands. Stayed with honestly, it lets the search stop circling what is visible and return to the Guru's path.
takeaway: Roaming ends when the Guru reveals the deeper union.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa pehilaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, First Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨਮਿ ਮਰੈ ਤ੍ਰੈ ਗੁਣ ਹਿਤਕਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: janam marai trai gun hitakaar ||
lines.translation: One who loves the three qualities is subject to birth and death.

lines.gurmukhi: ਚਾਰੇ ਬੇਦ ਕਥਹਿ ਆਕਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: chaare bedh katheh aakaar ||
lines.translation: The four Vedas speak only of the visible forms.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੀਨਿ ਅਵਸਥਾ ਕਹਹਿ ਵਖਿਆਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: teen avasathaa kaheh vakhiaan ||
lines.translation: They describe and explain the three states of mind,

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੁਰੀਆਵਸਥਾ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਤੇ ਹਰਿ ਜਾਨੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: tureeaavasathaa satigur te har jaan ||1||
lines.translation: but the fourth state, union with the Lord, is known only through the True Guru. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮ ਭਗਤਿ ਗੁਰ ਸੇਵਾ ਤਰਣਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: raam bhagat gur sevaa taranaa ||
lines.translation: Through devotional worship of the Lord, and service to the Guru, one swims across.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਾਹੁੜਿ ਜਨਮੁ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਹੈ ਮਰਣਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: baahuR janam na hoi hai maranaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Then, one is not born again, and is not subject to death. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਚਾਰਿ ਪਦਾਰਥ ਕਹੈ ਸਭੁ ਕੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: chaar padhaarath kahai sabh koiee ||
lines.translation: Everyone speaks of the four great blessings;

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਸਾਸਤ ਪੰਡਿਤ ਮੁਖਿ ਸੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: si(n)mirat saasat pa(n)ddit mukh soiee ||
lines.translation: the Simritees, the Shaastras and the Pandits speak of them as well.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਅਰਥੁ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ ਨ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: bin gur arath beechaar na paiaa ||
lines.translation: But without the Guru, they do not understand their true significance.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮੁਕਤਿ ਪਦਾਰਥੁ ਭਗਤਿ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: mukat padhaarath bhagat har paiaa ||2||
lines.translation: The treasure of liberation is obtained through devotional worship of the Lord. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾ ਕੈ ਹਿਰਦੈ ਵਸਿਆ ਹਰਿ ਸੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaa kai hiradhai vasiaa har soiee ||
lines.translation: Those, within whose hearts the Lord dwells,

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਹੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh bhagat paraapat hoiee ||
lines.translation: become Gurmukh; they receive the blessings of devotional worship.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਭਗਤਿ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਆਨੰਦੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kee bhagat mukat aana(n)dh ||
lines.translation: Through devotional worship of the Lord, liberation and bliss are obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਪਾਏ ਪਰਮਾਨੰਦੁ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: gurmat paae paramaana(n)dh ||3||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Teachings, supreme ecstasy is obtained. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਦੇਖਿ ਦਿਖਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: jin paiaa gur dhekh dhikhaiaa ||
lines.translation: One who meets the Guru, beholds Him, and inspires others to behold Him as well.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਸਾ ਮਾਹਿ ਨਿਰਾਸੁ ਬੁਝਾਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: aasaa maeh niraas bujhaiaa ||
lines.translation: In the midst of hope, the Guru teaches us to live above hope and desire.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੀਨਾ ਨਾਥੁ ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖਦਾਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: dheenaa naath sarab sukhadhaataa ||
lines.translation: He is the Master of the meek, the Giver of peace to all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣੀ ਮਨੁ ਰਾਤਾ ॥੪॥੧੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak har charanee man raataa ||4||12||
lines.translation: Nanak's mind is imbued with the Lotus Feet of the Lord. ||4||12||

structure: The shabad begins by showing how much of life stays trapped inside ordinary mental states.
From there it points to a deeper union that cannot be reached by visible forms alone.
The closing movement rests with devotion and service as the actual crossing where wandering gives way.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by naming the ordinary states the mind circles within. It then declares that the fourth state, union with the Lord, is known only through the True Guru and crossed into by devotion and service.
evidence.turn: From there it points to a deeper union that cannot be reached by visible forms alone.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person exhausted by movement, method, and spiritual curiosity that never lands. Stayed with honestly, it lets the search stop circling what is visible and return to the Guru's path. Roaming ends when the Guru reveals the deeper union.

title: The forgiving Lord shelters the lowly
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: The shabad begins by praising the Lord as forgiving, merciful, and tender toward the poor and unprotected. It keeps widening that refuge until the speaker can admit smallness without despair and enter sanctuary instead of comparison.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who feels envious, unsettled, or quietly beneath everyone else. Stayed with, it replaces comparison with refuge and makes humility safe because the Lord's mercy moves toward the lowly.
takeaway: Bring your smallness into the Lord's shelter instead of hiding it.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਬਖਸੰਦ ਦੀਨ ਦਇਆਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: prabh bakhasa(n)dh dheen dhiaal ||
lines.translation: God, the Forgiving Lord, is kind to the poor.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਗਤਿ ਵਛਲ ਸਦਾ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhagat vachhal sadhaa kirapaal ||
lines.translation: He loves His devotees, and He is always merciful to them.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਨਾਥ ਨਾਥ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਗੁਪਾਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: anaath naath gobi(n)dh gupaal ||
lines.translation: The Patron of the patronless, the Lord of the Universe, the Sustainer of the world,

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਰਬ ਘਟਾ ਕਰਤ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਲ ॥
lines.transliteration: sarab ghaTaa karat pratipaal ||
lines.translation: the Nourisher of all beings.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਦਿ ਪੁਰਖ ਕਾਰਣ ਕਰਤਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: aadh purakh kaaran karataar ||
lines.translation: The Primal Being, the Creator of the Creation.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਅਧਾਰ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhagat janaa ke praan adhaar ||
lines.translation: The Support of the breath of life of His devotees.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜੋ ਜੋ ਜਪੈ ਸੁ ਹੋਇ ਪੁਨੀਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: jo jo japai su hoi puneet ||
lines.translation: Whoever meditates on Him is sanctified,

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਗਤਿ ਭਾਇ ਲਾਵੈ ਮਨ ਹੀਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhagat bhai laavai man heet ||
lines.translation: focusing the mind in loving devotional worship.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮ ਨਿਰਗੁਨੀਆਰ ਨੀਚ ਅਜਾਨ ॥
lines.transliteration: ham niraguneeaar neech ajaan ||
lines.translation: I am unworthy, lowly and ignorant.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਤੁਮਰੀ ਸਰਨਿ ਪੁਰਖ ਭਗਵਾਨ ॥੭॥
lines.transliteration: naanak tumaree saran purakh bhagavaan ||7||
lines.translation: Nanak has entered Your Sanctuary, O Supreme Lord God. ||7||

structure: The shabad names the Lord as forgiving, compassionate, and protective of the poor.
From there it praises the One who sustains all beings and supports the breath of devotees.
It finally lets the speaker confess lowliness and step fully into the Lord's sanctuary.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad begins by praising the Lord as forgiving, merciful, and tender toward the poor and unprotected. It keeps widening that refuge until the speaker can admit smallness without despair and enter sanctuary instead of comparison.
evidence.turn: From there it praises the One who sustains all beings and supports the breath of devotees.
evidence.practicalImplication: This one meets the person who feels envious, unsettled, or quietly beneath everyone else. Stayed with, it replaces comparison with refuge and makes humility safe because the Lord's mercy moves toward the lowly. Bring your smallness into the Lord's shelter instead of hiding it.

title: The Guru asks for more than admiration
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 171
summary: The shabad opens with startling surrender — the body itself is sold before the Perfect Guru for the Lord's sake. It develops through lamp-like wisdom, the dispersal of doubt and fear, and the final honor of having placed one's head before the True Guru.
whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who wants spiritual help without yielding the center seat. Keep this shabad near moments of image-protection or self-assertion, and it presses devotion past sentiment into surrender.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: let surrender reach the body before the ego performs again.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਪੂਰਬੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੪ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee poorabee mahalaa chauthhaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree Poorbee, Fourth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਅਰਥਿ ਸਰੀਰੁ ਹਮ ਬੇਚਿਆ ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਆਗੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: har har arath sareer ham bechiaa poore gur kai aage ||
lines.translation: For the sake of the Lord, Har, Har, I have sold my body to the Perfect Guru.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਦਾਤੈ ਨਾਮੁ ਦਿੜਾਇਆ ਮੁਖਿ ਮਸਤਕਿ ਭਾਗ ਸਭਾਗੇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: satigur dhaatai naam dhiRaiaa mukh masatak bhaag sabhaage ||1||
lines.translation: The True Guru, the Giver, has implanted the Naam, the Name of the Lord, within me. A very blessed and fortunate destiny is recorded upon my forehead. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮ ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਹਰਿ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਗੇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: raam gurmat har liv laage ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Teachings, I am lovingly centered on the Lord. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਘਟਿ ਘਟਿ ਰਮਈਆ ਰਮਤ ਰਾਮ ਰਾਇ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਗੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: ghaT ghaT ramieeaa ramat raam rai gur sabadh guroo liv laage ||
lines.translation: The All-pervading Sovereign Lord King is contained in each and every heart. Through the Guru, and the Word of the Guru's Shabad, I am lovingly centered on the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਦੇਵਉ ਕਾਟਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਭ੍ਰਮੁ ਭਉ ਗੁਰ ਬਚਨੀ ਭਾਗੇ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: hau man tan dhevau kaaT guroo kau meraa bhram bhau gur bachanee bhaage ||2||
lines.translation: Cutting my mind and body into pieces, I offer them to my Guru. The Guru's Teachings have dispelled my doubt and fear. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਧਿਆਰੈ ਦੀਪਕ ਆਨਿ ਜਲਾਏ ਗੁਰ ਗਿਆਨਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਗੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)dhiaarai dheepak aan jalaae gur giaan guroo liv laage ||
lines.translation: In the darkness, the Guru has lit the lamp of the Guru's wisdom; I am lovingly focused on the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅਗਿਆਨੁ ਅੰਧੇਰਾ ਬਿਨਸਿ ਬਿਨਾਸਿਓ ਘਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ ਲਹੀ ਮਨ ਜਾਗੇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: agiaan a(n)dheraa binas binaasio ghar vasat lahee man jaage ||3||
lines.translation: The darkness of ignorance has been dispelled, and my mind has been awakened; within the home of my inner being, I have found the genuine article. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਾਕਤ ਬਧਿਕ ਮਾਇਆਧਾਰੀ ਤਿਨ ਜਮ ਜੋਹਨਿ ਲਾਗੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: saakat badhik maiaadhaaree tin jam johan laage ||
lines.translation: The vicious hunters, the faithless cynics, are hunted down by the Messenger of Death.

lines.gurmukhi: ਉਨ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਆਗੈ ਸੀਸੁ ਨ ਬੇਚਿਆ ਓਇ ਆਵਹਿ ਜਾਹਿ ਅਭਾਗੇ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: aun satigur aagai sees na bechiaa oi aaveh jaeh abhaage ||4||
lines.translation: They have not sold their heads to the True Guru; those wretched, unfortunate ones continue coming and going in reincarnation. ||4||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਮਰਾ ਬਿਨਉ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਹਮ ਸਰਣਿ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਹਰਿ ਮਾਗੇ ॥
lines.transliteration: hamaraa binau sunahu prabh Thaakur ham saran prabhoo har maage ||
lines.translation: Hear my prayer, O God, my Lord and Master: I beg for the Sanctuary of the Lord God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਕੀ ਲਜ ਪਾਤਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਹੈ ਸਿਰੁ ਬੇਚਿਓ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਆਗੇ ॥੫॥੧੦॥੨੪॥੬੨॥
lines.transliteration: jan naanak kee laj paat guroo hai sir bechio satigur aage ||5||10||24||62||
lines.translation: Servant Nanak's honor and respect is the Guru; he has sold his head to the True Guru. ||5||10||24||62||

structure: The shabad starts with total offering before the Guru rather than devotional display.
From there it shows the Guru lighting wisdom, dispelling fear, and waking the mind to what is genuine.
The closing movement rests by contrasting those who never yield with the honor of giving one's head before the True Guru.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad opens with startling surrender — the body itself is sold before the Perfect Guru for the Lord's sake. It develops through lamp-like wisdom, the dispersal of doubt and fear, and the final honor of having placed one's head before the True Guru.
evidence.turn: From there it shows the Guru lighting wisdom, dispelling fear, and waking the mind to what is genuine.
evidence.practicalImplication: This speaks to the person who wants spiritual help without yielding the center seat. Keep this shabad near moments of image-protection or self-assertion, and it presses devotion past sentiment into surrender. Keep this in front of you: let surrender reach the body before the ego performs again.

title: The Guru's word raises the soul into real stature
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 239
summary: The shabad keeps returning to what the Guru's word does from the inside — it lifts the seeker beyond self-made rank, steadies the mind, and joins the heart to the Supreme Lord. What looks like attainment from the outside is recast as what the Guru actually causes within.
whyItMatters: This shabad speaks to the part of us that chases improvement, image, or spiritual status without steady submission to the Guru's word. Taken seriously, it turns attainment from display into inward settlement.
takeaway: Remember this: let the Guru's word define attainment.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੫ ॥
lines.transliteration: gauRee mahalaa panjavaa ||
lines.translation: Gauree, Fifth Mehla:

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਮੋਹਿ ਪਰਮ ਗਤਿ ਪਾਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan moh param gat paiee ||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Word, I have attained the supreme status.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਮੇਰੀ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਾਈ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: gur poorai meree paij rakhaiee ||1||
lines.translation: The Perfect Guru has preserved my honor. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਧਿਆਇਓ ਮੋਹਿ ਨਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan dhiaaio moh naau ||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Word, I meditate on the Name.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਪਰਸਾਦਿ ਮੋਹਿ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਥਾਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur parasaadh moh miliaa thaau ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: By Guru's Grace, I have obtained a place of rest. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਸੁਣਿ ਰਸਨ ਵਖਾਣੀ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan sun rasan vakhaanee ||
lines.translation: I listen to the Guru's Word, and chant it with my tongue.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਤੇ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਮੇਰੀ ਬਾਣੀ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: gur kirapaa te a(n)mirat meree baanee ||2||
lines.translation: By Guru's Grace, my speech is like nectar. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਮਿਟਿਆ ਮੇਰਾ ਆਪੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan miTiaa meraa aap ||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Word, my selfishness and conceit have been removed.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਦਇਆ ਤੇ ਮੇਰਾ ਵਡ ਪਰਤਾਪੁ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: gur kee dhiaa te meraa vadd parataap ||3||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's kindness, I have obtained glorious greatness. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਮਿਟਿਆ ਮੇਰਾ ਭਰਮੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan miTiaa meraa bharam ||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Word, my doubts have been removed.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਪੇਖਿਓ ਸਭੁ ਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan pekhio sabh braham ||4||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Word, I see God everywhere. ||4||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਬਚਨਿ ਕੀਨੋ ਰਾਜੁ ਜੋਗੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bachan keeno raaj jog ||
lines.translation: Through the Guru's Word, I practice Raja Yoga, the Yoga of meditation and success.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰਿਆ ਸਭੁ ਲੋਗੁ ॥੫॥
